candidates.title: Surface Coating of Plastic Parts and Products

criteria.criterion: if the activity is the application of a coating to a plastic substrate (i.e., coating application) or an associated activity that is directly related to the application of a coating, then subject
if the material applied is an adhesive (a chemical substance applied for the purpose of bonding two surfaces together), then subject
if the activity is only the use of a cleaning material (surface preparation) that is not directly related to the application of a coating, then not subject

if the facility uses 378 liters (100 gallons) per year or more of coatings that contain HAP in the surface coating of plastic parts and products and the source is a major source (or located at a major source), then subject

if the surface coating or coating operation meets any of the exclusion criteria in paragraphs (c)(1) through (c)(17) of § 63.4481 (for example, uses only materials that contain no organic HAP), then not subject

if the activity is part of the affected source as defined (all coating operations; all storage containers and mixing vessels for coatings/thinners/additives/cleaning materials; conveying equipment for those materials; and storage/conveying equipment for waste from coating operations), then subject

if you choose the compliant material option and each coating's organic HAP content and each thinner/additive/cleaning material meet the mass-fraction/analysis procedures and limits in § 63.4541, then the coating operation is not required to meet the operating limits or work practice standards in §§ 63.4492 and 63.4493

checklist: Is the methylene-chloride application intended to bond (solvent weld) parts (i.e., purpose = bonding) or solely to clean/prepare the surface?
Does the applied material leave a solid film or dry coating on the substrate after evaporation, or is nothing with solids left behind?
Does the methylene-chloride application meet your facility's/your interpretation of the definition of an 'adhesive' (chemical applied to bond surfaces) or of a 'coating' per § 63.4581?
Is the methylene-chloride step directly related to the application of a separate coating (i.e., an associated activity) or independent (purely welding/assembly)?

How many liters (or gallons) per year of materials that qualify as 'coatings' containing HAP (not counting non-HAP coatings per § 63.4581) will be used at the affected source (current + after adding six lines)?
Is the facility a major source of HAP (potential to emit ≥ 9.07 Mg (10 tons) of any single HAP or ≥ 22.68 Mg (25 tons) total HAP per year)?
Do any of the exclusions in § 63.4481(c)(1)–(17) apply to this operation (e.g., uses only materials with no organic HAP; research/lab facility; extruding plastic onto parts; other listed exemptions)?
Is the solvent-welding operation located within the collection of components defined as the affected source (include storage, mixing, conveyance, and waste handling associated with the operation)?

For materials used: obtain manufacturer formulation data or test results (Method 311, Method 24 or approved alternatives) to determine mass fraction of organic HAP and mass fraction of coating solids per § 63.4541(a)–(c).

If relying on the compliant material option, can you document that each coating's organic HAP content is ≤ the applicable emission limit in § 63.4490 and that each thinner/additive/cleaning material contains no organic HAP, using the procedures in § 63.4541?
Recordkeeping: assemble documentation for initial compliance notifications and records per subpart PPPP (identify coating operations and method used to determine organic HAP and solids content).

judge_text: {"score": 1, "reason": "The answer includes the key points that MeCl used to bond is an 'adhesive' (cites §63.4581) and it asks about whether the material leaves coating solids and about measuring solids/HAP per §63.4541. However it does not explicitly capture the EPA's decisive point that when no coating solids remain the §63.4490 emission limit (lb HAP/lb solids) cannot be determined and therefore the rule is not applied to the solvent-welding lines."}

candidates.title: Secondary copper smelters (Subpart FFFFFF)

criteria.criterion: if you own or operate a new secondary copper smelter that is an area source of hazardous air pollutant (HAP) emissions then subject
if you commenced construction or reconstruction of the affected source on or after October 6, 2006 then subject
if your facility melts recycled copper scrap or copper alloy scrap only to produce ingots or for direct use in a manufacturing process then not subject
if your facility is a research and development facility as defined in section 112(c)(7) of the CAA then not subject

checklist: Confirm whether the facility processes copper scrap to produce anode copper (i.e., casts copper into anodes for subsequent electrolytic refining)

Confirm whether the facility uses a pyrometallurgical purification process (smelting furnace/melting furnace operations with fluxing, oxidation/reduction, or similar) versus merely melting scrap to produce ingots or feedstock for direct manufacture
Confirm the facility's potential-to-emit for HAPs to verify area source status (i.e., below major source thresholds)
Confirm the date construction or reconstruction of the affected source commenced (was it on or after October 6, 2006?)
Confirm whether the facility is categorized as a research and development facility under CAA section 112(c)(7)
Confirm whether, if subject to this subpart, you will obtain the required permit under 40 CFR part 70 or 40 CFR part 71

judge_text: {"score":2,"reason":"All key reasons from the EPA notes are present: the answer includes the pyrometallurgical purification vs. 'melting-only' distinction (captures the anode‑making smelter definition under 63.11158) and it cites 63.11153(a)-(b)/new area‑source coverage plus checklist items to confirm area‑source status and construction date (Oct 6, 2006), matching the EPA rationale."}

candidates.title: National Perchloroethylene Dry Cleaning

criteria.criterion: If the facility uses perchloroethylene then the owner or operator is subject to this subpart.
If the dry cleaning machine is coin-operated then the owner or operator is not subject to the requirements of this subpart.
If a dry cleaning system is located in a building with a residence then after December 21, 2020 the owner or operator shall eliminate any emission of perchloroethylene from that dry cleaning system.

If a dry cleaning system was installed or relocated after December 21, 2005 and is located in a building with a residence then the owner or operator shall eliminate any emission of perchloroethylene from that dry cleaning system.

If a dry cleaning system commenced construction or reconstruction on or after December 21, 2005 but before July 13, 2006 and is located in a building with a residence then the owner or operator shall comply with the additional requirements at §63.322(o)(5)(ii)(A)–(C) (vapor barrier enclosure; refrigerated condenser plus carbon adsorber immediately prior to door opening; and weekly inspections) in addition to other applicable requirements.

If the dry cleaning facility emits or has the potential to emit more than 9.1 megagrams per year (10 tons per year) of perchloroethylene, or meets the numeric perchloroethylene consumption criteria in §63.320(g)(1) or (g)(2), then the facility is a major source (if not, then it is an area source).

If the facility's total yearly perchloroethylene consumption determined according to §63.323(d) is less than 530 liters (140 gallons) for facilities with only dry-to-dry machines or less than 760 liters (200 gallons) for facilities with only transfer-machine systems then certain existing systems installed in specified date ranges may be exempt from specified provisions of §§63.322, 63.323, and 63.324 as described in §63.320(d) and (e).

checklist: Does the facility use perchloroethylene (PCE) at any time?
Is any dry cleaning machine coin-operated (customer loads/starts the machine)?
Is there a residence located in the same building as the dry cleaning machine (note: a vacant residence still counts per notification requirement)?
What is the exact date the dry cleaning machine was constructed, reconstructed, installed, or (if applicable) relocated (to determine which compliance dates and paragraphs apply)?
Is the machine a dry-to-dry machine or a transfer machine system?
Was the machine installed or relocated after December 21, 2005, or did construction/reconstruction commence between December 21, 2005 and July 13, 2006?
Calculate total PCE purchased for each of the prior 12 months and sum per §63.323(d) to determine yearly PCE consumption (keep purchase receipts/logs).
Does the yearly PCE consumption exceed 530 L (140 gal), 760 L (200 gal), 6,800 L (1,800 gal), or 8,000 L (2,100 gal) thresholds used in §63.320(d),(e),(g)?
Based on emissions or consumption thresholds, is the facility a major source (>9.1 Mg/yr or per §63.320(g) criteria) or an area source?

If located in a building with a residence, verify whether compliance demonstration under §63.320(b)(2)(ii) (systems commenced Dec 21, 2005–July 13, 2006) might apply (check construction date and building/residence status).
Maintain and be able to produce on site PCE purchase receipts and the monthly/yearly consumption log per §63.324(d) (records retained for 5 years).
If claiming any exemption for older machines per §63.320(d)/(e), document the machine installation dates and the facility PCE consumption calculation used to justify the exemption.

judge_text: {"score": 1, "reason": "The answer captures the key point that a dry cleaning system located in a building with a residence (including a vacant residence) triggers the §63.322(o)(5)(i) requirement, but it does not explicitly state the EPA’s additional key rationale that the requirement applies regardless of whether the machine is currently operating — i.e., it applies so long as the PCE machine remains in the building."}

candidates.title: Metal Fabrication and Finishing Area Sources

criteria.criterion: If you own or operate an area source that is primarily engaged in operations in one of the nine metal fabrication and finishing source categories listed in § 63.11514(a)(1) through (9) then you are subject to this subpart.

If you use materials that contain or have the potential to emit metal fabrication or finishing HAP (MFHAP) as defined in § 63.11522 (cadmium, chromium, lead, manganese, nickel at the concentrations specified) then the provisions of this subpart apply to the affected source types listed in § 63.11514(b)(1) through (5).

If your facility's production of products listed in one of the nine source category descriptions represents at least 50 percent of the production at the facility over the previous continuous 12 months then the facility is 'primarily engaged' in that source category for purposes of applicability.

If all or part of the operations are limited to research or laboratory facilities, tool or equipment repair, facility maintenance, or quality control activities as defined in § 63.11522 then those operations are not subject to this subpart.

If the operations are performed on site at installations owned or operated by the Armed Forces, the National Aeronautics and Space Administration, or the National Nuclear Security Administration, or if the operations produce military munitions as defined in § 63.11522, then this subpart does not apply to those operations.

If you perform machining, dry abrasive blasting, dry grinding and dry polishing with machines, spray painting, or welding operations that use materials containing MFHAP or have the potential to emit MFHAP then those operations qualify as the corresponding affected source types described in § 63.11514(b)(1) through (5).

If a welding affected source uses 2,000 pounds or more per year of welding rod containing one or more MFHAP (calculated on a rolling 12-month basis) then the owner or operator must demonstrate that management practices or fume control measures are being implemented by complying with the requirements in § 63.11516(f)(3) through (8).

If you commenced construction or reconstruction of the affected source before April 3, 2008 then the affected source is an existing source, and if you commenced construction or reconstruction on or after April 3, 2008 then the affected source is a new source.

checklist: Confirm that the facility is an 'area source' of HAP (not a major source).

Determine whether the facility is 'primarily engaged' (≥50% of production over the previous continuous 12 months) in any one of the nine metal fabrication and finishing source categories listed in § 63.11514(a)(1)-(9) (identify which category from Table 1).

Identify which operations are performed at the facility: machining, welding, dry abrasive blasting, dry grinding/dry polishing with machines, spray-applied painting, or other metal fabrication/finishing activities.
For each material, review formulation data/MSDS to determine whether it contains MFHAP: cadmium, chromium, lead, or nickel ≥0.1% by weight (as the metal) or manganese ≥1.0% by weight (as the metal).
For welding: track rolling 12-month usage (pounds) of welding rod that contains any MFHAP to see if it meets or exceeds 2,000 lb/yr.

If spray painting is performed, determine whether paints are spray-applied (hand-held spray, HVLP, electrostatic, airless, etc.) and whether the paints contain MFHAP; document spray booth/room configuration and filter technology if applicable.

If dry abrasive blasting is performed, determine whether blasting is totally enclosed/unvented or vented, whether blast media contain MFHAP, and the size of items blasted (greater than 8 ft in any dimension).
Determine whether any operations at the facility fall under the exclusions: research/laboratory, tool/equipment repair, facility maintenance, or quality control (per definitions in § 63.11522).
Determine whether the facility or operations are on installations owned/operated by the Armed Forces, NASA, or NNSA, or whether operations produce military munitions.
Document the date construction or reconstruction of any affected source commenced to classify sources as new (on/after April 3, 2008) or existing (before April 3, 2008).

Collect and retain supporting records for applicability determinations (equipment lists, processes included in affected source, changes and dates), MSDS/formulation data, production accounting used to establish 'primarily engaged' (showing percent by volume/linear foot/square foot or other metric), and rolling 12-month welding rod usage records.

judge_text: {"score":1, "reason":"The ANSWER includes the core applicability criteria (area source, must be 'primarily engaged' in one of the nine categories and the ≥50% test) but it fails to capture EPA’s key reasoning about SIC/NAICS classification — specifically the EPA Q&A pairing that NAICS 335999 maps to SIC 3699 (not SIC 3679) and thus the facility is outside the rule. The RESPONSE lacks an explicit SIC/NAICS mapping check or reference to that EPA guidance."}

candidates.title: Lime manufacturing plants (Subpart AAAAA)

criteria.criterion: if you own or operate a lime manufacturing plant (LMP) that is a major source, or that is located at, or is part of, a major source of hazardous air pollutant emissions then this subpart applies

if an establishment manufactures lime product by calcination of limestone, dolomite, shells, or other calcareous substances (i.e., it uses a lime kiln to produce lime product) then the establishment is an LMP

if a plant site emits or has the potential to emit any single HAP at a rate of 9.07 megagrams (10 tons) or more per year or any combination of HAP at a rate of 22.68 megagrams (25 tons) or more per year then the plant site is a major source

if the LMP is located at a kraft pulp mill, soda pulp mill, sulfite pulp mill, beet sugar manufacturing plant, or only processes sludge containing calcium carbonate from water softening processes then this subpart does not apply to that LMP

if you have existing or new lime kiln(s) and their associated cooler(s), and processed stone handling (PSH) operations located at an LMP that is a major source then this subpart applies to those lime kilns, associated coolers, and PSH systems

if construction or reconstruction of a lime kiln (and its associated cooler, if applicable) began after December 20, 2002 (and you met the applicability criteria in §63.7081 when construction/reconstruction began) then the kiln is considered new for purposes of the PM emissions limitations, and if construction or reconstruction of a lime kiln began after January 5, 2023 (and you met the applicability criteria in §63.7081 when construction/reconstruction began) then the kiln is considered new for purposes of the HCl, mercury, organic HAP, and D/F emissions limitations
if the equipment is a lime hydrator then it is not subject to this subpart
if the equipment is a nuisance dust collector on a lime cooler then it is part of the lime materials processing operations and is not covered by this subpart
if the material is stored in open material storage piles then those open piles are not subject to this subpart

checklist: Confirm whether the kiln is used to produce a lime product by calcination (identify feedstock: limestone, dolomite, shells, or other calcareous substances; explicitly note whether the feedstock is calcium carbonate lime mud from the caustic recovery loop)
Quantify actual and potential annual HAP emissions for the entire plant site to determine if single HAP ≥ 10 tpy or total HAP ≥ 25 tpy (include potential-to-emit calculations)

Confirm that the LMP is not located at or part of a kraft pulp mill, soda pulp mill, sulfite pulp mill, or beet sugar manufacturing plant, and confirm it does not only process sludge from water softening (calcium carbonate sludge)

Identify whether the kiln and any associated cooler or PSH equipment are present at the plant and list all processed stone handling equipment and transfer points (storage bins, conveyors, bucket elevators, screening, surge bins)

Determine construction/reconstruction dates for the kiln (and associated cooler) to compare with December 20, 2002 and January 5, 2023 and document whether applicability criteria in §63.7081 were met at that time
List all related equipment types (lime cooler, lime hydrator, nuisance dust collectors on coolers, open material storage piles) to determine which components are covered or excluded under the subpart
Document whether the operation produces lime product for internal reuse only or for sale (identify production purpose and end use)

judge_text: {"score":2,"reason":"All key EPA reasons are captured: the answer cites §63.7143/§63.7081 to show calcining calcareous lime mud qualifies as an LMP; it lists the specific exemptions (pulp mills, beet sugar, water‑softening sludge) and the checklist requires confirming the plant is not one of those exempt types (so soda ash recovery is not exempt); and the criteria implicitly cover lime produced for internal reuse (no sale requirement) and the checklist specifically asks to document reuse vs sale."}

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants for Reciprocating Internal Combustion Engines (Subpart ZZZZ)

criteria.criterion: If a stationary RICE meets any of the criteria in the definition of “remote stationary RICE” (offshore beyond the line of ordinary low water; located on a pipeline segment meeting the building-count and distance tests; or not on pipelines and having 5 or fewer buildings intended for human occupancy and no buildings with four or more stories within a 0.25 mile radius) then the engine is a remote stationary RICE.

If an existing non-emergency 4SLB or 4SRB stationary RICE with a site rating of more than 500 HP is located at an area source, is not a remote stationary RICE, and is operated more than 24 hours per calendar year then the initial compliance demonstration must be conducted as specified in §63.6630(e) (including the specified performance test/run and measurement requirements).

If you own or operate an existing stationary RICE located at an area source of HAP emissions then you must submit the notifications that apply to you as specified in §63.6645(a) (including the initial notification requirements in §63.9).

checklist: Engine type(s): confirm each engine is a four-stroke lean-burn (4SLB) or four-stroke rich-burn (4SRB) spark-ignited RICE.
Site-rated horsepower for each engine (document manufacturer/site-rated HP; e.g., 800 hp).
Source classification: confirm the facility is an area source of HAP (not a major source).
Operating status: confirm each engine is non-emergency vs emergency.
Annual hours of operation for each engine (determine whether operated more than 24 hours per calendar year).

Remote status tests: apply and document each remote criterion from §63.6675 — (a) offshore beyond line of ordinary low water (if applicable), (b) pipeline-segment test: count buildings intended for human occupancy within 1-mile segments and check for any buildings with ≥4 stories within 220 yards and 100-yard proximity to segment, and (c) non-pipeline test: count buildings within 0.25 mile and check for any buildings with ≥4 stories within 0.25 mile.
Dates and documentation showing when the engines met any claimed remote criteria (e.g., since October 2013).

Notification history: verify whether initial notifications, Notification of Intent to test, and Notification of Compliance Status required under Subpart ZZZZ/§63.9 have been submitted to the delegated State authority and/or EPA, and record submission dates and recipients.
Performance testing history: verify whether initial or annual performance tests have been performed (records, dates, methods, results) for these engines.

If claiming remote status to avoid performance testing, document the basis (which remote criterion applies), and retain mapping/site surveys and any communications with state/EPA regarding applicability or notifications.

judge_text: {"score": 1, "reason": "Some key points are present (the remote RICE definitions from §63.6675 and checklist items to document remote status and notifications), but the EPA Notes’ central points are missing or contradicted: the answer does not state that existing non‑emergency 4SLB/4SRB >500 hp at area sources do not require a remote‑status notification, it fails to cite the required 12‑month evaluation and recordkeeping duty at §63.6603(f), and it does not note that the delegated state (Utah DAQ) handles the conditional approval. Therefore only some EPA reasons are captured."}

candidates.title: Gasoline Dispensing Facilities (GDF) (Subpart CCCCCC)

criteria.criterion: if the facility is a gasoline dispensing facility (GDF) located at an area source, then the affected source includes each gasoline storage tank at that GDF and is subject to this subpart
if your GDF has a monthly throughput of less than 10,000 gallons of gasoline, then the affected source is subject to the requirements in § 63.11116 of this subpart
if a storage tank is not in gasoline service (for example it stores diesel or a fuel that does not meet the gasoline definition), then that tank is not covered by this subpart
if an item is the equipment used for the refueling of motor vehicles, then that equipment is not covered by this subpart

if an affected source's throughput ever exceeds an applicable throughput threshold, then the affected source will remain subject to the requirements for sources above the threshold even if throughput later falls below the threshold

if the facility dispenses gasoline into the fuel tanks of motor vehicles, nonroad vehicles, or nonroad engines, then the facility meets the definition of a gasoline dispensing facility (GDF) for this subpart

if dispensing from a fixed gasoline storage tank to a portable gasoline tank is performed for on-site delivery and subsequent dispensing into a motor vehicle, then that activity is subject only to § 63.11116

candidates.title: Area Source Standards for Bulk Gasoline Terminals, Pipeline Breakout Stations, Pipeline Pumping Stations, and Bulk Gasoline Plants (Subpart BBBBBB)

criteria.criterion: if you own or operate a bulk gasoline terminal, pipeline breakout station, pipeline pumping station, or bulk gasoline plant as identified in § 63.11081(a), then you are subject to this subpart

if gasoline storage tanks are located at an affected source identified in § 63.11081(a)(1)-(4) but are used only for dispensing gasoline in a manner consistent with tanks located at a gasoline dispensing facility as defined in § 63.11132, then those tanks are not subject to this subpart and must comply with subpart CCCCCC instead

if a bulk gasoline plant's annual average gasoline throughput reaches or exceeds 4,000 gallons per day, then the bulk gasoline plant will remain subject to the vapor balancing requirements even if the annual average throughput later falls below 4,000 gallons per day

checklist: For each tank, verify the fuel type stored (gasoline vs diesel) and for gasoline confirm Reid vapor pressure ≥ 27.6 kPa to meet the subpart's gasoline definition.
Determine whether the facility/practical location dispenses gasoline into the fuel tanks of motor vehicles, nonroad vehicles, or nonroad engines (i.e., whether it functions as a GDF per § 63.11132).

Calculate the monthly throughput for all gasoline storage tanks at each separate GDF using the method in § 63.11111(h)/§ 63.11132 (current day plus prior 364 days summed and divided by 12) and document results.
Confirm whether the tanks are 'storage tanks' in gasoline service (covered) versus only 'equipment used for refueling' (which the subpart excludes from coverage).
Check whether the tanks are part of a bulk gasoline terminal, pipeline breakout/pumping station, or bulk gasoline plant as listed in § 63.11081(a).
If subject to bulk-plant definitions, verify whether the tanks are used only in a manner consistent with GDF tanks (if so, they are excluded from subpart BBBBBB per § 63.11081(c)).

Verify whether any throughput ever exceeded applicable threshold levels (and if so, gather records showing the dates and amounts, because exceeding a threshold can make the source remain subject to higher-tier requirements per § 63.11111(i) and § 63.11081(f)).

Assemble and retain throughput records (and any required supporting documentation) so they can be produced within 24 hours upon request by the Administrator as required for area-source GDFs (§ 63.11116(b) and § 63.11111(e)/(j)).

These notes are therefore captured."}

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants for Portland Cement Plants (Subpart LLL)

criteria.criterion: if an inline coal mill is associated with a kiln, then the coal mill is an affected source subject to this subpart
if the inline coal mill has a separate stack associated with a kiln, then the combined PM emissions from the kiln and the coal mill stack are subject to the PM emissions limit in §63.1343(b)

if the coal mill exhaust is commingled with the kiln exhaust and sent to the kiln PM control device as a single stream, then the facility may meet an alternative PM emission limit calculated using Equation 1 (existing) or Equation 2 (new) in §63.1343(b)(2)

if your source is subject to limitations on PM emissions under §63.1343(b), then initial PM compliance must be demonstrated by a Method 5 or 5I performance test and continuous compliance must be demonstrated with a PM continuous parametric monitoring system (PM CPMS) with a site-specific operating limit established per §63.1349(b)(1) and §63.1350(b)

if the inline coal mill has a separate stack and you perform PM performance testing, then you must test the main kiln exhaust and the coal mill stack simultaneously and compute the combined PM emission rate for each run using Equation 8 in §63.1349(b)(1)(viii)

if you are determining the exhaust gas flow rate to the atmosphere from a coal mill stack for performance testing or emissions calculations, then you must either install, operate, calibrate and maintain a continuous exhaust gas flow instrument according to the requirements in §63.1350(n)(1)–(10) or use the maximum design exhaust gas flow rate as allowed in §63.1349(a)

if the PM performance test average is below or at/above 75 percent of the PM limit, then the procedure to calculate and set the PM CPMS site-specific operating limit follows the decision and equations in §63.1349(b)(1)(i)–(iv)

if the affected source (including coal mill contributions) is subject to PM performance testing, then each PM test must consist of at least three separate runs meeting the sample volume requirements specified in §63.1349(b)(1)(vi)

checklist: Confirm the coal mill is an "inline coal mill" associated with a Portland cement kiln (physical/duct connection or kiln gases intentionally diverted through the coal mill).
Confirm whether the coal mill exhausts to its own separate stack or is commingled with kiln/clinker cooler exhaust or routed to the kiln PM control device.

Determine whether the plant and kiln are subject to Subpart LLL (portland cement plant that is a major source or an area source) and whether the kiln is a new or existing source (to identify applicable PM limits/equations).

Measure or obtain design exhaust flow rates for the kiln (Qk), clinker cooler (Qc), alkali bypass (Qab) if present, and coal mill (Qcm) in consistent units (dscf/ton feed or scm/hr) for use in combined or alternative PM limit calculations.

Inventory whether the coal mill exhaust is treated by the same PM control device as the kiln (single stream to PMCD) or has its own control device and document PM control device type (fabric filter, ESP, none).

Verify presence or plan to install a continuous stack gas flow measurement system for the coal mill stack (or be prepared to use maximum design flow) per §63.1350(n), and document calibration/QA procedures.

Plan for PM performance testing using Method 5 or 5I with three runs and required sample volumes, and include simultaneous testing of kiln and coal mill stacks if coal mill has separate stack (prepare test plan and notify Administrator if requested).

Verify existing or plan to install a PM CPMS (specify instrument type, range, and signal output) and prepare to establish a site-specific PM CPMS operating limit following §63.1349(b)(1) and to repeat performance testing annually (or when instrument range/component changes).

Collect and retain data needed to compute combined lb/ton-clinker PM emissions (hourly PM mass from each tested stack, hourly clinker production or feed-to-clinker ratio, and flow rates) to apply Equation 8 and PM limit calculations.

Document where THC/Hg/HCl monitors (if present) measure relative to the coal mill (upstream of the mill or in the coal mill stack) since some metals and gas HAP monitoring may need to include coal mill stack measurements per the subpart requirements.

The OUR ANSWER captures the Subpart LLL combined-testing, PM CPMS, and annual/repeat testing requirements (§63.1349/63.1350) but fails to mention NSPS Subpart Y or the coal mill’s status as a thermal dryer, so a key reason from the EPA notes is missing."}

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants for Secondary Aluminum Production (Subpart RRR)

criteria.criterion: If an establishment uses aluminum scrap or dross as raw material and performs scrap drying, delacquering, or decoating, then it is a secondary aluminum production facility for purposes of this subpart.

If you are the owner or operator of a secondary aluminum production facility that is a major source of HAPs, then each scrap dryer/delacquering kiln/decoating kiln at the facility is an affected source subject to the requirements of this subpart.

If the facility is an area source of HAPs, then the requirements of this subpart pertaining to dioxin and furan emissions and associated operating, monitoring, reporting and recordkeeping apply to each scrap dryer/delacquering kiln/decoating kiln listed in §63.1500(c).
If the facility or equipment is used solely for research and development and not used to produce a saleable product, then the requirements of this subpart do not apply to that facility or equipment.

If the facility is an aluminum die casting facility, aluminum foundry, or aluminum extrusion facility that only melts clean charge, customer returns, or internal scrap and does not operate sweat furnaces, thermal chip dryers, or scrap dryers/delacquering kilns/decoating kilns, then it is not considered a secondary aluminum production facility for purposes of this subpart.

checklist: Confirm whether the plant uses aluminum scrap or dross as raw material (not just handling inert aluminum parts).

Confirm whether the delamination chambers are used primarily to remove organic contaminants (paint, lacquer, ink, plastic, rubber) or to separate foil/paper/plastic — i.e., whether they meet the definition of a scrap dryer/delacquering kiln/decoating kiln.
Determine whether the facility meets the regulatory definition of a secondary aluminum production facility under §63.1503 (performs one or more listed processes such as scrap drying/delacquering).

Determine whether the facility is a major source of HAPs (check applicability under the major/area source definitions in your permits and §63.2) or is an area source (this affects which provisions apply).
Verify whether the delamination units are used only for research & development and not to produce a saleable product (if so, the subpart does not apply per §63.1500(d)).

Verify whether the facility is an aluminum die casting/foundry/extrusion operation that only melts clean charge/internal scrap/customer returns and whether it operates scrap dryers/delacquering kilns (if it only melts clean charge and does not operate scrap dryers, it may not be a secondary aluminum production facility per §63.1503).

Collect documentation about the delamination unit operation (process description, typical feed materials, temperatures, and product flow) to compare with the definitions and affected-source listings in the cited sections.

Your answer includes the definitional/§63.1503 criteria but does not state or cite the post‑2015 change (that downstream melting is irrelevant), so only some key reasons are captured."}

candidates.title: Paint Stripping and Miscellaneous Surface Coating Operations for Area Sources (Subpart HHHHHH)

criteria.criterion: If you operate an area source of HAP and perform paint stripping using methylene chloride (MeCl) for removal of dried paint, then you are subject to this subpart.
If you operate an area source of HAP and perform spray application of coatings to motor vehicles or mobile equipment, then you are subject to this subpart.

If you are the owner or operator of a motor vehicle or mobile equipment surface coating operation and you spray apply no coatings that contain the target HAP and you submit a petition to the Administrator demonstrating this or, on and after May 9, 2023, you submit the notification described in § 63.11170(a)(2), then you are not subject to the surface coating provisions of this subpart.
If your spray coating applications meet the definition of facility maintenance in § 63.11180, then those spray coating applications are not subject to the surface coating provisions of this subpart.

If you perform spray application of coatings that contain the target HAP to plastic and/or metal parts or products (other than motor vehicles or mobile equipment), then you are subject to this subpart.
If your surface coating or paint stripping activities meet any of the exclusions listed in § 63.11169(d)(1) through (6), then those activities are not subject to this subpart.
If you are not an area source of HAP as defined in § 63.11170(b) (i.e., you are part of or are a major source), then this subpart's area-source provisions do not apply to you.

checklist: Confirm whether the facility is an area source per 40 CFR 63.11170(b) by calculating annual potential and actual HAP emissions (single HAP ≥10 tons/year or combined HAP ≥25 tons/year defines a major source).
Confirm whether you perform any paint stripping that uses methylene chloride (MeCl) for removal of dried paint (including frequency and processes where MeCl is used).
Determine annual MeCl usage in the facility (tons/year) to know if a written MeCl minimization plan is required (>1 ton/year triggers plan requirements per § 63.11173(b)).
Confirm whether you perform spray application of coatings to assembled motor vehicles or mobile equipment (including mobile, on-site repair vs fixed-location shop).

Determine whether any spray-applied coatings you use contain target HAP (Cr, Pb, Mn, Ni, Cd) at or above the thresholds in § 63.11180 (use supplier formulation data/MSDS representing HAP content as applied).

If you claim you spray apply no target-HAP-containing coatings, verify you have the formulation documentation to support that claim and whether you have submitted (or plan to submit) the petition or, on/after May 9, 2023, the notification to the Administrator as described in § 63.11170(a)(2) and § 63.11175.
Determine whether your spray activities qualify as facility maintenance under § 63.11180 (e.g., coatings to infrastructure or equipment intended to remain indefinitely) to assess that exclusion.

Verify whether your activities fall under any exclusions in § 63.11169(d)(1)–(6) (e.g., Armed Forces installations, military munitions, hobby/personal vehicles, research/lab activities, quality control activities, or are covered by another area source NESHAP).

If subject to the subpart, confirm recordkeeping and notification obligations (e.g., initial notification/notification of compliance status per § 63.11175 and retention of records of coatings and MeCl usage).

candidates.title: Area source paint stripping and miscellaneous surface coating operations (Subpart HHHHHH)

criteria.criterion: if you operate an area source of HAP and perform spray application of coatings that contain the target HAP to a plastic and/or metal substrate on a part or product (not motor vehicles or mobile equipment), then subject to this subpart

if you operate an area source of HAP and perform spray application of coatings to motor vehicles and mobile equipment (excluding spray coating that meets the definition of facility maintenance), then subject to this subpart

if a spray-applied coating contains any individual target HAP at or above the specified thresholds (≥0.1 percent by mass for carcinogenic target HAP such as cadmium, chromium, lead, or nickel; ≥1.0 percent by mass for manganese), then that coating is a target HAP containing coating
if your source is not an area source of HAP (for example, is a major source or is located at or part of a major source), then you are not the area source category addressed by this subpart

if the surface coating or paint stripping activity meets one of the exclusions (research and laboratory activities, quality control activities, facility maintenance, certain Federal/military installations, or activities covered under another area source NESHAP), then that activity is not covered by this subpart

if multiple surface coating operations and related equipment are located at the same source and under common control (mixing rooms, spray booths, spray guns, gun cleaning equipment, solvent handling, etc.), then they together constitute the affected source for determining applicability

checklist: Determine whether your facility is an area source (total HAP emissions potential < major source thresholds) or is a major source / part of a major source (see 40 CFR 63.11170(b))
Confirm whether the polyurea line uses spray-applied coating methods (hand-held or booth spray atomizing devices) as defined in §63.11180

For the polyurea line, obtain supplier formulation data/MSDS and calculate the target HAP concentration in the coating as applied (not just in purchased components) to verify whether any individual target HAP meets or exceeds ≥0.1% by mass (Cr, Cd, Pb, Ni) or ≥1.0% by mass (Mn)

Determine whether the parts coated on the polyurea line are motor vehicles or mobile equipment (motor vehicle/mobile equipment surface coating) or miscellaneous parts/products (metal/plastic parts not motor vehicles)

Determine whether the polyurea line activity is performed as facility maintenance, research and laboratory activities, or quality control activities (which are excluded) per the definitions in §63.11180 and exclusions in §63.11169(d)

Determine whether the polyurea line is part of the same affected source as other coating lines at your facility (mixing rooms, booths, spray guns, cleaning equipment, solvent handling) so that coatings used on other lines could affect overall source applicability per §63.11171(b)

If you coat motor vehicles/mobile equipment and you claim you spray apply no target HAP-containing coatings, prepare the petition or (on/after May 9, 2023) the notification to the Administrator and retain on-site records describing the coatings sprayed as allowed in §63.11170(a)(2)
Verify whether any other area source NESHAP covers the same coating activities at your facility (to assess the exclusion in §63.11169(d)(6))

candidates.title: Subpart YYYY

criteria.criterion: if your stationary combustion turbine is a new or reconstructed lean premix gas-fired stationary combustion turbine then you must comply with the emission limitations and operating limitations in Table 1 and Table 2 of this subpart

if your stationary combustion turbine is not equipped with an oxidation catalyst then you must petition the Administrator for operating limitations that you will monitor to demonstrate compliance with the formaldehyde emission limitation in Table 1 or petition for approval of no additional operating limitations, and you must not conduct the initial performance test until after the petition has been approved or disapproved by the Administrator

if you petition the Administrator for approval of additional operating limitations then your petition must include identification of the specific parameters, a discussion of the relationship between these parameters and HAP emissions, how you will establish upper and/or lower parameter values, the methods and instruments to measure and monitor the parameters including relative accuracy and precision, and the frequency and methods for recalibrating the instruments

if you petition the Administrator for approval of no additional operating limitations then your petition must identify parameters that could change, discuss any relationship between changes and HAP emissions, explain why establishing numeric limitations is not possible or feasible, describe measurement and monitoring methods and instruments and their accuracy/precision, describe recalibration frequency/methods, and explain why adopting parameters as operating limitations is infeasible, unreasonable, or unnecessary

if you are not using an oxidation catalyst then you must continuously monitor any parameters specified in your approved petition in order to comply with the operating limitations in Table 2 as specified in Table 5 of this subpart
if you are using an oxidation catalyst then you must continuously monitor your catalyst inlet temperature to comply with the operating limitations in Table 2 as specified in Table 5 of this subpart

if you are required to use a continuous monitoring system (CMS) after September 8, 2020 then you must develop and implement a CMS quality control program that includes written procedures per §63.8(d)(1) through (2) and keep those procedures on record

if you are required to conduct performance tests then you must conduct each performance test in Table 3 that applies to you and conduct the tests according to the requirements in Table 3 of this subpart

if you are required to conduct performance tests then the tests must be conducted at high load defined as 100 percent plus or minus 10 percent, must consist of three separate test runs each lasting at least 1 hour, and must not be conducted during periods of startup, shutdown, or malfunction with process information recorded to document operating conditions during the test

if you are required to comply with the formaldehyde emission limitation and complete a performance test then you must submit a Notification of Compliance Status including the performance test results before the close of business on the 60th calendar day following completion of the performance test

if you are required to conduct initial performance tests or other initial compliance demonstrations then you must conduct them within 180 calendar days after the compliance date specified for your stationary combustion turbine in §63.6095

if you start up a new or reconstructed stationary combustion turbine on or after March 5, 2004 then you must submit an Initial Notification not later than 120 calendar days after you become subject to this subpart

if you are required to conduct an initial performance test then you must submit a notification of intent to conduct the initial performance test at least 60 calendar days before the test is scheduled to begin

checklist: Confirm turbine classification: lean premix gas-fired stationary combustion turbine (new or reconstructed) and confirm the startup/date that determines whether it is a 'new or reconstructed' unit
Confirm whether the turbine is equipped with an oxidation catalyst (yes/no)

If no catalyst (your stated case), prepare and file a petition to the Administrator either proposing specific operating limitations to monitor or proposing no additional operating limitations; do not perform the initial performance test until petition is approved or disapproved

If proposing monitored parameters (e.g., turbine speed and inlet air temperature), document for each parameter: why it affects formaldehyde/HAP emissions, the expected relationship (how emissions change with parameter changes), proposed upper/lower limit values, and justification of those limits
For each proposed monitoring parameter, specify measurement method and instrument model, demonstrate instrument accuracy and precision, and specify calibration frequency and methods
Plan for continuous monitoring of the approved parameters (and implement a CMS quality control program with written procedures if CMS is required after Sept 8, 2020)
Schedule the initial performance test only after petition approval/disapproval and ensure test timing meets the requirement to be within 180 days after your compliance date per §63.6095

Prepare to conduct performance tests per Table 3 and ensure test conditions: high load (100% ±10%), three separate runs, each ≥1 hour, and avoid startup/shutdown/malfunction periods; record process data to show tests represent normal operation

Provide required notifications: Initial Notification within 120 days of becoming subject (if applicable), Notification of Intent to conduct initial performance test at least 60 days before the test, and Notification of Compliance Status including performance test results within 60 days after test completion
Retain records of monitoring procedures, calibrations, CMS quality control program, and performance test records to make available to the Administrator upon request

candidates.title: Metal Fabrication and Finishing Area Sources

criteria.criterion: if you own or operate an area source that is primarily engaged in the operations in one of the nine metal fabrication and finishing source categories listed in § 63.11514(a)(1)–(9) then this subpart applies to that area source

if you use materials that contain, or have the potential to emit, metal fabrication or finishing HAP (MFHAP) as defined by the metal content thresholds in § 63.11514(b) and § 63.11522 then the provisions of this subpart apply to each affected source that uses those materials

if your operations include dry abrasive blasting, machining, dry grinding and dry polishing with machines, spray painting, or welding that use materials that contain or have the potential to emit MFHAP then those operations constitute affected sources under this subpart

if the activities at the facility are limited to tool or equipment repair operations, facility maintenance, or quality control activities as defined in § 63.11522 then this subpart does not apply to those activities
if the facility is a research or laboratory facility as defined in CAA section 112(c)(7) then this subpart does not apply to that facility

if the operations are performed on-site at installations owned or operated by the U.S. Armed Forces, NASA, or NNSA, or the operations produce military munitions or equipment used directly and exclusively for transporting military munitions, then this subpart does not apply to those operations

if you commenced construction or reconstruction of the affected source before April 3, 2008 then the affected source is an existing affected source, and if you commenced construction or reconstruction on or after April 3, 2008 then the affected source is a new affected source (which affects applicable compliance dates)

checklist: Confirm whether the facility is an area source or a major source (actual and potential HAP emissions and permitting status).

Determine whether the facility is primarily engaged (≥50% of production by appropriate metric over the previous continuous 12 months) in one of the nine metal fabrication and finishing source categories listed in § 63.11514(a)(1)–(9); document the basis and calculations.

List all on-site operations and processes (specifically: dry abrasive blasting, welding, spray painting, machining, dry grinding/dry polishing with machines) and identify which are routinely performed.

For each material, coating, solvent, abrasive media, and welding rod used on-site, obtain MSDS/formulation data and verify metal content against MFHAP thresholds (cadmium, chromium, lead, nickel ≥0.1% by weight; manganese ≥1.0% by weight) to determine whether materials "contain MFHAP."

For dry abrasive blasting: verify whether blasting is performed in totally enclosed/unvented chambers or vented enclosures, whether blasting objects exceed 8 feet in any dimension, and whether blast media is reused or screened/filtered.

For spray painting: verify whether paints are spray-applied, whether paints contain MFHAP (per MSDS), whether spray booths/rooms are used and meet filter/waterwash criteria, type of spray equipment (HVLP, electrostatic, airless, etc.), and whether painters have/need required training/certification.

For welding: determine whether welding rods contain MFHAP (check MSDS) and calculate rolling 12-month welding rod usage in pounds to see if it is ≥2,000 lb/yr (which triggers additional welding requirements and records).

Determine whether any of the facility activities qualify as tool/equipment repair, facility maintenance, or quality control per § 63.11522 definitions (and document why activities do or do not meet those definitions).
Verify whether the facility is owned/operated by the Armed Forces, NASA, or NNSA, or performs military munitions production or uses equipment exclusively for transporting munitions.
Document dates of construction or reconstruction of affected sources (before or on/after April 3, 2008) to determine new vs. existing affected source status and applicable compliance dates.

Verify whether initial notifications, notifications of compliance status, and annual certification and compliance reports have been or must be submitted under § 63.11519 and note applicable deadlines; assemble and retain required records (manufacturer specifications for control devices, filter efficiency records, training records, welding rod usage records) for the required retention periods.

It does not, however, address the EPA Q&A SIC/NAICS lookup issue or explicitly require checking the EPA SIC/NAICS correspondence table cited by Region 1, so not all key reasons are reflected."}

candidates.title: Metal Fabrication and Finishing Area Sources (this subpart)

criteria.criterion: If you own or operate an area source that is primarily engaged in the operations in one of the nine source categories listed in §63.11514(a)(1)–(9) then you are subject to this subpart.

If manufacturing, fabricating, or forging of one or more products listed in one of the nine metal fabrication and finishing source categories represents at least 50 percent of the facility's production (using an industry-appropriate metric) over the previous continuous 12 months then the facility meets the 'primarily engaged' test.

If you perform machining, dry grinding/dry polishing with machines, dry abrasive blasting, spray painting, or welding operations that use materials that contain MFHAP or have the potential to emit MFHAP then those affected source operations (the affected sources listed in §63.11514(b)(1)–(5)) are subject to the requirements of this subpart.

If the materials you use (including paints and welding rods) do not contain MFHAP above the definition thresholds (cadmium, chromium, lead, or nickel ≥ 0.1% by weight as the metal; manganese ≥ 1.0% by weight as the metal) then the MFHAP-specific affected-source requirements do not apply to those operations.
If the activities performed are tool or equipment repair operations, facility maintenance, or quality control activities as defined in §63.11522 then those activities are not subject to this subpart.

If welding operations use 2,000 pounds or more per year of welding rod containing one or more MFHAP (calculated on a rolling 12‑month basis) then the additional management practice and fume-control monitoring requirements in §63.11516(f)(3)–(8) apply.

checklist: Confirm facility status as an 'area source' (i.e., not a major HAP source) using applicable major-source thresholds and record the basis.
Identify which of the nine source categories in §63.11514(a)(1)–(9) and Table 1 best describes your principal product/operation (review Table 1 descriptions).

Calculate production over the previous continuous 12 months by an industry-appropriate metric (units, volume, linear foot, square foot, etc.) and determine whether products in a single one of the nine categories represent ≥50% of facility production.

Document whether your on-site work on pumps (assembly of purchased components vs fabrication of components) constitutes 'manufacturing' or 'fabricating' of the listed products per Table 1 descriptions and retain the rationale (per §63.11522 and §63.10(b)(3)).

Inventory finishing operations (spot welding, dry machining, dry grinding, abrasive blasting, spray painting) and count how many pumps/units receive each finishing operation to support the production-based analysis.

For each material used in machining, grinding, blasting, painting, or welding, review manufacturer/supplier formulation data or MSDS to determine MFHAP content using the thresholds: cadmium, chromium, lead, nickel ≥0.1% by weight (as the metal); manganese ≥1.0% by weight (as the metal).

Determine whether spray painting performed is 'spray-applied painting' as defined (atomized hand-held devices etc.) and whether the paints used contain MFHAP; if paints do not contain MFHAP, spray-painting MFHAP requirements do not apply.
Measure or track annual usage (rolling 12‑month) of welding rods that contain MFHAP to see if usage is ≥2,000 lb/yr (this triggers additional welding-specific requirements).
Assess whether any of the tasks you perform meet the definitions of tool or equipment repair, facility maintenance, or quality control (if so, those activities are excluded); document justification.

If you perform dry abrasive blasting, determine whether blasting media or blasted substrates contain MFHAP and whether blasting is conducted in totally enclosed/unvented chambers versus vented enclosures (to identify applicable management practices and control requirements).
Maintain and retain records supporting the 'primarily engaged' determination and all MFHAP content determinations (MSDS/formulation data) and operational inventories used to evaluate applicability.

These capture the EPA notes that applicability is determined by the product-based production test, not by the share of pumps receiving finishing steps."}

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants for Stationary Reciprocating Internal Combustion Engines

criteria.criterion: If you own or operate a stationary RICE at a major or area source of HAP emissions then the engine is subject to Subpart ZZZZ.
If the engine is used to propel a motor vehicle or is a non-road engine as defined at 40 CFR 1068.30 then the engine is not a stationary RICE and is not subject to this subpart.
If the stationary RICE is being tested at a stationary RICE test cell/stand then it is not subject to this subpart.

If the engine is one of the existing residential, commercial, or institutional emergency stationary RICE located at an area source of HAP emissions that do not operate for the purpose specified in § 63.6640(f)(4)(ii) then it is not subject to this subpart.

If the stationary RICE meets the definition of existing, new, or reconstructed based on its site rating and construction/reconstruction dates in § 63.6590(a)(1) through (3) then it is an affected source under this subpart.

If the stationary RICE meets any of the criteria in § 63.6590(c)(1) through (7) (for example certain new or reconstructed engines or engines at area sources) then you must meet the requirements of 40 CFR part 60 (subpart IIII for CI engines or subpart JJJJ for SI engines) and no further requirements apply under this part.

checklist: For each diesel engine, confirm whether it is physically stationary (permanently affixed) or mounted on portable equipment that is moved frequently; determine whether it meets the non-road engine definition in 40 CFR 1068.30 (i.e., used to propel a vehicle).
Record each engine's fuel/type (diesel = compression ignition) and site-rated brake horsepower (HP).
Determine the plant's source classification: calculate potential to emit (PTE) of HAPs to decide if the facility is a major source (single HAP ≥ 10 tpy or total HAP ≥ 25 tpy) or an area source.

For each engine, document construction and reconstruction dates to classify as existing, new, or reconstructed according to the date/site-rating thresholds in 40 CFR 63.6590(a) (e.g., Dec 19, 2002 and June 12, 2006 dates referenced).

Determine whether each engine is operated as an emergency stationary RICE under the definition in 40 CFR 63.6675 (used to provide power/mechanical work during emergencies) and whether it operates for purposes excluded by § 63.6640(f)(4)(ii).
For each engine, record annual hours of operation to assess limited use status (e.g., limited use < 100 hours/yr) and any other limited-use designations referenced in § 63.6590.
Check whether any engine is being tested at a stationary RICE test cell/stand (excluded from this subpart).

Verify whether any engine is new or reconstructed and falls into the § 63.6590(c)(1)-(7) categories that require compliance with 40 CFR part 60 subpart IIII or JJJJ instead of further Part 63 requirements (e.g., new/reconstructed at area sources, CI engines ≤ 500 HP, etc.).

If applicable, verify whether any special exclusions or alternative compliance options apply (for example emergency engine categories or Tier certification pathways referenced in the subpart provisions).

candidates.title: Engine Test Cells/Stands (NESHAP)

criteria.criterion: if you own or operate an engine test cell/stand that is located at a major source of HAP emissions then you are subject to this subpart
if the apparatus is used for testing uninstalled stationary or uninstalled mobile (motive) engines located at a major source then it is part of the affected source for this subpart

if the affected source is existing (construction or reconstruction of the affected source was commenced on or before May 14, 2002) then the affected source does not have to meet the requirements of this subpart and of subpart A

if any portion of a new or reconstructed affected source located at a major source is used exclusively for testing internal combustion engines with rated power of less than 25 horsepower (19 kW) then that portion does not have to meet the requirements of this subpart (except the initial notification requirements of § 63.9345(b))

if any portion of a new or reconstructed affected source located at a major source is used exclusively for testing combustion turbine engines, rocket engines, research and teaching activities at non‑commercial facilities, or for testing/evaluating fuels, transmissions, or electronics then that portion does not have to meet the requirements of this subpart

if the affected source is new or reconstructed and is used in whole or in part for testing internal combustion engines with rated power of 25 horsepower (19 kW) or more and is located at a major source then you must comply with the emission limitations in Table 1 to this subpart
if an engine is installed in, or an integrated part of, the final product then it is not an "uninstalled engine" as defined for this subpart

checklist: Determine whether the plant is a major source of HAPs (≥10 tons/yr single HAP or ≥25 tons/yr combined HAP) as defined in 40 CFR 63.9285(c)
Confirm whether the test engines are 'uninstalled' (not installed in or an integrated part of the final product) per 40 CFR 63.9375

Determine whether the apparatus at the site is used for testing uninstalled stationary or uninstalled mobile (motive) engines (i.e., qualifies as an engine test cell/stand) per 40 CFR 63.9285(a) and 63.9290(a)
Establish whether the affected source is new/reconstructed (commenced construction after May 14, 2002) or existing (commenced on or before May 14, 2002) using the criteria in 40 CFR 63.9290(a)(1)
If new or reconstructed, verify whether any portion of the affected source is used exclusively for testing engines <25 hp (19 kW) per 40 CFR 63.9290(c)

If new or reconstructed, verify whether any portion is used exclusively for combustion turbines, rocket engines, non‑commercial research/teaching, or testing/evaluating fuels, transmissions, or electronics per 40 CFR 63.9290(d)(1)‑(4)
Confirm the rated power of the engines being tested (e.g., 335–600 hp) to evaluate the ≥25 hp threshold referenced in 40 CFR 63.9300 and 63.9290(c)

If the affected source is new or reconstructed and used in whole or in part to test engines ≥25 hp at a major source, determine the applicable emission limitations in Table 1 to this subpart per 40 CFR 63.9300

candidates.title: Utility Mercury and Air Toxics Standards (Utility MACT)

criteria.criterion: if you own or operate a coal-fired EGU or an oil-fired EGU as defined in § 63.10042 then subject
if an electric utility steam generating unit is not a coal- or oil-fired EGU and meets the definition of a natural gas-fired EGU in § 63.10042 then not subject

if an electric steam generating unit has the capability of combusting more than 25 MW of coal or oil but did not fire sufficient coal or oil to satisfy the average annual heat input requirement set forth in the definitions for coal-fired and oil-fired EGUs in § 63.10042 then not subject

candidates.title: Major Source Boiler MACT (Industrial/Commercial/Institutional Boilers and Process Heaters)

criteria.criterion: if you own or operate an industrial, commercial, or institutional boiler or process heater located at, or part of, a major source of HAP then subject

if the boiler or process heater is an electric utility steam generating unit covered by subpart UUUUU or a natural gas-fired EGU firing at least 85 percent natural gas on an annual heat input basis then not subject

checklist: Confirm whether the unit is an electric utility steam generating unit (EGU): does it serve a generator that produces electricity for sale and is it >25 MWe (or otherwise meets the EGU definition in 40 CFR 63.10042)?

Obtain the unit's permitted/actual fuel types and fuel handling capability (are oil and natural gas both permitted and supported by on-site fuel handling/storage?), as described in the "fossil fuel-fired" capability language in 40 CFR 63.10042

Calculate the 3-calendar-year rolling average percent heat input from oil (three previous calendar years) and the percent heat input from oil for any single calendar year to determine if oil combustion exceeds >10% (3-year average) or >15% (any one year) per 40 CFR 63.10042

Calculate the 3-calendar-year rolling average percent heat input from natural gas and the percent for any single year to determine if the unit meets the natural gas-fired EGU thresholds (>10% 3-year average or >15% any one year) in 40 CFR 63.10042
Determine whether annual heat input from natural gas is at least 85 percent (annual basis) to check the exclusion in 40 CFR 63.7491(a)

Verify whether the unit has the capability to combust more than 25 MW of coal or oil (permits, equipment such as coal handling, oil storage, etc.) to evaluate the applicability language in 40 CFR 63.9983(c)
Establish whether the facility is a major source of HAP (permitted/regulated status) to assess applicability of subpart DDDDD under 40 CFR 63.7485

Document startup fuel usage and hours (to support heat-input calculations and any limited-use classifications), including whether oil is used only during startup and the fraction of heat input attributable to those periods

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Pesticide Active Ingredient (PAI) Manufacturing (Subpart MMM)

criteria.criterion: If the distillation column is part of the facility-wide collection of pesticide active ingredient manufacturing process units (PAI process units) that process, use, or produce HAP at a plant site that is a major source then the unit is an affected source under subpart MMM

If construction or reconstruction of the affected source (or of the distillation as part of an affected source) commenced after November 10, 1997 then the source meets the new-source applicability criteria in subpart MMM

If the distillation equipment qualifies as a dedicated PAI process unit and has the potential to emit 10 tons/yr of any one HAP or 25 tons/yr of combined HAP then the dedicated-unit new-source criteria in subpart MMM apply

If the storage tanks and the distillation unit are assigned to a PAI process unit according to the storage-vessel input/output rules or tank-farm rules then those tanks and the distillation may be part of the affected source under subpart MMM

If the unit operation is a distillation (a unit operation or separation/purification step) used to produce or prepare intermediates or products primarily used as PAI then it fits within the definition of a PAI process unit for subpart MMM

If the operation meets any of the exemptions listed (research and development facility, PAI process units subject to subpart F, production of ethylene, coal tar distillation, specified emission points, or equipment intended to operate <300 hr/yr) then it is not subject to subpart MMM

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Miscellaneous Organic Chemical Manufacturing (Subpart FFFF)

criteria.criterion: If you own or operate miscellaneous organic chemical manufacturing process units (MCPU) that are located at, or are part of, a major source of HAP then those MCPU are subject to subpart FFFF

If the distillation equipment is part of an MCPU that produces materials described in §63.2435(b)(1) (organic chemicals identified by the listed SIC/NAICS codes or recovered solvents) and the MCPU processes, uses, or generates organic HAP then the equipment satisfies the MCPU definition in subpart FFFF
If the equipment or MCPU is an affected source or part of an affected source under another subpart of part 63 then it is not subject to subpart FFFF

If construction or reconstruction of the affected source (facility-wide MCPU collection) commenced after April 4, 2002 then the affected source meets the new-source applicability criteria in subpart FFFF

If the distillation is a dedicated MCPU with the potential to emit 10 tpy of any one HAP or 25 tpy of combined HAP and construction or reconstruction commenced after April 4, 2002 then it meets the dedicated-new-source criteria in subpart FFFF
If the operation falls within the exemptions listed in §63.2435(c) (e.g., research and development, specific NAICS/SIC exceptions, other enumerated exclusions) then it is not subject to subpart FFFF

checklist: Is the plant a major source of HAP (subject to CAA section 112(a))?
Is the material being produced/processed (2,4-D or its intermediates) a pesticide active ingredient (PAI) as defined in §63.1361?

Will the distillation column be operated as part of the PAI manufacturing process (physically and operationally integrated) or instead be part of a miscellaneous organic chemical manufacturing process (MCPU)?
Was construction or reconstruction of the distillation column (or affected source) commenced before or after Nov 10, 1997 (for Subpart MMM applicability)?
Was construction or reconstruction of the distillation column (or affected source) commenced before or after Apr 4, 2002 (for Subpart FFFF applicability)?

Will the distillation unit be a dedicated unit (designed/operated to produce only the PAI) and, if so, what is its potential to emit (PTE) HAP in tpy (estimate single-HAP and combined HAP PTE vs 10 tpy / 25 tpy thresholds)?

Which storage tanks supply the raw material and receive product, and for each tank determine: a) was the tank already subject to another 40 CFR part 63 subpart on June 23, 1999 (per §63.1360(f)(1))? b) does the tank's greatest input or output link it to the PAI process unit per §63.1360(f)(2)-(3)?
Are the existing raw material storage tanks contiguous or under common control such that they are on the same plant site per the plant-site definition in §63.1361?
Does the MCPU definition (NAICS/SIC codes in §63.2435(b)(1)) or any listed exclusions in §63.2435(c) cover your product/operation?
Does the distillation operation process, use, or generate organic HAP (confirm identity and concentrations of HAP in feed and product streams)?
Are there any other part 63 subparts that already apply to the distillation, tanks, or process vents (if yes, determine whether that other subpart or MMM/FFFF should be applied per overlap rules)?
Will the distillation or associated tanks operate less than 300 hours/year in organic HAP service (possible MMM exemption per §63.1360(d)(viii))?

If considering vapor routing/control: will you route vents to control devices or implement closed-vent systems that would trigger storage-vessel or process-vent control requirements under Subpart MMM (see §63.1362(b) and (c))?

candidates.title: Paints and Allied Products Area Source NESHAP

criteria.criterion: if you own or operate a facility that performs paints and allied products manufacturing that is an area source of HAP emissions and processes, uses, or generates materials containing HAP then you are subject to Subpart CCCCCCC

if the facility no longer processes, uses, or generates materials containing HAP and does not plan to process, use, or generate materials containing HAP in the future then the facility is no longer subject to Subpart CCCCCCC
if you are a research and development facility as defined in section 112(c)(7) of the CAA then you are not subject to Subpart CCCCCCC

candidates.title: Chemical Manufacturing Area Sources (CMPU) NESHAP

criteria.criterion: if you own or operate a chemical manufacturing process unit (CMPU) that is located at an area source and Table 1 HAP are present in the CMPU at the concentrations specified in §63.11494(a)(2) then you are subject to Subpart VVVVVV
if the operation is Manufacture of Paint and Allied Products that is subject to Subpart CCCCCCC then Subpart VVVVVV does not apply to that operation

candidates.title: Chemical Preparations (NAICS 325998) definitions (Subpart BBBBBBB)

criteria.criterion: if the operation is a chemical preparation operation (mixing, blending, milling, or extruding equipment used to manufacture chemical preparations under NAICS 325998) and the operation processes materials that are target HAP-containing (for nickel, compounds of nickel at or above 0.1 percent by weight as metal) then the operation is in target HAP service as defined in Subpart BBBBBBB and falls under that subpart's defined scope
if equipment in the chemical preparation operation neither contains, contacts, nor processes target HAP-containing materials then that equipment is not in target HAP service under Subpart BBBBBBB

checklist: Determine the NAICS code that applies to the cathode slurry mixing operation (is it within NAICS 325 or NAICS 325998 chemical preparations?).
Verify whether the facility will be an area source (i.e., total facility HAP emissions are below major source thresholds) or a major source for HAPs.

Determine whether the cathode slurry mixing activity is performed as part of 'paints and allied products manufacturing' at the facility (i.e., is the operation classified as paints & allied products manufacturing).

Measure or obtain formulation data (e.g., supplier SDS/formulation) for the active material and slurry to confirm presence and concentration (weight percent) of nickel (metal) in the material or feedstock; verify whether nickel compounds are ≥ 0.1% by weight (target HAP threshold in definitions).

Confirm whether the slurry/additions are handled as dry pigment/solid additions versus paste, slurry, or liquid form (i.e., are nickel-containing materials added as dry solids or already in slurry/liquid form).

Determine whether the cathode mixing/coating/drying equipment meets the definition of a CMPU (includes all process vessels, equipment, storage tanks and transfer operations associated with NAICS 325 chemical manufacturing per §63.11494(b)).

If considering Subpart VVVVVV, verify whether any Table 1 HAP (per §63.11494) are present in feedstocks or generated at the concentrations specified in §63.11494(a)(2) (use supplier formulation/SDS and use upper bound of any ranges).
Confirm whether the operation is covered by the exclusion that an affected CMPU does not apply if it is the Manufacture of Paint and Allied Products already subject to Subpart CCCCCCC.
Determine whether the operation qualifies as a research and development facility (CAA §112(c)(7)) or otherwise meets any exemptions noted in the cited sections.
Document whether mixing vessels store or process benzene or methylene chloride (to assess applicability of specific vessel requirements in Subpart CCCCCCC, §63.11601(b)).

However the EPA notes’ specific rationale that the cathode slurry is a ‘‘coating that leaves a dried film’’ (the basis for classifying it under paints & allied products per §63.11607) is not explicitly referenced or captured in the criteria/checklist (nor is §63.11607 cited), so the critical classificatory basis is missing."}

candidates.title: Area Source Glass Manufacturing (Subpart SSSSSS)

criteria.criterion: if you own or operate a glass manufacturing facility that manufactures flat glass, glass containers, or pressed and blown glass by melting raw materials to produce molten glass and form the molten glass into sheets, containers, or other shapes then subject
if the facility is an area source of HAP emissions (i.e., does not have the potential to emit any single HAP ≥ 9.07 Mg/yr (10 tpy) or any combination of HAP ≥ 22.68 Mg/yr (25 tpy)) then subject

if your glass manufacturing facility uses one or more continuous furnaces to produce glass that contains compounds of one or more glass manufacturing metal HAP as raw materials in a glass manufacturing batch formulation then subject

if a glass melting furnace is a continuous furnace, is charged with compounds of one or more glass manufacturing metal HAP as raw materials, and is used to produce glass at a rate of at least 45 Mg/yr (50 tpy) then subject
if a furnace is a research and development process unit then not subject

candidates.title: Area Source Paints and Allied Products Manufacturing (Subpart CCCCCCC)

criteria.criterion: if you own or operate a facility that performs paints and allied products manufacturing that is an area source of HAP emissions and processes, uses, or generates materials containing HAP then subject
if the affected source no longer processes, uses, or generates materials containing HAP and does not plan to process, use, or generate materials containing HAP in the future then not subject
if the facility is a research and development facility as defined in section 112(c)(7) of the CAA then not subject

candidates.title: Chemical Preparations Area Source (Subpart BBBBBBB)

criteria.criterion: if you own or operate a chemical preparations facility that is a stationary area source of HAP and the facility has at least one chemical preparations operation in target HAP service then subject
if the chemical preparations operations at your facility are subject to the requirements specified in subpart VVVVVV or subpart CCCCCCC then not subject to this subpart

checklist: Does the plant manufacture glass by melting raw materials into molten glass and forming the molten glass (i.e., meet the definition of a glass manufacturing facility)?
Is the plant an area source of HAPs (calculate potential to emit: any single HAP < 9.07 Mg/yr (10 tpy) and total HAP < 22.68 Mg/yr (25 tpy))?
Do you operate one or more continuous furnaces (not batch furnaces) for melting?
Are the furnaces charged with compounds of glass manufacturing metal HAP (e.g., nickel-containing raw materials)?
Is the glass produced by a given furnace at a rate of at least 45 Mg/yr (50 tpy) per furnace?
Is any furnace a research and development process unit?
Do any facility processes constitute paints and allied products manufacturing that process, use, or generate materials containing HAP?

Do any facility operations qualify as chemical preparations operations, and if so, are any in 'target HAP service' (verify the definition of chemical preparations operation and target HAP service in §63.11588)?
Are the chemical preparations operations at the facility already subject to subpart CCCCCCC (paints) or subpart VVVVVV (if so, subpart BBBBBBB may be exempt)?
What is the facility NAICS code(s) and do facility activities align with NAICS descriptions (e.g., frit production method vs. paint or chemical preparations manufacturing)?
Does the facility currently have, or need, a Title V permit under 40 CFR part 70/71 (note: Subpart SSSSSS area sources must obtain a permit per 63.11449(e))?
