YOUR ANSWER includes the paints subpart (CCCCCCC) criterion for facilities that process/use HAP-containing materials and prompts checking NAICS codes and whether operations are HAP-containing, and it also captures the exclusion of the chemical-preparations subpart (BBBBBBB) where operations are subject to the paints subpart or VVVVVV. However, the EPA Notes’ key specifics — that NAICS 3255 covers products intended to leave a dried film on a substrate and that nickel >0.1% makes the material HAP-containing — are not explicitly stated in the candidate criteria (the numeric Ni threshold and the ‘‘dried film’’/NAICS-3255-as-paints rationale are missing)." }

candidates.title: Secondary Aluminum Production (Subpart RRR)

criteria.criterion: if the facility is a secondary aluminum production facility and is a major source of HAPs and there is a thermal chip dryer at the facility then the thermal chip dryer is an affected source under this subpart

if the facility is a secondary aluminum production facility and is an area source and there is a thermal chip dryer at the facility then the subpart's dioxin/furan requirements apply to the thermal chip dryer
if a unit uses heat to evaporate oil or oil/water mixtures from unpainted or uncoated aluminum chips then that unit is a thermal chip dryer for purposes of this subpart

if a unit is used solely to remove water from aluminum scrap (for example pre-heating boxes or dryers used solely to remove water) then it is not considered a thermal chip dryer for purposes of this subpart

if a thermal chip dryer is subject to initial performance testing then the owner or operator must conduct a performance test to measure THC and D/F emissions at the outlet of the control device while the unit processes only unpainted aluminum chips

if a thermal chip dryer has emissions controlled by an afterburner then the owner or operator must record the type of materials charged for each operating cycle and submit a certification of compliance with the applicable operational standard for charge materials every 6 months

checklist: Confirm whether your facility meets the regulatory definition of a "secondary aluminum production facility" in 40 CFR 63.1503 (does the establishment perform scrap shredding, scrap drying/delacquering/decoating, thermal chip drying, furnace operations, dross recovery, in-line fluxing, or dross cooling?).
Determine whether the facility is a major source (potential to emit ≥10 tpy of any single listed HAP or ≥25 tpy of combined HAP) or an area source.

Determine whether the dryer is designed and operated to evaporate oil or oil/water mixtures from unpainted/uncoated aluminum chips (thermal chip dryer function) or is used solely to remove water (pre-heating/water-removal dryer).
Verify whether the chips/metal charged to the unit are painted/coated or unpainted/uncoated for typical operation and for any required performance test periods.

If the unit is claimed to be a thermal chip dryer, verify whether an afterburner or other control device is installed and whether performance testing for THC and D/F will be conducted while processing only unpainted chips as required.
Record the type of materials charged to the unit for each operating cycle and prepare to submit the 6-month certification of compliance with charge-material operational standards if applicable.

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants from Coal- and Oil-Fired Electric Utility Steam Generating Units (Subpart UUUUU)

criteria.criterion: if the unit meets the definition of an electric utility steam generating unit (EGU) in 40 CFR 63.10042 (i.e., a fossil fuel-fired unit >25 MWe that serves a generator producing electricity for sale and, for oil-fired, meets the oil-fired fuel-use thresholds), then the requirements of this subpart apply to the unit unless excluded under 40 CFR 63.9983
if fuel is fired in the boiler after a shutdown event for any purpose, then that period is 'startup' under 40 CFR 63.10042(1)

if you elect to rely on paragraph (2) of the 'startup' definition prior to January 2, 2025, then startup begins when fuel is fired to produce electricity or useful thermal energy (including steam) after a shutdown and ends 4 hours after the EGU generates electricity or makes useful thermal energy (including on-site use) as specified in 40 CFR 63.10042(2) and allowed by 40 CFR 63.10000(m)

if your EGU is coal-fired, liquid oil-fired, or solid oil-derived fuel-fired, then the numeric emission limits in this subpart do not apply during startup and shutdown and you must meet the startup/shutdown work practice requirements in Table 3 to this subpart as described in 40 CFR 63.10000(a) and 40 CFR 63.10021(h)

if you rely on paragraph (2) of the 'startup' definition for startup periods (only allowed before January 2, 2025), then you must record the timing and quantity/heat input of clean fuel and gross output and other startup data required by 40 CFR 63.10020(e)

checklist: Confirm the unit's classification: is it an EGU as defined in 40 CFR 63.10042 (capacity >25 MWe and serves a generator that produces electricity for sale)?

Determine fuel-use history: did the unit burn oil for more than the oil-fired EGU threshold (see 40 CFR 63.10042) based on the average annual heat input over the prior 3 calendar years after the compliance date?
Verify whether the particular firing event occurs after a shutdown (i.e., is it a firing 'after a shutdown event'?)
Determine the purpose of the firing: is it to produce electricity for sale, or to produce useful thermal energy/steam for on-site use (e.g., tank heating) only?

Decide which startup definition you are relying on (paragraph (1) or, if before Jan 2, 2025, paragraph (2) of 40 CFR 63.10042) and confirm the date (on/after Jan 2, 2025 paragraph (2) is no longer available per 40 CFR 63.10000(m))

If relying on paragraph (2) of the startup definition (pre-Jan 2, 2025), prepare to record the required startup/shutdown data (dates/times fuel changes, quantity and heat input of clean fuel each startup hour, gross output each startup hour) per 40 CFR 63.10020(e)

If the unit is coal-, liquid oil-, or solid oil-derived fuel-fired, identify the applicable work practice items in Table 3 (startup/shutdown) and ensure monitoring systems and records required by 40 CFR 63.10000(l) and 40 CFR 63.10020 are in place
Check whether the unit is excluded from this subpart under 40 CFR 63.9983 (for example, if it qualifies as a natural gas-fired EGU or otherwise meets an exclusion) and document supporting evidence

Thus the EPA Notes’ key reason (that producing auxiliary steam is outside startup) is not captured."}

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants for Coal- and Oil-Fired Electric Utility Steam Generating Units (EGUs)

criteria.criterion: if the unit is an electric utility steam generating unit (EGU) — i.e., a fossil fuel-fired combustion unit of more than 25 MWe that serves a generator that produces electricity for sale — then it falls within the class of EGUs addressed by this subpart

if the unit burns oil for more than 10.0 percent of the average annual heat input during the 3 previous calendar years (or more than 15.0 percent of the annual heat input in any one of those calendar years) then it meets the definition of an oil-fired EGU for this subpart

if an oil-fired EGU has an annual capacity factor when burning oil of less than 8 percent of its maximum (or nameplate) heat input, averaged over a 24-month contiguous period commencing on the first of the month following the applicable compliance date, then it qualifies as a limited-use liquid oil-fired EGU subcategory

if your unit qualifies as a limited-use liquid oil-fired EGU as defined in § 63.10042 then it is not subject to the emission limits in Tables 1 and 2 of this subpart (but must comply with the performance tune-up work practice requirements in Table 3)

if the unit does not meet the definition of an oil- or coal-fired EGU because it did not fire sufficient oil or coal to satisfy the percentage-based fuel thresholds in § 63.10042 then it is not an oil-fired or coal-fired EGU for purposes of this subpart
if the unit meets the definition of a natural gas-fired EGU in § 63.10042 (i.e., is not a coal- or oil-fired EGU) then it is not subject to this subpart

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants for Major Sources: Industrial, Commercial, and Institutional Boilers and Process Heaters

criteria.criterion: if a boiler is an electric utility steam generating unit (EGU) covered by subpart UUUUU then that boiler or process heater is not subject to subpart DDDDD
if a unit meets the definition of a natural gas-fired EGU and fires at least 85 percent natural gas on an annual heat input basis then it is not subject to subpart DDDDD

checklist: Confirm whether Unit 1 meets the EGU definition: maximum electrical output >25 MWe and produces electricity for sale (check permits and net summer capacity).
Determine the unit's maximum (nameplate) hourly heat input (MMBtu/hr) used in the capacity factor calculation.
Calculate annual heat input from oil for the relevant years (MMBtu) and for the 24-month contiguous block(s) required (total oil heat input per year and per 24 months).

Compute the capacity factor for oil use: (total annual heat input from oil) / (maximum hourly heat input × 8,760) and then average over the required 24-month block to compare to the 8% limited-use threshold.

Determine the percentage of annual heat input from oil versus other fuels for each of the previous 3 calendar years to evaluate the >10% (3-year average) or >15% (any one year) thresholds for 'oil-fired EGU' status.
Identify and classify the specific fuels burned (confirm No. 2 fuel oil = distillate oil, No. 4 fuel oil = residual oil) to ensure they fall under the 'oil' definitions in § 63.10042.

Document the amount of natural gas burned (annual heat input from natural gas) to confirm whether the unit might instead meet the natural gas-fired EGU criteria or the ≥85% natural gas exclusion for subpart DDDDD.
Record the facility's applicable compliance date (and the first day of the 24-month averaging period following that compliance date) used for determining limited-use status.

Verify whether the unit sells electricity to the grid (or otherwise meets the 'serves a generator that produces electricity for sale' criterion) and whether any permit or physical limitations affect the unit's fuel capability.
If relying on prior-year fuel data, ensure fuel usage records (fuel invoices, fuel meters, heat input calculations) are available and auditable for the required averaging periods.

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants: Miscellaneous Coating Manufacturing Operations

criteria.criterion: if you own or operate miscellaneous coating manufacturing operations that are located at or are part of a major source of hazardous air pollutant (HAP) emissions then you are subject to Subpart HHHHH
if you manufacture coatings as defined in 40 CFR 63.8105 then you are subject to Subpart HHHHH
if you process, use, or produce HAP then you are subject to Subpart HHHHH
if your operations are part of an affected source under another subpart of part 63 then you are not subject to Subpart HHHHH

if a formulation component is synthesized by chemical reaction or separation activity and then transferred to another vessel where it is formulated and the synthesized or separated component is not stored prior to formulation then the resulting material is not considered a 'coating' for purposes of this subpart

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants: Miscellaneous Organic Chemical Manufacturing Process Units (MCPU)

criteria.criterion: if you own or operate a miscellaneous organic chemical manufacturing process unit (MCPU) that is located at or is part of a major source of HAP emissions then you are subject to Subpart FFFF

if an MCPU produces material(s) described in §63.2435(b)(1) (e.g., organic chemicals under the cited SIC/NAICS descriptions) and the MCPU processes, uses, or generates organic HAP or hydrogen halide and halogen HAP then the equipment collectively functions as an MCPU subject to Subpart FFFF
if the MCPU is an affected source or part of an affected source under another subpart of part 63 then Subpart FFFF does not apply to that affected source (with the exceptions noted in the regulation)

if the manufacturing process includes separation, recovery, or purification unit operations (for example filtration, decanters, distillation, condensers, or other separation equipment) then those steps are part of a miscellaneous organic chemical manufacturing process for purposes of Subpart FFFF

if the operations are affiliated operations located at an affected source under subparts GG, KK, JJJJ, MMMM, or SSSS (for example mixing or dissolving of coating ingredients; cleaning of coating lines; handling and storage of coatings and solvent) then those affiliated operations are excluded from Subpart FFFF

checklist: Is the facility a major source of HAP (determine major source status per CAA §112(a))?

Does the operation produce a product that meets the regulatory definition of 'coating' (i.e., produced by blending, mixing, diluting, or otherwise formulated) or does it meet the exclusion (a formulation component was synthesized by chemical reaction or separation activity then transferred and not stored prior to formulation)?

Is the final filtration step a separation/purification activity that yields a synthesized or separated component that is transferred to another vessel (without storage), or is filtration only a final quality-control step removing solids from a finished formulated coating?

Which HAP (if any) are processed, used, or produced in the operation and at what concentrations and annual mass (to document whether HAP are present and whether thresholds for MCPU definitions are met)?

Is the equipment chain (including filters, reactors, mixers, storage tanks, transfer racks) organized and used as an MCPU as defined in §63.2550 (i.e., does it include reaction, recovery, separation, purification, or other unit operations)?
Are any of the operations already part of an affected source under another Part 63 subpart (e.g., subparts covering surface coating or other industry-specific NESHAPs)?

Are the coating-related activities at the site considered 'affiliated operations' at an affected source covered by subparts GG, KK, JJJJ, MMMM, or SSSS (examples: mixing/dissolving of coating ingredients, coating line cleaning, handling/storage of coatings and solvent)?

For any component claimed as a synthesized or separated intermediate, document whether that component is stored prior to formulation (presence/absence of storage and vessel identification) and whether the separation step (including filtration) is listed among unit operations in the MCPU definition.

Does the filter operation produce or recover a separate liquid or solid stream that is subsequently reused, recycled, or transferred to another vessel (document stream composition and downstream disposition)?
For transfer racks or storage tanks potentially shared among processes, determine predominant use per the relevant subpart procedures (to decide assignment to coating operations or to an MCPU)

However it does not explicitly capture the EPA's central finding that a final product filtration is not a 'separation activity' under 63.8105 (the determination that filtering is not a separation/purification step is only posed as a question in the checklist, not stated as a criterion)." }

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants: Petroleum Refineries (Subpart CC)

criteria.criterion: If a combustion device lacks an enclosed combustion chamber and uses an uncontrolled volume of ambient air to burn gases then the device is a 'flare' under this subpart and the flare-specific requirements in §63.670 apply when that flare is used as a control device for an emission point subject to this subpart.

If the combustion device is an enclosed combustion device (for example, an incinerator, boiler, or process heater) then it is not a 'flare' under this subpart and the monitoring provisions for incinerators, boilers, or process heaters in §63.644(a)(1), (3), or (4) apply instead.

If a Group 1 miscellaneous process vent uses a combustion device to comply with §63.643(a) then the owner or operator must install and operate the monitoring equipment specified in §63.644(a) (or request approval for alternate monitoring under §63.644(b)) depending on the type of combustion device used.

checklist: Determine whether the truck loading rack vent is a Group 1 miscellaneous process vent (verify total organic HAP concentration and TOC/emission rate thresholds used to classify Group 1).
Confirm whether the vented vapors are routed to a fuel gas system (miscellaneous process vents routed to a fuel gas system are excluded per definition).

Obtain the combustor's design documentation and vendor/manual specifications to verify whether the device has an enclosed combustion chamber (i.e., is physically enclosed vs an open tip) and whether combustion relies on an uncontrolled volume of ambient air.

Verify whether the combustor is designed and operated as an incinerator, boiler, or process heater (e.g., presence of a firebox, catalyst bed, or heat recovery to produce steam) versus a flare-type tip without an enclosed chamber.
Determine whether the combustor receives the regulated material from the loading-rack vent as a control device used to comply with §63.643(a).
Document how combustion air is supplied (ambient uncontrolled entrainment vs intentional assist air/steam or forced-air system) and whether there is an open flare tip or a sealed stack/firebox.
Check for bypass lines or valves that could divert the vent stream away from the combustor and whether these are secured/monitored per §63.644(c).

If classified as a flare, verify presence and type of pilot(s), pilot monitoring capability, and other features required by §63.670 (pilot flame monitoring, flow/composition monitoring, visible emissions monitoring, assist steam/air measurement).

If classified as an enclosed control device (incinerator/boiler/heater), identify the monitoring equipment installed (e.g., temperature monitor with continuous recorder) and confirm it meets the monitoring options in §63.644(a).
Retain records/drawings showing the physical boundary between the vent stream and the combustion device (piping diagrams, point(s) where vent gas meets device) to support the classification decision.

judge_text: {"score":2,"reason":"The answer includes the key legal basis cited by EPA: the §63.641 definition of a flare (and that an enclosed combustion device is not a flare) and the consequence that §63.670/63.671 flare requirements therefore do not apply. It also captures the follow-up requirement that the combustor must be treated under the enclosed-device/Group 1 monitoring provisions (§63.644/§63.643) — i.e., tested/monitored to demonstrate compliance with Subpart CC limits — and the checklist items cover verifying enclosure, control use, and monitoring. No substantive EPA note reason is missing."}

candidates.title: Paper and Other Web Coating Operations

criteria.criterion: If a facility is a major source of HAP and operates web coating lines (as defined in §63.3310), then the provisions of this subpart apply to the facility.

If an operation applies a continuous layer of liquid or semi-liquid coating material across the entire width or any portion of the width of a continuous substrate (a web) and has any associated curing/drying equipment between an unwind/feed station and a rewind/cutting station, then that operation meets the definition of a web coating line and is part of the affected source for this subpart.

If the substrate is not a continuous substrate flexible enough to be wound or unwound as rolls (i.e., is sheet-fed rather than roll-fed), then the operation is not a 'web' (and thus not a web coating line) under this subpart.
If a web coating line falls within any of the categories listed in paragraphs (a) through (g) of §63.3300, then that web coating line is not part of the affected source under this subpart.

If a web coating line coats both paper (or another web) and another substrate, then the subpart that applies is determined by the predominant activity (90 percent or more of the mass of substrate coated during the compliance period), and if 90 percent or more is paper/web then this subpart applies (rather than subpart OOOO).

If a web coating line is modified to include printing activities and the mass of materials applied to the line's print station(s) in a month ever exceeds 5 percent of the total mass of materials applied to the line during that month, then the owner/operator must evaluate the 5 percent threshold (and may elect to continue complying with this subpart in lieu of subpart KK under the stated conditions).

If all of the subject web coating lines at the facility utilize only non-HAP coatings and a one-time report documenting use of only non-HAP coatings is submitted as required, then the facility can become exempt from the reporting requirements of this subpart.

checklist: Determine whether the facility is a major source of HAP (check total actual potential HAP emissions against the major-source threshold).
For each production line, verify whether the substrate is a continuous, flexible web capable of being wound/unwound as rolls (roll-fed) or is sheet-fed (individual sheets).

For each roll-fed line, verify whether coating is applied as a continuous layer across all or part of the web width and whether there is curing/drying equipment located between an unwind/feed station and a rewind/cutting station.
For the sheet-handling line, document whether the operation uses discrete sheets (not a continuous web) to determine if it falls outside the web coating definition.

Check whether any web coating line at the facility is already regulated under one of the exclusions in §63.3300(a)–(g) (e.g., included in subpart KK, product and packaging rotogravure or wide-web flexographic press under subpart KK, lithography/screenprinting/narrow-web flexographic printing, subpart EE, subpart SSSS, subpart OOOO, or is research/laboratory equipment).

If a line coats multiple substrate types, calculate the mass of substrate coated by type over a representative period (at least one year or a period expected to represent future operations) to determine whether web/paper is the predominant activity (≥90%) and prepare annual documentation of that determination.
If printing stations are present, track monthly mass of materials applied to print stations and total mass applied to the line to evaluate the 5 percent monthly threshold in §63.3300(i).

Inventory the coatings used on each line for organic HAP content; if coatings are non-HAP only and you intend to claim the reporting exemption, prepare the one-time report referenced in §63.3300(j) for submission to the permitting authority.
Document whether each affected source is new or existing (construction/reconstruction date relative to 9/13/2000) if needed for determining applicable emission-standard levels under this subpart.

judge_text: {"score":1,"reason":"The answer captures the key reasons for subpart JJJJ (distinguishing roll-fed continuous web vs sheet-fed and the web-coating definition/exclusions under §63.3310/§63.3300), but it fails to address the EPA’s second key point: the determination that the finished mica insulation products are not refractory products under §63.9824 (subpart SSSSS), so that rationale is missing."}

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants: Natural Gas Transmission and Storage (Glycol Dehydration Units)

criteria.criterion: If a facility transports or stores natural gas prior to entering the pipeline to a local distribution company or final end user and is a major source of HAP emissions, then this subpart applies to the owner or operator
If a glycol dehydration unit (large or small) is present at the facility, then each such glycol dehydration unit is an affected source under this subpart

If an enclosed device uses controlled flame combustion and its primary purpose is to transfer heat to a process fluid or process material rather than for steam generation, then it meets the definition of a process heater under this subpart
If a boiler or process heater is used as the control device for a glycol dehydration unit process vent, then the vent stream must be introduced into the flame zone of the boiler or process heater
If gas or vapor from regulated equipment is routed to a process (for example, to a fuel gas system), then the conveyance system shall not be considered a closed-vent system under this subpart

If an enclosed combustion device is used as the control device, then it must meet one of the performance requirements in this subpart (95 percent mass reduction, ≤20 ppmv dry @ 3% O2 outlet, or operate at ≥760 °C as demonstrated) as specified in §63.1281(d)(1)(i)(A)–(C)

If gases, vapors, or fumes from the emissions units are routed through a closed-vent system to a control device, then the control device must be operating at all times when those gases are vented to it

checklist: Determine whether the facility is a major source of HAPs (calculate/confirm per 40 CFR 63.1270(a) using throughput or other documented method).

Confirm whether one or more glycol dehydration units are present and identify each unit as a 'large' or 'small' glycol dehydration unit per the definitions and thresholds in 40 CFR 63.1271 and 63.1270(b).

Document the current routing of the glycol dehydration unit process vent(s) (e.g., still vent): to a flare, to a closed-vent/control device, to a fuel gas/process line, or vented directly to atmosphere.

For the reboiler: confirm the primary purpose of the unit (steam/hot water generation versus direct heating of a process fluid), and compare to the 'boiler' and 'process heater' definitions in 40 CFR 63.1271.

Verify whether the glycol process vent stream is physically introduced into the flame zone of the reboiler/burner (review piping diagrams, as-built drawings, and manufacturer/designer documentation showing where the vent stream enters the device).

If the reboiler burner is claimed as the control device, verify that the control device meets the applicable performance requirement (95% reduction or ≤20 ppmv dry corrected to 3% O2 or demonstrated operation ≥760 °C) and that required performance demonstration records exist (see 40 CFR 63.1281(d)(1)(i)).

Confirm whether the conveyance from the glycol unit to the reboiler would be considered a closed-vent system or whether it is routed to a process/fuel gas system (if routed to a process, it is not a closed-vent per 40 CFR 63.1271).

Verify that, if the reboiler is used as the control device, the reboiler/control device is operated whenever gases are vented to it and that operational/monitoring records demonstrate continuous operation during venting (per 40 CFR 63.1281(d)(4)(i) and 63.1281(f)(2)(i)).

Collect design and operational evidence showing the reboiler exhaust path (does combustion exhaust go straight to atmosphere without receiving glycol vent?) including stack drawings, P&IDs, and commissioning/operational records.

If there are any bypasses, drains, safety devices, or potential routes that could divert vented gases away from the control device, document their existence and how they are secured or monitored (see 40 CFR 63.1281(c)(3)).

judge_text: {"score":1,"reason":"Partial match. The submission captures the process-heater/heat-transfer definition and checks on where the vent is routed and whether the reboiler is acting as a control device, but it fails to capture the EPA’s key points that HHH only covers still-vent/flash-tank emissions (i.e., HHH does not reach the reboiler combustion chamber) and that Subpart DDDDD (see 63.7575) applies because the reboiler’s fuel is not regulated by another subpart and its exhaust is uncontrolled. The candidate list omits DDDDD and contains no criterion about ‘fuel regulated by another subpart’ or that uncontrolled exhaust triggers the boiler/process heater MACT."}

candidates.title: Area Source NESHAP for Electric Arc Furnace (EAF) Steelmaking (Subpart YYYYY)

criteria.criterion: if you own or operate an electric arc furnace (EAF) steelmaking facility that is an area source of hazardous air pollutant (HAP) emissions then subject to Subpart YYYYY
if the EAF steelmaking facility is located at a steel foundry or is used to produce nonferrous metals then not subject to Subpart YYYYY

if the affected source is existing or new is determined by whether construction or reconstruction commenced on or before or after September 20, 2007 then that classification applies for Subpart YYYYY applicability

candidates.title: Area Source NESHAP for Iron and Steel Foundries (Subpart ZZZZZ)

criteria.criterion: if you own or operate an iron and steel foundry that is an area source of HAP emissions then subject to Subpart ZZZZZ

if your facility melts scrap, ingot, and/or other forms of iron or steel and pours the resulting molten metal into molds to produce final or near final shape products for introduction into commerce then the facility meets the definition of an iron and steel foundry
if your iron and steel foundry becomes a major source as defined in § 63.2 then you must meet the requirements of 40 CFR part 63, subpart EEEEE (rather than remain covered only under Subpart ZZZZZ)

if the affected source is existing or new is determined by whether construction or reconstruction commenced before or on/after September 17, 2007 then that classification applies for Subpart ZZZZZ applicability and sizing
if the facility is a research and development facility as defined in section 112(c)(7) of the CAA then not subject to Subpart ZZZZZ
if you are an existing affected source you must determine whether you are a small or large foundry based on calendar year 2008 metal melt production (≤20,000 tons = small; >20,000 tons = large)
if you are a new affected source you must determine whether you are a small or large foundry based on annual metal melt capacity at startup (≤10,000 tons = small; >10,000 tons = large)

candidates.title: NESHAP for Iron and Steel Foundries (Subpart EEEEE)

criteria.criterion: if you own or operate an iron and steel foundry (new or existing affected source) then Subpart EEEEE covers emissions from metal melting furnaces, scrap preheaters, pouring areas, pouring stations, automated conveyor and pallet cooling lines, automated shakeout lines, mold and core making lines, and fugitive emissions from foundry operations
if your iron and steel foundry becomes a major source as defined in § 63.2 then you must meet the requirements of Subpart EEEEE

if the affected source is existing or new is determined by whether construction or reconstruction commenced before or on/after December 23, 2002 then that classification applies for Subpart EEEEE applicability

checklist: Is your facility an electric arc furnace (EAF) that produces molten steel heated by electric arcs (i.e., does your furnace match the EAF definition)? (see 40 CFR 63.10692 and 40 CFR 63.10906)
Is the EAF located at a steel foundry or used to produce nonferrous metals (EAF steelmaking subpart excludes EAFs at steel foundries and EAFs producing nonferrous metals)? (see 40 CFR 63.10692)

Do you melt scrap, ingot, or other iron/steel and pour the resulting molten metal into molds to make final or near-final shape products for commercial sale (i.e., do you perform the 'pouring into molds' step that defines an iron and steel foundry)? (see 40 CFR 63.10906 and 40 CFR 63.10880(a))

Do you instead atomize molten metal (e.g., water atomization to make shot/grit) rather than pouring into molds? (this determines whether the 'pouring into molds' foundry definition applies) (see 40 CFR 63.10906)
Is your operation a research and development facility excluded from the foundry subpart definitions? (see 40 CFR 63.10880(d))
Is your facility an area source or a major source of HAPs (total HAP emissions determination per § 63.2)? (see 40 CFR 63.10680(a) and 40 CFR 63.10880(c))
If a foundry, what was your calendar year 2008 metal melt production (to classify existing foundries as small ≤20,000 tons or large >20,000 tons)? (see 40 CFR 63.10880(f))
If a new foundry, what is your annual metal melt capacity at startup (to classify new foundries as small ≤10,000 tons or large >10,000 tons)? (see 40 CFR 63.10880(g) and 40 CFR 63.10906)

When did you commence construction or reconstruction of the affected source (compare to 9/20/2007 for Subpart YYYYY; 9/17/2007 for Subpart ZZZZZ; 12/23/2002 for Subpart EEEEE)? (see 40 CFR 63.10680(b), 40 CFR 63.10880(b), 40 CFR 63.7682(c)-(d))

Which specific foundry operations do you conduct (mold/core making, pouring, shakeout, shotblasting, grinding, sand handling, scrap preheating, etc.) to see which subpart provisions or subparts cover those emissions points? (see 40 CFR 63.7682(b) and 40 CFR 63.10906 definitions)

judge_text: {"score":2,"reason":"The answer includes the 63.10906 pouring‑into‑molds definition and explicitly asks whether the facility atomizes rather than pours, and it also includes Subpart YYYYY applicability for EAF steelmaking—capturing EPA’s rationale that absence of pouring excludes the foundry subpart and leaves the site subject to the EAF NESHAP (EPA’s additional note about NSPS AAa is informational but the key legal basis is covered)."}

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants for Industrial, Commercial, and Institutional Boilers—Area Sources

criteria.criterion: if you own or operate an industrial, commercial, or institutional boiler that is located at, or is part of, an area source of hazardous air pollutants then the boiler is subject to Subpart JJJJJJ

if the boiler is a gas-fired boiler as defined in this subpart (i.e., burns gaseous fuels not combined with any solid fuels and burns liquid fuel only during periods of gas curtailment, supply interruption, startups, or for periodic testing/maintenance/training not to exceed a combined total of 48 hours per calendar year) then the boiler is not subject to Subpart JJJJJJ

if the boiler is an electric utility steam generating unit (EGU) as defined in this subpart (e.g., a fossil fuel-fired unit of more than 25 megawatts that serves a generator that produces electricity for sale and meets the fossil-fuel firing percentage criteria) then the boiler is not subject to Subpart JJJJJJ
if the boiler is specifically listed as, or included in the definition of, an affected source in another standard(s) under this part then the boiler is not subject to Subpart JJJJJJ

checklist: Confirm whether the facility is an area source of HAP (i.e., not a major source) and document the basis
Confirm the boiler classification (industrial, commercial, or institutional) per §63.11237
Verify each boiler's normal and permitted fuel types and usage patterns (primary fuel, any liquid fuel burn allowances, and whether solid fuels are ever burned)

Quantify and document the actual and permitted hours per calendar year that each boiler burns liquid fuel for testing, maintenance, startups, or during gas curtailment (compare combined hours to the 48-hour limit in the gas-fired boiler definition)

Document whether liquid fuel burning is limited to periods of gas curtailment/supply interruption/startup/periodic testing as defined in §63.11237 and whether those periods meet the definition of 'period of gas curtailment or supply interruption'

Check permits and on-site fuel handling to confirm whether the boilers are 'capable of combusting' fuels that would make them EGUs (e.g., coal or oil handling equipment) and record nameplate electric capacity (MW) and whether electricity is produced for sale
Determine the boilers' electrical output and fossil-fuel firing percentages (3-year average >10% or annual >15% thresholds in the EGU definition) if applicable

Verify that the boilers are not otherwise excluded categories listed in §63.11195 (e.g., hot water heaters, temporary boilers, residential boilers, electric boilers, waste-heat boilers, boilers covered by other subparts) and document supporting evidence

If claiming the gas-fired exemption, retain records demonstrating liquid fuel use hours, instances of gas curtailment (including cause and duration), and any contractual arrangements with fuel suppliers

candidates.title: Subpart DDDDD — Industrial, Commercial, and Institutional Boilers and Process Heaters (Boiler MACT)

criteria.criterion: if you own or operate an industrial, commercial, or institutional boiler or process heater that is located at, or is part of, a major source of HAP then subject

if the boiler or process heater is part of the affected source subject to another subpart of this part (for example boilers/process heaters used as control devices to comply with other subparts) then not subject

if at least 50 percent of the average annual heat input during any 3 consecutive calendar years to the boiler or process heater is provided by regulated gas streams that are subject to another standard then not subject

if the boiler or process heater is one of the types listed in paragraphs (a) through (n) of §63.7491 (e.g., electric utility EGUs, recovery boilers covered by subpart MM, hot water heaters, temporary boilers, blast-furnace-gas-fired units, hazardous-waste-burning units, residential boilers, etc.) then not subject

candidates.title: Subpart JJJJJJ — Area-source/other boilers (exemptions for boilers listed in other standards)

criteria.criterion: if a boiler is specifically listed as, or included in the definition of, an affected source in another standard under this part then not subject to Subpart JJJJJJ
if the boiler is gas-fired as defined in this subpart then not subject to Subpart JJJJJJ

candidates.title: Subpart DDDD — Plywood and Composite Wood Products (PCWP) NESHAP

criteria.criterion: if you own or operate a PCWP manufacturing facility (manufactures plywood and/or composite wood products as defined) and the facility is located at a major source of HAP then this subpart applies to each affected source at that facility

if the affected source includes combustion unit exhaust streams that are routinely used to direct-fire process units (for example dryers) then those combustion unit exhaust streams are included in the affected source covered by this subpart

if the affected source consists of the collection of dryers, refiners, blenders, formers, presses, board coolers, and other process units associated with PCWP manufacturing then those units are part of the affected source

checklist: Confirm whether your facility is a plywood and/or composite wood products (PCWP) manufacturing facility as defined in 40 CFR 63.2231(a) (types of products manufactured).

Confirm whether the PCWP facility is located at a major source of HAP (calculate actual or potential HAP emissions against the 10 t/yr single HAP or 25 t/yr combined HAP thresholds referenced in 40 CFR 63.2231(b)).

Determine whether the rotary gasifiers and the secondary combustion chamber exhaust streams are routed to, or routinely used to direct-fire, the PCWP dryers or other PCWP process units (i.e., are they part of the affected source per 40 CFR 63.2232(b)?).
Verify whether the dryers/process units (and their combustion exhaust) are already claimed as part of the PCWP affected source subject to Subpart DDDD (document routing and control boundaries).

If claiming exclusion from Boiler MACT because the unit is part of another subpart, confirm the unit is in fact part of an affected source regulated by that other subpart (per 40 CFR 63.7491(h) and 40 CFR 63.11195(a)).

If relying on the '50 percent heat input' exclusion, calculate the percent of average annual heat input to the boiler/process heater provided by regulated gas streams subject to another standard over any 3 consecutive calendar years (per 40 CFR 63.7491(i) and 40 CFR 63.11195(g)).
Confirm whether the unit burns hazardous waste or is subject to subpart EEE (hazardous-waste-burning boilers) which would change applicability (see 40 CFR 63.7491(m) and 40 CFR 63.11195(c)).

Confirm whether the unit meets other exclusion categories (electric boilers, hot water heaters, temporary or residential boilers, gas-fired boiler as defined in Subpart JJJJJJ) referenced in 40 CFR 63.7491 and 40 CFR 63.11195 that would make it not subject to the boiler/process heater standards.

Document whether any portion of the gasifier exhaust bypasses the dryers to heat thermal oil and whether that bypassed stream is routed to process units that would or would not be part of the PCWP affected source (to establish whether the entire gasification system is within the PCWP affected source boundaries).

candidates.title: Plywood and Composite Wood Products (PCWP)

criteria.criterion: if you own or operate a PCWP manufacturing facility then this subpart applies to you
if the PCWP manufacturing facility is located at a major source of HAP emissions (any single HAP ≥ 10 tpy or any combination ≥ 25 tpy) then this subpart applies to you
if this subpart applies to your PCWP manufacturing facility then each affected source at the facility is covered and the affected source includes lumber kilns at PCWP manufacturing facilities

if an area source increases its emissions or its potential to emit such that it becomes a major source then you must be in compliance with this subpart by October 1, 2007 or upon initial startup of your affected source as a major source, whichever is later

candidates.title: General Provisions

criteria.criterion: if an area source that previously was a major source becomes a major source again then the source is subject to the applicable major-source requirements under this part immediately upon becoming a major source again, provided the compliance date for the major source requirements has passed
if an area source increases its emissions or its potential to emit such that it becomes a major source then the source is subject to the notification requirements of this subpart

if a stationary source emits or has the potential to emit 10 tons per year or more of any hazardous air pollutant or 25 tons per year or more of any combination of hazardous air pollutants then it is a major source

checklist: Confirm whether your facility is a PCWP manufacturing facility as defined (manufactures plywood and/or composite wood products or includes dry veneer and lumber kilns)
Calculate current actual and projected potential-to-emit (considering federally enforceable limits and controls) for individual HAPs (e.g., methanol) and for combined HAPs in tpy
Determine whether your facility's HAP emissions or potential-to-emit meet or exceed 10 tpy for any single HAP or 25 tpy combined (major source thresholds)
Identify whether the PCWP operations and the lumber kilns are located within a single contiguous area and are under common control
Verify whether any federally enforceable permit limits currently restrict your potential-to-emit (and whether those limits will remain after the production increase)
If reclassification via a revised permit is expected, note the effective date of the reclassification and whether the compliance date(s) for the applicable major-source requirements have passed
Prepare to submit required initial notifications under 40 CFR part 63 (per §63.9) upon becoming a major source and confirm required timing for such notifications
Document whether any affected source construction/startup dates or reconstruction criteria apply to the kilns (see definitions of new/reconstructed/affected source)

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Chemical Manufacturing Area Sources (Subpart VVVVVV)

criteria.criterion: if you own or operate a chemical manufacturing process unit (CMPU) that is located at an area source and Table 1 HAP are present in the CMPU as specified in paragraph (a)(2) then you are subject to this subpart
if the operations are among the exclusions listed in paragraphs (c)(1) through (6) of this section then this subpart does not apply to those operations

if an area source installed a federally-enforceable control device on an affected CMPU and the control device is necessary to maintain the source's emissions at area source levels then the source is required to obtain a permit under 40 CFR part 70 or 40 CFR part 71

candidates.title: General Provisions (Subpart A) — Title V applicability for area source standards

criteria.criterion: if an area-source standard specifies that States will have the option to exclude area sources affected by that standard from the requirement to obtain a Title V permit then area sources affected by that standard are not subject to the Title V permit requirement in States that exercise the option

if an area-source standard specifies that States will have the option to defer permitting of area sources in that category until the Administrator takes rulemaking action to determine applicability of the permitting requirements then area sources may not be required to obtain a Title V permit until such deferral ends

if a standard fails to specify what the permitting requirements will be for area sources affected by such a standard then area sources that are subject to the standard will be subject to the requirement to obtain a Title V permit

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Chemical Preparations Facilities (Subpart BBBBBBB)

criteria.criterion: if you are subject to this subpart then you are exempt from the obligation to obtain a permit under 40 CFR part 70 or 40 CFR part 71, provided you are not otherwise required by law to obtain a permit under 40 CFR 70.3(a) or 71.3(a)

checklist: Determine whether the facility is an area source (potential to emit and actual emissions below major-source thresholds as defined in 40 CFR 63.2).

Identify whether you own or operate one or more CMPUs as defined in 40 CFR 63.11494(b) and 63.11502 (i.e., the collection of process vessels, equipment, storage tanks, transfer operations, surge control vessels, bottoms receivers, and associated recovery devices for NAICS 325 processes).

For each CMPU, verify whether any Table 1 HAP are present at the trigger concentrations in 40 CFR 63.11494(a)(2) (feedstock concentrations from SDS or supplier data; byproduct or product concentrations in process or waste streams; hydrazine/product criteria).
Confirm whether the facility installed a control device that is federally enforceable and is installed on an affected CMPU (document the device and the federally enforceable mechanism).

Determine whether the control device is necessary to maintain the source's emissions at area source levels (i.e., without the device the source's actual emissions or potential to emit would meet or exceed major source thresholds).

Document any existing federally-enforceable limits or permits that limit potential to emit (identify whether limits are in a Title V permit, part 70/71 permit, SIP, FIP, construction permit, or other federally enforceable instrument).

Check whether Subpart VVVVVV (63.11494) or relevant subparts explicitly address Title V applicability for your situation (see 63.11494(e)) and whether Ohio's permitting authority has adopted any option to exclude or defer area-source permitting under this standard.
Verify whether the facility is subject to other subparts (e.g., Subpart BBBBBBB or Subpart CCCCCCC) that contain Title V exemptions or different Title V applicability.
Confirm whether you are otherwise required by law to obtain a Title V permit under 40 CFR 70.3(a) or 40 CFR 71.3(a) irrespective of the area-source standard.

candidates.title: Lead Acid Battery Manufacturing (Subpart PPPPPP)

criteria.criterion: if you own or operate a lead acid battery manufacturing plant or a lead acid battery component manufacturing plant that is an area source of HAP emissions then you are subject to this subpart

if an affected source is a lead acid battery manufacturing plant then the affected source includes all grid casting, paste mixing, three-process operation, lead oxide manufacturing, lead reclamation, and any other lead-emitting operation associated with the plant

if a prior performance test was conducted using the same methods and either no process changes have been made since the test or you can demonstrate the results reliably demonstrate compliance despite process changes then existing sources are not required to conduct an initial performance test

if you elect to group similar affected sources together for subsequent performance testing then the grouped units must be of the same process type and have the same type of air pollution control device

if you plan to conduct subsequent performance tests on representative affected sources then you must prepare and submit a testing plan to the Administrator or delegated authority no later than 90 days prior to the first scheduled performance test and include the lists and schedule specified in paragraph (c)(5)(iii)

if your facility commenced construction or reconstruction after February 23, 2023 then you must comply with the requirements in § 63.11423(a)(2) by initial startup or February 23, 2023, whichever is later

candidates.title: Performance Testing Requirements (Subpart A)

criteria.criterion: if required to do performance testing by a relevant standard and unless a waiver of performance testing is obtained under this section then the owner or operator must perform such tests within 180 days of the compliance date for the source

if you request a waiver of an initial or subsequent performance test and a site-specific test plan is not submitted then the application for the waiver must be submitted at least 60 days before the performance test

if you apply for a waiver of a performance test then your application must include information justifying the waiver such as technical or economic infeasibility or impracticality of performing the required test

if you apply for a waiver of a performance test then the Administrator will approve or deny the request when he/she approves or denies an extension of compliance, approves or disapproves a site-specific test plan, makes a determination of compliance following required reports, or makes a determination of suitable progress towards compliance as applicable

candidates.title: Extension of Compliance and Waivers (Subpart YY)

criteria.criterion: if the owner or operator demonstrates the source is meeting the relevant standards on a continuous basis or the source is operating under an extension of compliance or has requested an extension and the Administrator is considering that request then individual performance tests may be waived upon written application to the Administrator

if an application for a waiver of an initial performance test or a subsequent performance test is made and a site-specific test plan is not submitted then the application shall be submitted at least 60 days before the performance test

if you submit an application for waiver of a performance test then the Administrator will approve or deny the request when he/she approves or denies an extension of compliance, approves or disapproves a site-specific test plan, makes a determination of compliance following submission of required reports, or makes a determination of suitable progress towards compliance

checklist: Confirm whether your facility is a lead acid battery manufacturing plant or a lead acid battery component manufacturing plant area source (per 40 CFR 63.11421(a)).
Determine whether the plant (affected source) is existing or new by the applicable construction/reconstruction date thresholds in 40 CFR 63.11421(b)(1)–(4) and 63.11422.
Identify whether the two new Humidity Curing and Drying Oven Chambers are part of the affected source (i.e., part of the plant operations listed in 63.11421(b)).

Gather records of any prior performance tests for the same ovens or exhaust points: test dates, test methods used, test results, sample times/volumes, and report files (to evaluate applicability of 63.11423(c)(1)).

Verify whether any process changes have occurred since the prior performance test(s) for the same units or whether you can demonstrate the prior test results reliably demonstrate compliance despite process changes (per 40 CFR 63.11423(c)(1)).
Document the control device type for the new ovens (e.g., fabric filter, HEPA, scrubber) and whether it is the same type as on previously tested, similar units (per 40 CFR 63.11423(c)(5)(i)).

If intending to group the new ovens with similar units for representative testing, prepare the testing plan contents required in 40 CFR 63.11423(c)(5)(iii)(A)–(C) and note the 90-day prior submission requirement.
Confirm whether prior waiver(s) of performance testing have been granted for existing units and obtain copies of the waiver letters or Administrator communications.

If you plan to request a waiver, prepare justification showing continuous compliance or technical/economic infeasibility and be ready to submit the waiver application at least 60 days before the scheduled test if no site-specific test plan is submitted (per 40 CFR 63.7(h)(3) and 40 CFR 63.1112(b)(3)).

Collect monitoring and operating records that would demonstrate continuous compliance (e.g., pressure drop records, visible emission observations, prior test records) to support a waiver request under 40 CFR 63.1112(b)(2) and 63.7(h).

Determine whether the Administrator (or delegated authority) approval pathways referenced in 40 CFR 63.7(h)(4) and 40 CFR 63.1112(b)(4) (extension of compliance, site-specific plan approval, compliance status reports) are relevant to your planned waiver request and prepare any accompanying reports.

If the ovens exhaust to fabric filters or scrubbers, verify applicable monitoring/inspection frequencies and requirements in 40 CFR 63.11423(b) and (e) to confirm ongoing compliance documentation available to support a waiver.

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants for Stationary Combustion Turbines (Subpart YYYY)

criteria.criterion: if your stationary combustion turbine is a lean premix gas-fired, lean premix oil-fired, diffusion flame gas-fired, or diffusion flame oil-fired stationary combustion turbine, then you must comply with the emission limitations and operating limitations in Table 1 and Table 2 of this subpart

if your stationary combustion turbine is not equipped with an oxidation catalyst, then you must petition the Administrator for operating limitations that you will monitor to demonstrate compliance with the formaldehyde emission limitation in Table 1 (or alternatively petition for approval of no additional operating limitations)

if you submit a petition under this section for operating limitations, then you must not conduct the initial performance test until after the petition has been approved or disapproved by the Administrator

if you petition the Administrator for operating limitations for a turbine not equipped with an oxidation catalyst, then you must measure the proposed operating parameters during the initial performance test and continuously monitor them thereafter
if you petition for approval of additional operating limitations, then the petition must include identification of the specific parameters you propose to use as additional operating limitations

if you petition for approval of additional operating limitations, then the petition must include a discussion of the relationship between the proposed parameters and HAP emissions, identifying how HAP emissions change with changes in these parameters and how limitations on these parameters will limit HAP emissions

if you petition for approval of additional operating limitations, then the petition must include a discussion of how you will establish the upper and/or lower values for the proposed parameters that will constitute the operating limits

if you petition for approval of additional operating limitations, then the petition must include a discussion identifying the methods and instruments you will use to measure and monitor the proposed parameters and the relative accuracy and precision of those methods and instruments

if you petition for approval of additional operating limitations, then the petition must include a discussion identifying the frequency and methods for recalibrating the instruments you will use for monitoring the proposed parameters

if you are not using an oxidation catalyst, then you must continuously monitor any parameters specified in your approved petition to the Administrator in order to comply with the operating limitations in Table 2 as specified in Table 5 of this subpart

if you are operating a stationary combustion turbine that uses an oxidation catalyst, then you must monitor on a continuous basis your catalyst inlet temperature to comply with the operating limitations in Table 2 and as specified in Table 5
if you must conduct a performance test, then the performance test must be conducted at high load, defined as 100 percent plus or minus 10 percent

if the stationary combustion turbine is operating, then you must conduct all parametric monitoring at all times the turbine is operating except during monitor malfunctions, associated repairs, and required QA/QC activities

checklist: Confirm turbine classification (e.g., lean premix gas-fired) to determine applicability of Table 1 and Table 2 requirements
Confirm whether the turbine is equipped with an oxidation (formaldehyde) catalyst
If no catalyst, decide whether to petition for specific operating limitations (e.g., %Load and inlet air temperature T1) or to petition for approval of no additional operating limitations

If petitioning for operating limitations: prepare to include (a) identification of the proposed parameters (%Load, T1), (b) a technical discussion linking each parameter to formaldehyde/HAP emissions, (c) proposed upper and/or lower limit values, (d) measurement and monitoring methods and instruments with stated accuracy/precision, and (e) calibration/recalibration frequency and methods (per 63.6120(f)(1)-(5))
Do not perform the initial performance test until the petition has been approved or disapproved by the Administrator (per 63.6120(e))

Plan to measure the proposed parameters during the initial performance test conducted at high load (100% ±10%) and to continuously monitor them thereafter if petition is approved (per 63.6120(c) and 63.6120(e))

Confirm that continuous monitoring of the approved parameters can be performed at all times the turbine is operating and that QA/QC, downtime, and data exclusion rules are implemented (per 63.6135(a) and 63.6125(b))
Verify instrumentation availability and capability for continuous measurement of %Load and inlet air temperature (T1), including accuracy, precision, data logging, and recalibration procedures

Check whether the turbine fires landfill gas, digester gas, or gasified MSW at ≥10% of gross heat input annually (fuel-specific monitoring and recording requirements in 63.6125(c)), and whether any distillate oil is used at the major source (63.6125(d))

Determine the compliance date and initial performance test date requirements applicable to your unit (see §63.6095 and §63.6110 for timing) and confirm any previous performance tests that might be usable under §63.6110(b)
