candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Municipal Solid Waste Landfills (Subpart AAAA)

criteria.criterion: if the landfill is a closed landfill (i.e., solid waste is no longer being placed and no additional solid wastes will be placed without first filing a notification of modification) then the removal criterion in §63.1957(b)(1) is met

if the gas collection and control system has been in operation a minimum of 15 years or the owner or operator demonstrates that the gas collection and control system will be unable to operate for 15 years due to declining gas flow then the removal criterion in §63.1957(b)(2) is met

if the calculated NMOC emission rate at the landfill is less than 50 Mg/yr on three successive test dates that are each no less than 90 days apart and no more than 180 days apart, calculated following the procedures in §63.1959(c), then the removal criterion in §63.1957(b)(3) is met
if the landfill meets all of the collection and control system removal criteria in §63.1957(b) then the landfill is no longer required to comply with this subpart

if the landfill has a design capacity equal to or greater than 2.5 million Mg and 2.5 million m3 then the owner or operator must either comply with the collection and control requirements in §63.1959(b)(2) or calculate and report NMOC emissions as specified in §63.1959(b)

checklist: Confirm the landfill status is "closed" per 40 CFR 63.1990 (no additional solid waste will be placed unless a notification of modification under §63.9(b) is filed) and assemble/confirm a closure report to submit per §63.1981(f).

Document the gas collection and control system start-up and continuous operation dates to verify a minimum 15-year operation period, or prepare technical and operational evidence demonstrating the system will be unable to operate for 15 years due to declining gas flow (e.g., performance test reports, decline curves, operational records) as described in §63.1957(b)(2) and §63.1981(g)(1)(ii).

Obtain three successive NMOC emission rate determinations showing <50 Mg/yr, with each test date at least 90 days apart and no more than 180 days apart, and ensure calculations follow §63.1959(c) (measure QLFG at the common header per Method 2E and CNMOC from the common header before gas movers/condensate removal per Method 25 or 25C, converting by dividing by 6); keep full test reports and dates for inclusion in the equipment removal report per §63.1981(g)(1)(iii).

Verify that NMOC sampling locations, sampling methods, and flow measurements meet the procedural requirements in §63.1959(c) (common header location before gas-moving or condensate removal equipment and Method 2E/25/25C specifications).

Confirm whether prior required reports (design capacity report, initial NMOC reports, collection and control system design plan, initial performance test, closure report) have been submitted previously to EPA or state/tribal authorities; if so, note dates and include statements/copies per §63.1981(a),(c),(d),(f),(i).

Prepare an equipment removal report to submit at least 30 days prior to removal/cessation that includes: the closure report (§63.1981(g)(1)(i)), either an initial performance test report demonstrating the 15‑year minimum control period has expired or information demonstrating inability to operate 15 years (§63.1981(g)(1)(ii)), and dated copies or evidence of three successive NMOC emission rate reports (§63.1981(g)(1)(iii)).

Verify design capacity (mass or volume) per the most recent permit or calculated using site-specific density and include map/plot of landfill areas as required in the design capacity report (§63.1981(a)(1)-(2)) to confirm applicability (e.g., your reported ~5.9 million Mg).

Confirm electronic reporting readiness and whether the NMOC and equipment removal reports have been or will be submitted via CEDRI/CDX per §63.1981(l), and gather any previously submitted CDX submission dates to reference in the equipment removal report per §63.1981(g)(1)(iii).

If any alternate methods or site-specific parameters (e.g., site-specific CNMOC or methane generation rate) were used in NMOC calculations, assemble documentation of methods and approvals per §63.1959(a)(3)-(4) and §63.1959(a)(5).

judge_text: {"score":2,"reason":"EPA's note states the landfill is subject to the MSW Landfill NESHAP (i.e., the rule applies). OUR ANSWER explicitly cites Subpart AAAA, includes the design-capacity applicability criterion (≥2.5 million Mg) and checklist step confirming the reported ~5.9 million Mg, so the key reason in the EPA notes is captured."}

candidates.title: Plywood and Composite Wood Products (Subpart DDDD)

criteria.criterion: if equipment is a process unit then you must meet one compliance option for that process unit (either a production-based total HAP option or an add-on control system option) and you cannot combine production-based and add-on control system compliance options for the same process unit

if two pieces of equipment are separate process units then you must meet a compliance option for each process unit (i.e., you cannot aggregate two separate process units into a single process-unit compliance demonstration)

if you operate a reconstituted wood product press (at a new or existing affected source) or a reconstituted wood product board cooler (at a new affected source) then you must either use a wood products enclosure that meets the press enclosure design criteria or measure the capture efficiency of the capture device using Methods 204 and 204A–204F of 40 CFR part 51, appendix M (as appropriate) or the alternative tracer gas method in appendix A to this subpart and submit documentation with your Notification of Compliance Status

if you choose a concentration-based compliance option for a control system outlet (options 2, 4, or 6 in Table 1B) for a reconstituted wood product press (new or existing affected source) or a reconstituted wood product board cooler (new affected source) then the capture device must either meet the definition of wood products enclosure or achieve a capture efficiency greater than or equal to 95 percent

if you elect to demonstrate initial compliance with add-on control system compliance options then you must conduct performance tests and establish each site-specific operating requirement according to the requirements referenced for initial compliance and submit the test results in the Notification of Compliance Status (with specified exemptions for combustion units accepting process exhausts into the flame zone as noted)

checklist: Verify whether each piece of equipment (press and board cooler) meets the Subpart DDDD definitions for 'reconstituted wood product press' and 'reconstituted wood product board cooler' (40 CFR 63.2292).
Verify whether the press and the board cooler are configured and operated as separate 'process units' (boundaries, vents, capture systems) per the 'process unit' definition (40 CFR 63.2292).

Determine for each process unit whether you will use a production-based total HAP compliance option (Table 1A) or an add-on control system compliance option (Table 1B), remembering you must choose one option per process unit and cannot mix within a single process unit (40 CFR 63.2240(a),(b)).

If you plan to use a concentration-based option (options 2, 4, or 6 in Table 1B) for a press or a board cooler, verify whether the capture device is a wood products enclosure that meets all design criteria or, if not, measure/verify capture efficiency and confirm it is ≥95% (40 CFR 63.2240(b); 40 CFR 63.2292).

If relying on a wood products enclosure, confirm the enclosure meets the design criteria (natural draft opening distance, total natural opening area ≤5% of surface area, average facial velocity ≥3,600 m/hr (200 fpm) into the enclosure, access doors/windows closed during routine operation, and designed/maintained to capture all emissions) as specified in 40 CFR 63.2292.

If measuring capture efficiency, plan and document a capture efficiency test using EPA Methods 204 and 204A–204F (part 51, appendix M) or the alternative tracer gas method in appendix A to Subpart DDDD, and prepare to submit the enclosure design documentation or capture test results with the Notification of Compliance Status (40 CFR 63.2267).

If using an add-on control system, plan performance testing and establishment of site-specific operating requirements per the initial compliance requirements and prepare to submit performance test results and operating limits in the Notification of Compliance Status (40 CFR 63.2260(a)).

Verify whether any combustion unit accepts process exhaust into the flame zone (which may be exempt from certain performance testing requirements for thermal oxidizers) so you can determine applicable testing exemptions (40 CFR 63.2260(a)).

Confirm affected source status and relevant construction/reconstruction dates for applicability of specific compliance tables or future compliance deadlines (e.g., new vs existing affected source, dates referenced in 40 CFR 63.2240(d) as applicable).

Prepare Notification of Compliance Status documentation to include chosen compliance options for each process unit, capture device/enclosure documentation or capture efficiency test results, performance test reports (if applicable), and any site-specific operating requirements established.

judge_text: {"score":2,"reason":"The answer explicitly includes the key rationale from the EPA notes: each process unit must meet its own compliance option and you cannot aggregate/combine or sum compliance options across separate process units, citing 40 CFR 63.2240 and 63.2292, which matches the EPA statement that the rule does not allow summing."}

candidates.title: National emission standards for hazardous air pollutants for rubber tire manufacturing

criteria.criterion: if you own or operate a rubber tire manufacturing facility that is located at, or is a part of, a major source of hazardous air pollutant (HAP) emissions then subject

if a stationary source or group of stationary sources within a contiguous area and under common control emits or has the potential to emit any single HAP at a rate of 9.07 megagrams (10 tons) or more per year or any combination of HAP at a rate of 22.68 megagrams (25 tons) or more per year then subject
if your facility's affected source includes tire repair operations that use or process cements and solvents as defined in § 63.6015 then subject
if the materials used in your operations meet the definition of "cements and solvents" in § 63.6015 then subject

if you own or operate a tire cord production affected source but the primary product produced at the affected source is determined to be subject to another subpart under this part as of the effective date of that subpart or startup then not subject

if your rubber tire manufacturing affected source is a research and development facility operated under the close supervision of technically trained personnel and is not engaged in the manufacture of products for commercial sale in commerce except in a de minimis manner then not subject
if you have an existing, new, or reconstructed affected source at a facility engaged in the manufacture of rubber tires or their components then subject

checklist: Determine whether the facility is part of a major source: calculate actual emissions and potential-to-emit (PTE) for each HAP and for combined HAPs (thresholds: ≥10 tpy single HAP or ≥25 tpy combined HAP).
List all processes performed on-site (including retreading/repair, bead work, undertread, painting, cleaning, slab dip, etc.) and identify which processes use or process cements and solvents.

Inventory all materials that could be cements and solvents (as purchased formulations, cleaning solvents, paints, marking inks, green tire spray, slab dip mixtures, process aids) and quantify annual usage for each.
Confirm whether operations include tire repair/retread activities that use cements/solvents (retread operations, tire repair operations, green tire spray, blemish repair paints).

Verify whether the facility manufactures new tires or manufactures components that become integral parts of tires (mixed rubber compound, tread, sidewalls, liners, beads) versus only performing repair/retread services.

If the facility operates tire cord production, determine the primary product over a 5-year period and whether that primary product is subject to another subpart as of the other subpart's effective date or source startup.
Determine whether the affected source is a research and development facility operated under close supervision and whether any product is sold commercially beyond de minimis amounts.
Determine the construction/startup date(s) of affected sources to classify them as existing, new (construction commenced after Oct 18, 2000), or reconstructed per § 63.2.
Aggregate emissions across all stationary sources on the contiguous property under common control when assessing major source status (include emissions controls when calculating PTE).

judge_text: {"score":2,"reason":"EPA's sole key reason — the facilities are not major sources of HAPs — is captured in OUR ANSWER by the major source applicability criteria (40 CFR 63.5981(a) and 63.5981(a)(2)) and the checklist item to determine major source status (calculate actual/PTE against 10 tpy single / 25 tpy combined thresholds)."}

candidates.title: Petroleum Refinery Catalytic Cracking Units

criteria.criterion: If the catalytic cracking unit regenerator does not introduce any other gas streams into the catalyst regeneration vent (i.e., is a complete combustion unit with no additional combustion devices), then you may use the alternative continuous-parameter-based calculation (Equation 1 in §63.1573(a)(1)) to determine the regenerator actual exhaust gas flow rate instead of using Method 2 for Qr.

If you have a gas analyzer installed in the catalytic cracking regenerator exhaust vent prior to the addition of air or other gas streams and you install and operate continuous monitoring of regenerator air flow plus continuous gas analyzers for CO2, CO, and O2, then you may use Equation 2 in §63.1573(a)(2) to calculate the volumetric flow rate Qr instead of measuring Qr by Method 2.

If you use the alternative Qr measurement for the regenerator exhaust, then you may measure upstream or downstream of an electrostatic precipitator but you must measure upstream of a carbon monoxide boiler as required for the alternative procedure.

If you intend to use the alternative procedure only to determine inlet velocity to the primary internal cyclones to demonstrate compliance with §63.1564(c)(5), then you must use that same alternative procedure for the performance test and for monitoring after the performance test.

checklist: Confirm whether the FCCU regenerator introduces any other gas streams into the catalyst regeneration vent (examples: oxygen-enriched air, nitrogen streams, or any additional combustion devices).

If relying on Equation 1 alternative: verify a continuous parameter monitoring system (or control room instrumentation) is installed and operating to measure and record the hourly average volumetric air flow rate to the regenerator.

If relying on Equation 1 alternative: verify a continuous parameter monitoring system (or control room instrumentation) is installed and operating to measure and record the gas temperature near the control device or exiting the regenerator, and whether you will measure or assume vent pressure (Pvent; you may assume Pvent = 1 atm for final atmospheric vent stacks).

If relying on Equation 2 alternative: verify a continuous gas analyzer is installed in the regenerator exhaust vent prior to addition of air/gas streams and upstream of any CO boiler, and that it measures and records CO2, CO, and O2 concentrations.

If using the alternative and you have an electrostatic precipitator, decide and document whether measurements will be taken upstream or downstream of the ESP (allowed either way) and ensure measurements are upstream of any CO boiler.

Determine whether you are electing Option 1b or Option 2 under 40 CFR 63.1564(a)(1) (NSPS coke burn-off or PM per coke burn-off) or another compliance option that requires calculating Qr for PM per coke burn calculations.

If you plan to use the alternative only to compute inlet velocity to primary internal cyclones per §63.1564(c)(5), confirm you will use the same alternative procedure for the performance test and for subsequent monitoring.

Verify that continuous monitoring systems (CEMS, CPMS, or continuous gas analyzers) will be installed, operated, and maintained consistent with the requirements in §63.1572 (installation, operation, maintenance, data completeness, and averaging requirements).
Assemble supporting calculations and control-room/instrumentation records showing Qa, Qoxy (if applicable), Tempgas, %CO2, %CO, %O2, and Pvent as required by the selected alternative procedure.

judge_text: {"score":2,"reason":"EPA’s key point—that the NESHAP alternative equations for coke burn-off and regenerator exhaust flow are acceptable under the cited regulations—is reflected in the candidate criteria and checklist (limits on added gas streams, requirement for analyzers upstream of added streams/CO boiler, ESP measurement options, and linkage to §63.1564 compliance), so the key reasons in the EPA notes are captured."}

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants for Petroleum Refineries (Refinery MACT)

criteria.criterion: if a plant site is a major source as defined in section 112(a) of the Clean Air Act and has petroleum refining process units that contain or contact one or more HAP listed in table 1 of this subpart then subpart CC applies to those petroleum refining process units and the related emission points listed in § 63.640(c)

if a wastewater stream at a petroleum refinery has a total annual benzene loading of 10 megagrams per year or greater, a flow rate of 0.02 liters per minute or greater, a benzene concentration of 10 parts per million by weight or greater, and is not exempt from control requirements under 40 CFR part 61 subpart FF then the stream is a Group 1 wastewater stream under this subpart

if a Group 1 wastewater stream is managed in a piece of equipment that is also subject to the provisions of 40 CFR part 60 subpart QQQ after the compliance dates specified in § 63.640(h) then that Group 1 wastewater stream is required to comply only with subpart CC

if a flare is used as a control device for a Group 1 wastewater stream then on and after January 30, 2019 the flare must meet the requirements of § 63.670 (and prior to that date must meet the applicable requirements of part 61 subpart FF or § 63.670) when the wastewater provisions apply

candidates.title: 40 CFR part 60, subpart QQQ (NSPS) — (as referenced in Subpart CC)

criteria.criterion: if a wastewater stream is a Group 1 wastewater stream and is managed in equipment that is also subject to 40 CFR part 60 subpart QQQ after the compliance dates specified in § 63.640(h) then the wastewater stream is not subject to subpart QQQ and is required to comply only with subpart CC

candidates.title: 40 CFR part 61, subpart FF (Benzene Waste Operations NESHAP) — (as referenced in Subpart CC)

criteria.criterion: if a wastewater stream is exempt from control requirements under 40 CFR part 61 subpart FF then that stream is not a Group 1 wastewater stream under this subpart

if an owner or operator is required under subpart FF to perform periodic measurement of benzene concentration in wastewater or to monitor process or control device operating parameters then they must operate the process, treatment unit, or control device consistent with minimum or maximum permitted concentration or operating parameter values as specified in this subpart

if an owner or operator is subject to the wastewater provisions in § 63.647 then they must comply with the recordkeeping and reporting provisions in §§ 61.356 and 61.357 of 40 CFR part 61 subpart FF unless they are complying with the wastewater provisions specified in § 63.640(o)(2)(ii)

checklist: Verify whether your plant site is a major source as defined in Clean Air Act section 112(a).
Confirm that the affected unit(s) are petroleum refining process units as defined in § 63.641.
Calculate the wastewater stream's total annual benzene loading per 40 CFR 61.342 to determine if it is ≥ 10 megagrams/year.
Measure or verify the wastewater stream flow rate to confirm it is ≥ 0.02 liters per minute.
Verify the wastewater stream benzene concentration to confirm it is ≥ 10 parts per million by weight.
Determine whether the wastewater stream is exempt from control requirements under 40 CFR part 61 subpart FF.
Identify the specific equipment (treatment unit, conveyance, storage, etc.) that manages the wastewater stream and whether that equipment is also subject to 40 CFR part 60 subpart QQQ.
Check the applicable compliance dates in § 63.640(h) (Table 11) to know whether the overlap/only-this-subpart provision is in effect for your stream and equipment.

If you plan to control the stream under 40 CFR part 61 subpart FF, confirm you are performing any periodic benzene measurements and control-parameter monitoring required by subpart FF and § 63.647(d).
If a flare will be used as the control device, confirm the flare meets the applicable requirements of § 63.670 on/after January 30, 2019 (or the pre-2019 referenced requirements prior to that date).
Determine which subpart's recordkeeping and reporting you will follow (see § 63.655(a) and § 63.640(o)(2)(ii)) depending on the compliance path elected.

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Chemical Recovery Combustion Sources (Subpart MM)

criteria.criterion: If the November 2003 particulate (PM) tests used the PM test methods and procedural requirements specified in this subpart (e.g., Method 5 or 29, or Method 17 with the required adjustment, the specified minimum sampling time and volume, use of water as cleanup solvent, and the required traverse/flow/oxygen/moisture methods), then those tests satisfy the subpart's required test methods and procedures for performance testing.

If the November 2003 tests were conducted during representative normal operating conditions (excluding startup, shutdown, and malfunctions) and process information was recorded to document that the conditions represent normal operation, then those tests meet the subpart's representativeness and documentation requirements for performance testing.

If the November 2003 tests were completed before the Subpart MM compliance date of March 13, 2004, then they occurred prior to the compliance deadline and therefore predate the compliance date referenced for existing affected sources in this subpart.

If the owner/operator certifies that all control techniques and processes have not been modified since the November 2003 testing and the test data were obtained using the test methods and procedures required in this subpart, then those previous performance test data may be used to establish operating limits or be relied upon under the subpart's provisions for using previous performance test data.

checklist: Confirm the exact date(s) of the November 2003 PM tests and compare to the Subpart MM compliance date (March 13, 2004). (40 CFR 63.863(a))
Identify which PM test method was used (Method 5, Method 29, or Method 17) and whether Method 17 results had 0.009 g/dscm added and stack temperature was ≤205 °C (400 °F). (40 CFR 63.865(b)(1))
Verify sample time and sample volume for each run were at least 60 minutes and 0.90 dscm (31.8 dscf). (40 CFR 63.865(b)(1))
Verify the cleanup solvent used in the sample recovery procedure (water required instead of acetone where specified). (40 CFR 63.865(b)(1))

Verify that traverse location/number and gas velocity/flow measurement methods followed Method 1 (or 1A) and Methods 2/2A/2C/2D/2F/2G as applicable, and that oxygen measurement used Method 3/3A/3B (or ANSI/ASME alternative). (40 CFR 63.865(b)(5)(i)-(iii))

Confirm oxygen concentration measurements and that PM and volumetric flow were corrected to the appropriate oxygen concentration (e.g., 8% for recovery furnaces) using the correction equations required in the subpart. (40 CFR 63.865(b)(2)-(4))

Confirm that process data necessary to determine black liquor solids firing rate (BLS), volumetric gas flow rates, and CaO production rate (where applicable) were measured and recorded during the test. (40 CFR 63.865(b)(6))

Document that the tests were conducted during representative normal operating conditions (not during startup, shutdown, or malfunction) and retain the explanation/records that demonstrate representativeness. (40 CFR 63.865(b))
Determine whether the test data were used previously to establish monitoring operating limits; if so, obtain the certification or records used to set those limits. (40 CFR 63.864(j)(2))

Verify whether any physical or operational modifications to the air pollution control device(s) or processes have occurred since November 2003; if relying on 2003 data to set limits, prepare to certify that no such modifications occurred. (40 CFR 63.864(j)(2))

If using the alternative overall PM limit approach (establishing per-unit limits and calculating an overall PM emission rate), verify that volumetric flow and firing-rate data were measured for all recovery furnaces, SDTs, and lime kilns as required to apply the equations in §63.865(a)(1)-(2). (40 CFR 63.865(a)(1)-(2))

Retain all performance test records and be prepared to make them available to the Administrator upon request, including process data, method run sheets, and documentation that tests met required procedures. (40 CFR 63.865(b))

(40 CFR 63.865(b)(6))","Document that the tests were conducted during representative normal operating conditions (not during startup, shutdown, or malfunction) and retain the explanation/records that demonstrate representativeness. candidates.title: Portland Cement Manufacturing NESHAP (Subpart LLL)

criteria.criterion: If the emissions stream includes clinker cooler exhaust (including clinker cooler gases commingled with kiln exhaust in a common stack) at a facility that is a major source subject to Subpart LLL then those emissions are subject to an opacity limit of 10 percent.

If an affected source is subject to the opacity limitation under § 63.1345 then compliance must be demonstrated using Method 9 and the maximum 6-minute average opacity exhibited during the performance test period determines compliance and the typical Method 9 test duration is 3 hours unless the reduced-duration conditions apply.

If the exhaust streams of a kiln with an in-line raw mill and a clinker cooler are comingled then the commingled exhaust stream must be tested with the raw mill on and with the raw mill off for the applicable performance tests.

checklist: Confirm whether your facility is a 'major source' subject to Subpart LLL.
Confirm whether the clinker cooler exhaust is commingled with kiln exhaust in a common stack (document the physical ducting/stack configuration).

Determine whether the clinker cooler gases pass through the in-line kiln/raw mill or bypass it, and quantify the fraction or volumetric flow rates (e.g., verify the stated ~20% bypass and measure Qc and Qk if needed).
Verify whether the kiln has an in-line raw mill (and the operating fraction of mill-on vs mill-off time used for weighted calculations).
Confirm whether the commingled exhaust is routed to a single PM control device/stack (i.e., combined to a single emission point).
If subject to §63.1345 opacity limits, prepare to conduct Method 9 performance testing and use the maximum 6-minute average opacity during the test to assess compliance.
If commingled and the kiln has an in-line raw mill, plan to perform performance testing with the raw mill on and with the raw mill off as required.

Document and retain records of Method 22/Method 9 visible emissions testing frequency and results and be prepared to initiate corrective actions within one hour if visible emissions exceed the applicable limit as required by the monitoring provisions.

candidates.title: Surface Coating of Miscellaneous Metal Parts and Products

criteria.criterion: If a coating contains heat-activated polymer systems in either solvent or water that, when applied to metal substrates, dry to a non-tacky surface and react chemically with rubber and metal during a vulcanization process, then the coating operation is in the rubber-to-metal coatings subcategory.

If a surface coating operation does not meet the definition of rubber-to-metal coating, high performance coating, magnet wire coating, or extreme performance fluoropolymer coating, then the coating operation is in the general use coating subcategory.

If the facility uses 946 liters (250 gallons) per year or more of coatings that contain hazardous air pollutants (HAP) in the surface coating of miscellaneous metal parts and products and the facility is a major source (or located at or part of a major source of HAP), then the facility is subject to this subpart.
If the surface coating or coating operation meets any of the exclusion criteria listed in paragraphs (c)(1) through (c)(17) of §63.3881, then that coating or operation is not subject to this subpart.

If a coating operation is classified in the rubber-to-metal subcategory then the applicable emission limits for new and existing sources are those specified for rubber-to-metal coatings in §63.3890(a)(4) and §63.3890(b)(4), respectively.

If the activity is the application of a coating to a substrate by methods such as spray guns or dip tanks (including associated surface preparation, cleaning, mixing, and storage directly related to application), then the activity is considered surface coating under this subpart.

checklist: Does the coating formulation contain heat-activated polymer systems (solvent- or waterborne)?
Does the coating, when applied to metal, dry to a non-tacky surface?

Does the bonding/heating step involve vulcanization of rubber and a chemical reaction between the coating, rubber, and metal (i.e., rubber vulcanization), or does the heating/bonding occur without rubber vulcanization?
What application method is used (spray, dip, brush, adhesive bonding, etc.) and is it considered surface coating per §63.3881(a)(1)?
Does the coating otherwise meet definitions for high performance, magnet wire, or extreme performance fluoropolymer coatings in §63.3981?
Annual volume of HAP-containing coatings, thinners, and additives used for this operation (liters per year) and whether non-HAP coatings are excluded from that volume calculation; is this ≥946 L/yr?
Is the facility a major source of HAP (potential to emit ≥9.07 Mg/yr (10 tpy) of any single HAP or ≥22.68 Mg/yr (25 tpy) of combined HAP)?
Do any of the exclusions in §63.3881(c)(1)-(17) apply (e.g., uses only non-HAP coatings, volumes below thresholds, subject to another surface coating NESHAP listed in the exclusions)?
If classified as rubber-to-metal or general-use, determine the applicable emission limit to apply from §63.3890 and which compliance demonstration method (§63.3951, §63.3961) you will use.

candidates.title: Wool Fiberglass Manufacturing (Subpart NNN)

criteria.criterion: if the wool fiberglass manufacturing facility is a major source then the requirements of this subpart apply to the owner or operator
if the owner or operator demonstrates to the Administrator that the facility is not a major source then the requirements of this subpart do not apply
if a rotary spin wool fiberglass manufacturing line produces a bonded wool fiberglass building insulation product then the requirements of this subpart apply to emissions from that line
if a flame attenuation wool fiberglass manufacturing line produces a bonded product then the requirements of this subpart apply to emissions from that line
if there is a new or existing glass-melting furnace located at a wool fiberglass manufacturing facility then the requirements of this subpart apply to emissions from that furnace
if a product has a loss on ignition of less than 8 percent and a density of less than 32 kilograms per cubic meter then it is a "building insulation" product as defined in this subpart
if wool fiberglass has been bonded with a phenol-formaldehyde binder then it meets the subpart's definition of "bonded" wool fiberglass
if you determine product LOI for applicability or classification then you must use the method contained in appendix A of this subpart as required by this subpart
if you determine product density for applicability or classification then you must use the method contained in appendix C of this subpart as required by this subpart
if the insulation fibers are made from glass produced or melted at the same facility then they meet the subpart's definition of "wool fiberglass"

checklist: Determine whether the facility is a "major source" as defined in 40 CFR 63.2 (documented and current).
If claiming non-major status, verify and document demonstration to the Administrator that the facility is not a major source (per 40 CFR 63.1380(c)).
Identify each manufacturing line and its process type (rotary spin vs. flame attenuation).
For each line, determine whether the product is "bonded" (phenol-formaldehyde binder applied).
For each product, measure loss on ignition (LOI) using the method in appendix A (per 40 CFR 63.1385(a)(7)) and record percent LOI.
For each product, measure density using the method in appendix C (per 40 CFR 63.1385(a)(9)) and record density in kg/m3.
Verify whether any rotary spin line produces a bonded product that meets the "building insulation" LOI (<8%) and density (<32 kg/m3) criteria.
Verify whether any flame attenuation line produces bonded products (regardless of building-insulation test) subject to the subpart.
Inventory any new or existing glass-melting furnace(s) at the manufacturing facility and document emissions points.
Confirm whether the glass fibers are made from glass produced or melted at the same facility (to meet the "wool fiberglass" definition).

If classifying lines as aerospace, HVAC, OEM, pipe, or heavy-density products for other provisions, determine the percent of the line's annual operating hours devoted to that product type (75% threshold per definitions).

candidates.title: Polyether Polyol Manufacturing (Subpart PPP)

criteria.criterion: if a process unit manufactures a polyether polyol as its primary product and the plant site is a major source then that process unit shall be designated as a polyether polyol manufacturing process unit (PMPU) and be part of an affected source subject to this subpart

if a PMPU does not use or manufacture any organic HAP during the production of one or more products then that PMPU is not subject to any provisions of this subpart except that the owner or operator must retain documentation of the basis for that determination and must demonstrate it when requested by the Administrator

if an organic HAP is used or manufactured in the production of polyether polyols but no organic HAP is used in the production of non-polyether polyol products then the PMPU is not subject to any provision of this subpart during the production of those non-polyether polyol products other than the documentation and demonstration requirements in paragraph (b)(1)

if a process vent is in a PMPU that uses tetrahydrofuran (THF) to produce one or more polyether polyol products and is part of an affected source then the owner or operator shall comply with the HON process vent requirements in §§ 63.113 through 63.118 as modified by the provisions of § 63.1425(f)
if epoxides are used in the production of polyether polyols then the owner or operator shall comply with the epoxide-specific process vent control requirements in § 63.1425(b)

if a process vent uses a combustion, recovery, or recapture device to comply with the process vent control requirements in § 63.1425 then the owner or operator shall install, calibrate, maintain, and operate the monitoring equipment specified in § 63.1429(a) appropriate to the device

if the owner or operator designates a process vent that would otherwise be subject to paragraphs (b), (c), or (d) of § 63.1425 as a maintenance vent then that vent is subject only to the maintenance vent provisions in § 63.1425(h) and the associated recordkeeping and reporting requirements

checklist: Is the plant site a major source (i.e., meets the major source threshold used by your permitting authority)?
For the process unit in question: identify the primary product using § 63.1420(e) rules (is the primary product a polyether polyol?).
List all raw materials, reagents, catalysts, and solvents purchased for and introduced into the polymerization step (purchase records, MSDS/SDS).
Confirm whether tetrahydrofuran (THF) is used to produce polyether polyol products in the process unit (yes/no and mass rates).

Determine whether any organic HAP (per table 4 of this subpart / HON definitions) are knowingly used or produced in the process (beyond impurities); if uncertain, quantify concentrations in process streams or reactor liquid.

If you claim the PMPU does not use or manufacture any organic HAP, assemble and retain supporting documentation (chemical purchase records, process stream analyses, engineering calculations, process knowledge) per § 63.1420(b)(1)(i).

If organic HAP are present, identify all process vents, storage vessels, equipment leaks, heat exchangers, and wastewater streams that are associated with the PMPU (per § 63.1420(a)(4) and definitions in § 63.1423).

For each process vent: determine whether epoxides are used; measure or estimate vent flow rates, organic HAP concentrations, and annual HAP mass emissions to classify Group 1 vs Group 2 and to evaluate TRE where applicable (see § 63.1423 definitions referenced in § 63.1425).

For process vents where THF is used: identify whether any combustion, recovery, or recapture device will be used and whether HON process-vent parameters and monitoring (e.g., Method 18/25A, applicable monitoring devices) are feasible (see § 63.1425(f) and § 63.1429(a)).

If using control devices (flare, incinerator, absorber, condenser, carbon adsorber, boiler/process heater), confirm the specific monitoring equipment required and plan for installation/calibration/recording as described in § 63.1429(a).

If you plan to claim maintenance-vent status for any vent, document the limited conditions of use (start-up, shutdown, maintenance, inspection), and confirm ability to meet the testing/pressure/LEL/VOC-mass criteria in § 63.1425(h)(1)–(3).

If the process uses no catalyst and you believe no HAP are used or made during the polymerization step, confirm via process stream analysis or material balances that unreacted reagents or byproducts do not constitute organic HAP above the 'impurity only' threshold used in § 63.1420(b).
Retain all records, calculations, monitoring data, and notifications required by §§ 63.1438–63.1439 if the PMPU is determined to be part of an affected source (see § 63.1424 cross-references).

judge_text: {"score":2,"reason":"Both key EPA points are reflected: the answer identifies THF-specific process-vent obligations (cites §63.1425(f) and treats THF vents as subject to HON requirements) and separately treats epoxide-specific provisions, implicitly distinguishing epoxide polymerization from THF; it also requires assembling the §63.1420(b)(1) no‑HAP documentation and verification steps (and notes EPA may reject insufficient demonstrations). Thus the EPA Notes’ two reasons are captured."}

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants for Paper and Other Web Coating

criteria.criterion: if the facility is a major source of HAP and web coating lines are operated at the facility then subject

if the operation includes a web coating line (one or more work stations applying a continuous layer of liquid or semi-liquid coating material between an unwind or feed station and a rewind or cutting station) then subject
if any web coating line is stand-alone equipment under subpart KK of this part which the owner or operator includes in the affected source under subpart KK then not subject
if any web coating line is a product and packaging rotogravure or wide-web flexographic press under subpart KK of this part which is included in the affected source under subpart KK then not subject
if the web coating consists of lithography, screenprinting, letterpress, or narrow-web flexographic printing processes then not subject
if any web coating line is subject to subpart EE (Magnetic Tape Manufacturing Operations) then not subject
if any web coating line is subject to subpart SSSS (Surface Coating of Metal Coil) then not subject
if any web coating line is subject to subpart OOOO (Printing, Coating, and Dyeing of Fabrics and Other Textiles) then not subject
if any web coating line is defined as research or laboratory equipment then not subject
if a web coating line coats both paper (or another web) and another substrate and 90 percent or more of the mass of substrate coated during the compliance period is paper then subject

if a web coating line with product and packaging rotogravure and/or wide-web flexographic print station(s) is subject to this subpart and the mass of the materials applied to the line's print station(s) in a month ever exceeds 5 percent of the total mass of materials applied onto the line during the same period then subject (owner may elect to remain subject to this subpart in lieu of subpart KK)

if all of the subject web coating lines at the facility utilize non-HAP coatings and the owner submits the one-time report required in § 63.3370(s) then not subject (to the reporting requirements of this subpart)

checklist: Determine whether the facility is a major source of HAP (per applicability definitions in 40 CFR part 63/§63.2).

Confirm whether your equipment meets the definition of a web coating line: work station(s) applying a continuous layer of liquid or semi-liquid coating material between an unwind/feed station and a rewind/cutting station.

For each web coating line, list the substrates coated and calculate the mass fraction of each substrate type over a representative period (at least one year or another reasonable period) to determine if paper constitutes ≥90% of the mass coated.

For each web coating line, verify whether it is covered instead by another subpart: stand-alone under subpart KK; product/packaging rotogravure or wide-web flexographic press under subpart KK; lithography, screenprinting, letterpress, or narrow-web flexographic printing; subject to subpart EE, SSSS, or OOOO; or classified as research/laboratory equipment.

If any lines include printing stations, check monthly whether the mass of materials applied to the print station(s) ever exceeds 5% of the total mass applied to that line in the same month (for the election in §63.3300(i)).
Verify whether all coatings used on subject web coating lines contain no organic HAP; if so, prepare the one-time report required in §63.3370(s) to claim exemption from reporting requirements.
Determine for each affected source whether it is an existing or new affected source based on construction/reconstruction date (existing if commenced on or before September 13, 2000).

If planning to use control devices (e.g., oxidizer), document planned control approach and ability to meet emission control options in §63.3320(b) (e.g., oxidizer outlet ≤20 ppmv and capture efficiency = 100%, or monthly percent limits), and classify each work station as never-, intermittently-, or always-controlled per definitions.

Gather records and calculation methods you will use to demonstrate 'applied' HAP, coating material mass, and coating solids mass for monthly compliance demonstration per the emission-standard options.

candidates.title: Wood furniture manufacturing (Subpart JJ)

criteria.criterion: if a facility is engaged, either in part or in whole, in the manufacture of wood furniture or wood furniture components and is located at a plant site that is a major source of hazardous air pollutants then the affected source is subject to Subpart JJ

if the owner or operator uses no more than 250 gallons per month, for every month, of coating, gluing, cleaning, and washoff materials at the plant site (including materials used for source categories other than wood furniture) then the source is an area source for purposes of this subpart and is not subject to any other provision of this subpart

if the owner or operator uses no more than 3,000 gallons per rolling 12-month period of coating, gluing, cleaning, and washoff materials at the plant site (including materials used for source categories other than wood furniture) then the source is an area source for purposes of this subpart and is not subject to any other provision of this subpart

if the source emits no more than 4.5 Mg of any one HAP per rolling 12-month period and no more than 11.4 Mg of any combination of HAP per rolling 12-month period and at least 90 percent of plantwide emissions per rolling 12-month period are associated with the manufacture of wood furniture or wood furniture components then the source is an area source for purposes of this subpart and is not subject to other provisions

if the surface coating is of metal parts and products other than metal components of wood furniture and that coating meets the applicability criteria for miscellaneous metal parts and products surface coating (subpart MMMM) then that surface coating operation is not subject to Subpart JJ
if the surface coating is of metal furniture and meets the applicability criteria for metal furniture surface coating (subpart RRRR) then that surface coating operation is not subject to Subpart JJ
if the surface coating is of metal components of wood furniture performed at a wood furniture or wood furniture component manufacturing facility then that coating is subject to Subpart JJ

candidates.title: Metal furniture surface coating (Subpart RRRR)

criteria.criterion: if the activity is surface coating of metal furniture (as defined) and you own or operate a new, reconstructed, or existing affected source in that source category that is a major source, is located at a major source, or is part of a major source of HAP then you are subject to Subpart RRRR
if the surface coating conducted at an affected source uses only coatings, thinners, and cleaning materials that contain no organic HAP then that surface coating is not subject to Subpart RRRR

if the surface coating of metal components of wood furniture is conducted in an operation that is subject to the wood furniture manufacturing NESHAP (Subpart JJ) then that surface coating is not subject to Subpart RRRR
if the surface coating is conducted at research or laboratory facilities or is part of janitorial, building, and facility maintenance operations then it is not subject to Subpart RRRR

if the surface coating is conducted for the purpose of repairing or maintaining metal furniture used by a major source and not for commerce then it is not subject to Subpart RRRR unless organic HAP emissions from the surface coating itself are as high as the major-source rates specified in paragraph (b) of this section

if coating operations, storage containers and mixing vessels, conveying equipment and piping, and waste-handling containers and equipment are used for surface coating of metal furniture as listed in §63.4882(b) then those items are part of the affected source for Subpart RRRR

if an activity falls within the definitions of coating, coating operation, or coating solids in §63.4981 then that activity is subject to the terms of Subpart RRRR unless an exclusion in §63.4881(c) applies

checklist: Determine whether the plant site is a major source of HAP (calculate actual and potential to emit against major-source thresholds used by these subparts).
Determine whether the facility is engaged in the manufacture of wood furniture or wood furniture components (even in part).
Determine whether the metal refinishing/coating work is applied to metal components of wood furniture versus metal parts/products that are not wood-furniture components.
Record total gallons of coating, gluing, cleaning, and washoff materials used at the plant site for each calendar month (to evaluate the 250 gallons/month criterion).
Calculate total gallons of coating, gluing, cleaning, and washoff materials used over the most recent rolling 12-month period (to evaluate the 3,000 gallons/rolling-12-month criterion).

Determine rolling 12-month emissions of each single HAP and of combined HAP to compare with 4.5 Mg (5 ton) single-HAP and 11.4 Mg (12.5 ton) combined-HAP thresholds and determine percent of plantwide emissions associated with wood furniture operations (90% test in §63.800(b)(3)).
Document whether the coatings, thinners, and cleaning materials used for the metal work contain organic HAP (to check the no-organic-HAP exclusion in §63.4881(c)(1)).

Determine whether the metal coating activity is performed as repair or maintenance of metal furniture used only by the facility and not for commerce (to evaluate the repair/maintenance exclusion in §63.4881(c)(5)).

Determine whether the metal coating operations meet the definitions of 'metal furniture' and 'surface coating' in §63.4881(a) and §63.4981 (i.e., are the items being coated considered metal furniture or metal furniture components?).
Determine whether the metal coating operations and associated storage/mixing/conveying/waste handling are co-located and part of the affected source as described in §63.4882(b).

If relying on an area-source exclusion under Subpart JJ, assemble records to demonstrate that finishing materials, adhesives, cleaning solvents and washoff solvents used for wood furniture operations account for at least 90% of annual HAP emissions (as required by §63.800(b)).
Track monthly and annual usage specifically for the metal refinishing/coating work (the reported ~250 gal/year must be compared to monthly and rolling-12-month thresholds in the rules).

candidates.title: Printing, coating, slashing, dyeing, and finishing of fabric and other textiles (Subpart OOOO)

criteria.criterion: if you perform coating, printing, slashing, dyeing, or finishing of fabric or other textiles then your operations fall within the source category to which this subpart applies and may be subject to this subpart

if you own or operate a new, reconstructed, or existing affected source that is a major source, is located at a major source, or is part of a major source of hazardous air pollutants then the affected source is subject to this subpart
if your coating, printing, slashing, dyeing, or finishing operations use only regulated materials that contain no organic HAP then those operations are not subject to this subpart

if the coating, printing, slashing, dyeing, or finishing is conducted at research or laboratory operations or is part of janitorial, building, and facility maintenance operations then those operations are not subject to this subpart

if the coating, printing, slashing, dyeing, or finishing is used by a facility and not for commerce then those operations are not subject to this subpart unless organic HAP emissions from those operations are as high as the major source thresholds

if fabric and other textile substrate web coating or printing operations are conducted at ambient temperatures and do not involve drying or curing equipment such as ovens, tenter frames, steam cans, or dryers then those web coating/printing operations are not subject to this subpart

if a web coating operation at your facility is part of an affected source that is regulated under subpart JJJJ, subpart XXXX, or subpart KK, or if it is at a synthetic fiber manufacturing facility where the fibers are the final product, then that web coating operation is not part of the affected source for this subpart

if a web coating line coats both fabric/other textiles and another substrate then the subpart that applies is determined by the predominant activity (90 percent of the mass of substrate coated during the compliance period) and the web coating line must comply with the subpart for that predominant activity

checklist: Determine whether the operation is a coating, printing, slashing, dyeing, or finishing operation as defined in 40 CFR 63.4371 (e.g., does the application form a continuous solid film (coating) or impregnate fibers (finishing)?).
Confirm whether the substrate is a 'fabric' or 'textile' under 40 CFR 63.4371 (note that "fabric"/"textile" definitions include thread).
Verify whether the materials applied (as purchased) contain any organic HAP and whether they meet the 'no organic HAP' thresholds in 40 CFR 63.4371.
Verify whether the operation uses drying or curing equipment (ovens, tenter frames, steam cans, dryers) or is conducted at ambient temperature without such equipment.
Determine whether the operation is conducted for commerce or only for in-house/noncommercial purposes.
Determine whether the operation is conducted as research/laboratory work or as janitorial/building/facility maintenance.
Determine whether the facility is a major source of HAPs, is located at a major source, or is part of a major source (40 CFR 63.2 definitions for major source).
Check whether the web coating line also coats non-textile substrates and, if so, calculate the mass percent of each substrate to determine the predominant activity (90% rule).
Check whether the web coating operation is regulated under other NESHAPs referenced (subpart JJJJ, XXXX, or KK) or is at a synthetic fiber manufacturing facility where fibers are the final product.

Confirm whether any application or cleaning materials are applied using handheld, non-refillable aerosol containers or touch-up markers (those uses may be excluded from being a coating/printing/dyeing operation under definitions).

candidates.title: Applicability and designation of source

criteria.criterion: if an individual batch vapor, in-line vapor, in-line cold, or batch cold solvent cleaning machine uses any solvent containing methylene chloride, perchloroethylene, trichloroethylene, 1,1,1-trichloroethane, carbon tetrachloride, or chloroform at a total concentration greater than 5 percent by weight as a cleaning and/or drying agent then the provisions of this subpart apply to that individual solvent cleaning machine

candidates.title: Batch vapor and in-line cleaning machine standards

criteria.criterion: if a solvent cleaning machine is a batch vapor or in-line solvent cleaning machine (and the owner/operator does not elect the alternative standards of §63.464) then the owner/operator must ensure the machine conforms to the design requirements specified in §63.463(a)(1) through (7)

if a batch vapor cleaning machine has a solvent/air interface area less than or equal to 1.21 square meters then the owner/operator must either employ one of the control combinations listed in table 1 or demonstrate an idling emission limit of 0.22 kilograms per hour per square meter as specified in §63.463(b)(1)

if a batch vapor cleaning machine has a solvent/air interface area greater than 1.21 square meters then the owner/operator must either employ one of the control combinations listed in table 2 or demonstrate an idling emission limit of 0.22 kilograms per hour per square meter as specified in §63.463(b)(2)

if an in-line cleaning machine is an existing unit then the owner/operator must either employ one of the control combinations listed in table 3 or demonstrate and maintain an idling emission limit of 0.10 kilograms per hour per square meter as specified in §63.463(c)(1)

if an in-line cleaning machine is a new unit then the owner/operator must either employ one of the control combinations listed in table 4 or demonstrate and maintain an idling emission limit of 0.10 kilograms per hour per square meter as specified in §63.463(c)(2)

candidates.title: Alternative standards

criteria.criterion: if the owner or operator elects to comply with §63.464 as an alternative to §63.463 for a batch vapor or in-line solvent cleaning machine that has a solvent/air interface then the owner or operator must maintain a log of solvent additions and deletions and ensure emissions from each machine are equal to or less than the applicable emission limit in table 5 as determined using the procedures in §63.465

if the owner or operator elects to comply with §63.464 as an alternative for a batch vapor cleaning machine that does not have a solvent/air interface then the owner or operator must maintain a log of solvent additions and deletions and ensure emissions meet the applicable limits in table 6 or equation 1 based on the machine cleaning capacity as specified in §63.464(a)(2)

checklist: Determine whether each machine uses any of the listed halogenated HAPs (methylene chloride, perchloroethylene, trichloroethylene, 1,1,1‑trichloroethane, carbon tetrachloride, chloroform) and whether the total concentration of those HAPs in the solvent is greater than 5% by weight.

Determine whether each device meets the definition of a solvent cleaning machine (i.e., uses halogenated HAP liquid or vapor to remove soils) and classify each machine type (batch vapor, batch cold immersion, remote‑reservoir cold, in‑line vapor, continuous web, remote reservoir continuous web, etc.).

Determine whether each machine has a solvent/air interface (for vapor machines: the midline of the primary condenser; for cold machines: the liquid solvent surface) or is constructed/operated without a solvent/air interface.

If the machine has no solvent/air interface, measure and record the cleaning capacity (volume of the cleaning chamber) in cubic meters and compare to table 6 / equation 1 thresholds (notably whether ≤2.95 m3 or >2.95 m3).

For cold/immersion machines, determine whether they are immersion batch or remote‑reservoir batch and whether they can meet the cover + water layer (≥1.0 inch) option or the cover + freeboard ratio ≥0.75 option per cold‑cleaning requirements.

For vapor machines, verify presence and operation of required components: primary condenser, vapor level and sump‑heat shutoff devices, freeboard ratio (measure freeboard height and interior dimension to compute freeboard ratio), automated parts handling speed (≤3.4 m/min), and any covers or reduced room‑draft measures.

If using alternative standards, prepare to log solvent additions/deletions for each machine and to calculate monthly emissions per §63.465 procedures to compare to table 5 or table 6/equation 1 limits.

Determine whether the machine was constructed/reconstructed before or after November 29, 1993 (to classify existing vs new) and whether construction/reconstruction dates invoke specific compliance dates or different control options.

Inventory which control combinations or work practices are currently installed (covers, freeboard refrigeration device, freeboard ratio value, dwell, superheated vapor/part technology, carbon adsorber, lip exhaust routing) to assess conformity with tables 1–4 or with alternative standards.

Document and retain records and monitoring capability required to demonstrate compliance (monitoring of control device parameters, logs, and the ability to perform idling emission demonstrations if relying on emission limits).

These capture the principal reasons in the EPA notes."}

candidates.title: Printing, coating, slashing, dyeing, and finishing of fabric and other textiles

criteria.criterion: If the facility applies stain‑repellent finishes to textile substrates as part of a finishing operation, then the operation is part of the dyeing and finishing subcategory and the regulated materials include the dyeing and finishing materials used at that affected source.

If you choose the compliant material option for a dyeing/finishing operation, then you must apply no dyeing or finishing material with a mass fraction of organic HAP that exceeds the applicable emission limit in Table 1 to this subpart.

If the solvent used at your plant is a thinning material (an organic solvent added to a coating or printing material after the coating or printing material is received from the supplier), then that solvent is treated as a thinning material and, for web coating/printing affected sources using the compliant material option, thinning and cleaning materials must contain no organic HAP.

If you alter a regulated material by adding solvent after receipt, then for purposes of demonstrating compliance using the compliant material option you must evaluate the regulated material in the condition it is received from the manufacturer or supplier and prior to any alteration when determining organic HAP content.

checklist: Is the operation that applies the stain‑repellent finish a dyeing/finishing operation as defined in 40 CFR 63.4371 (i.e., chemical treatment of textile to impart properties such as stain resist)?
Is the affected source at your facility a major source of HAP (per 40 CFR 63.2) or located at a major source (affects applicability per 40 CFR 63.4281(b))?

Is the solvent used to dilute the finishing material: (a) supplied as part of the finishing material (mixed by supplier), or (b) added on‑site after receipt (i.e., a post‑purchase alteration/thinning)?
For each finishing material as received from the supplier, what is the mass fraction of organic HAP (use supplier formulation data or test results per 40 CFR 63.4321(e)(1))?

If the solvent is added on‑site, what is the organic HAP content of the solvent itself and of the resulting altered mixture (but note compliance calculation uses material as received prior to alteration for the compliant material option per 40 CFR 63.4321(e))?
Are you planning to use the 'compliant material' option or another compliance option (emission rate or control efficiency)?
What is the applicable emission limit in Table 1 to this subpart for your finishing operation (you must compare the material mass fraction of organic HAP or kg HAP/kg solids to that limit)?

If any thinning or cleaning solvents are used on web coating/printing lines at the same affected source, do those thinning/cleaning materials contain any organic HAP (they must contain no organic HAP to use the compliant material option for coating/printing per 40 CFR 63.4321(a) and 63.4321(e)(4))?
Do you maintain supplier documentation and records required by §§ 63.4312 and 63.4313 and include statements in the Notification of Compliance Status as required by 40 CFR 63.4321(e)(4)?

judge_text: {"score": 1, "reason": "EPA's key point—that solvents used to dilute textile finishing materials are subject to the finishing-operation organic HAP limits—is only partially reflected. The answer notes that dyeing/finishing materials are regulated and discusses thinning-material definitions and compliant‑material evaluation (materials as received), but it does not clearly state that solvents added as diluents to finishing materials are treated as part of the regulated finishing material/emission limit for these operations (and the cited thinning restriction is framed narrowly for web coating/printing). Thus some but not all key reasoning from the notes is captured."}

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants for Surface Coating of Wood Building Products (Subpart QQQQ)

criteria.criterion: if the item being coated contains more than 50 percent by weight wood or wood fiber (excluding the weight of any glass components) and is used in the construction of a residential, commercial, or institutional building and coatings (including adhesives) are applied in finishing or laminating, then the operation is in the wood building products source category for this subpart

if you own or operate an affected source that uses 4,170 liters (1,100 gallons) per year or more of coatings in the wood building products source category and the source is a major source, is located at a major source, or is part of a major source of HAP, then you are subject to this subpart
if the surface coating or other operations meet any of the exclusion criteria listed in paragraphs (c)(1) through (5) of § 63.4681, then this subpart does not apply to those operations

if your affected source’s surface coating operations that are subject to another subpart account for at least 95 percent of the total annual coating usage for the affected source, then you may demonstrate compliance with that other subpart for the entire affected source instead of this subpart

if your equipment and activities for surface coating of wood building products include all coating operations, storage containers and mixing vessels for coatings/thinners/cleaning materials, conveying equipment for coatings/thinners/cleaning materials, and storage/conveying equipment for waste generated by coating, then those items together constitute the affected source addressed by this subpart

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants for Surface Coating of Miscellaneous Metal Parts and Products (Subpart MMMM)

criteria.criterion: if you apply coatings to miscellaneous metal parts or products (including items such as extruded aluminum structural components and other metal components), then those surface coating operations are within the miscellaneous metal parts and products source category

if your surface coating operations are performed using coatings that meet the definition of high performance architectural coating or high temperature coating in § 63.3981, then those operations are in the high performance coating subcategory of this NESHAP

if you own or operate a new, reconstructed, or existing affected source that uses 946 liters (250 gallons) per year or more of coatings that contain HAP in the surface coating of miscellaneous metal parts and products and the source is a major source, is located at a major source, or is part of a major source of HAP, then you are subject to this subpart

if the surface coating or coating operation meets any of the exclusion criteria in paragraphs (c)(1) through (17) of § 63.3881 (for example, if the operation uses only materials that contain no organic HAP or if the metal components are metal components of wood building products that meet subpart QQQQ applicability), then this subpart does not apply to those operations

if an adhesive or adhesive coating is used for bonding and meets the subpart’s definition of adhesive/adhesive coating, then that adhesive application is treated as a coating operation for the purposes of this subpart

checklist: Confirm whether each window component you coat is a wood building product (contains >50% wood/wood fiber by weight, excluding glass) and is used in residential, commercial, or institutional building construction (per 40 CFR 63.4681(a)).

Document whether the coating you apply to wood components is part of finishing or laminating (including use of adhesives that meet the subpart’s definition of coating/adhesive) (40 CFR 63.4681(a); 40 CFR 63.4781).
Measure annual volume of coatings used on wood building products (liters or gallons) to determine if it is ≥4,170 L (1,100 gal) per year (40 CFR 63.4681(b)).
Determine whether the facility is a major HAP source (any single HAP ≥9.07 Mg/yr (10 tpy) or combined HAP ≥22.68 Mg/yr (25 tpy)) or is located at/part of a major source (40 CFR 63.4681(b)).

Verify whether any coating operations meet the exclusions in §63.4681(c) (e.g., wood furniture subject to subpart JJ, plywood/composite processes listed, research/lab or non-commercial operations) (40 CFR 63.4681(c)).

Check whether surface coating operations at the affected source that are subject to another subpart account for ≥95% of total annual coating usage (to determine applicability/alternative compliance per 40 CFR 63.4681(d)).
For aluminum components, confirm that the parts are miscellaneous metal parts/products (e.g., extruded aluminum structural components) and not excluded categories (40 CFR 63.3881(a)).
Measure annual volume of HAP-containing coatings used on miscellaneous metal parts (liters or gallons) to determine if it is ≥946 L (250 gal) per year (40 CFR 63.3881(b)).

Determine whether the coatings applied to aluminum components meet the definition of high performance architectural coating (AAMA 605.2-2000) or other high performance/high temperature coatings as defined in §63.3981 (40 CFR 63.3881(a)(3); 40 CFR 63.3981).
Determine whether the metal components you coat are metal components of wood building products that meet subpart QQQQ applicability (if so, check exclusion at 40 CFR 63.3881(c)(9)).
Confirm whether all coatings, thinners, additives, and cleaning materials used in the metal coating operations contain no organic HAP (per exemption at 40 CFR 63.3881(c)(1)).

Identify whether any other surface coating NESHAP(s) apply at the facility and whether a single surface coating activity accounts for ≥90% (predominant) or whether you qualify to use a facility-specific emission limit or other compliance choice described in §63.3881(e)/(3) or §63.4681(d) (40 CFR 63.3881(e); 40 CFR 63.4681(d)).

Record coating application methods (e.g., roll coater, curtain coater, spray guns, dip tanks) and whether the operation is a coating operation as defined in the applicable subpart (40 CFR 63.4681(a); 40 CFR 63.3881(a)(1)).

Verify whether adhesives used are reactive adhesives (if applicable) and whether HAP in reactive adhesive are emitted (see definition in 40 CFR 63.3981) to correctly account for organic HAP content in coatings.

candidates.title: Aerospace Manufacturing and Rework Operations (Subpart GG)

criteria.criterion: if a facility is engaged, either in part or in whole, in the manufacture or rework of commercial, civil, or military aerospace vehicles or components and is a major source as defined in §63.2 then this subpart applies to the facility
if an activity is a cleaning operation (hand-wipe, spray gun, or flush cleaning) then that activity is an affected source under this subpart
if the cleaning involves electronic parts and assemblies (other than cleaning and topcoating of completed assemblies) then the cleaning operation is not regulated by this subpart

if the cleaning is of aircraft or ground support equipment fluid systems that are exposed to the fluid, including hydraulic fluid systems, then the cleaning operation is exempt from the hand-wipe cleaning requirements of this subpart

if a cleaning solvent or other listed material meets the definition of 'Non-HAP material' in §63.742 then the requirements of this subpart do not apply to those primers, topcoats, specialty coatings, chemical milling maskants, strippers, or cleaning solvents

if a hand-wipe cleaning operation uses solvents that meet one of the composition requirements in Table 1 of §63.744(b)(1), or have a composite vapor pressure of 45 mm Hg or less at 20 °C per §63.744(b)(2), or demonstrate a 60% reduction in solvent volume from an approved baseline per §63.744(b)(3), then the hand-wipe cleaning operation meets the standards of §63.744(b)

if a spray gun cleaning operation is performed then the owner or operator must use one or more of the techniques specified for spray gun cleaning (enclosed system; nonatomized cleaning; disassembled spray gun cleaning in a closed vat; or atomizing cleaning with capture) as listed in §63.744(c)(1)–(4)

if a flush cleaning operation is performed then used cleaning solvent must be emptied into an enclosed container or collection system that remains closed when not in use or into a system with equivalent emission control as required by §63.744(d)
if a source is subject to this subpart then the owner or operator must obtain an operating permit from the State permitting authority in accordance with part 70 as required by §63.741(d)

if a cleaning operation is subject to this subpart then the owner or operator must record and retain the solvent identity, vapor pressure, documentation of organic HAP constituents, and usage/volume records as specified for cleaning operations in §63.752(b)(1)–(4)

if an owner or operator proposes to use an air pollution control device or equipment not listed in this subpart then they must submit a device description, performance test data, and proposed operating parameters to the Administrator for approval at least 120 days prior to the compliance date as required by §63.743(c)

checklist: Is the facility a 'major source' as defined in 40 CFR 63.2?
Does the facility engage in manufacture or rework of aerospace vehicles or components (even in part)?
For each cleaning activity: is it hand-wipe, spray gun, or flush cleaning as defined in §63.742?

Are the items being cleaned electronic parts/assemblies or printed circuit boards, and if so, are they 'completed assemblies' (cleaning of electronic parts and assemblies is exempt except for cleaning/topcoating of completed assemblies)?
Is the cleaning being performed on aircraft/ground-support fluid systems exposed to the fluid (e.g., hydraulic fluid systems)?
Obtain and review MSDS/manufacturer data for each solvent/azeotropic blend: list all organic HAP constituents and their mass percentages to evaluate the 'Non-HAP material' thresholds in §63.742
Determine the composite vapor pressure at 20 °C for each hand-wipe solvent (is it ≤45 mm Hg?)
Determine whether the hand-wipe solvent meets Table 1 composition requirements (aqueous or hydrocarbon-based) in §63.744(b)(1) or is semi-aqueous

If relying on the 60% reduction compliance option for hand-wipe solvents, assemble baseline usage data (1996–1997 or other approved baseline) and State/Administrator approval for the baseline and reduction plan

For spray-gun cleaning: document the cleaning method used (enclosed system, nonatomized, disassembled in closed vat, or atomizing with capture) and the presence/condition of leak controls and maintenance procedures
For flush cleaning: document the solvent collection system (enclosed container or equivalent control) and procedures for keeping containers closed when not in use

If using azeotropic blends (e.g., hydrofluoroether + dichloroethylene), verify whether any component is an organic HAP and its concentration relative to non-HAP thresholds; if HAPs present, determine applicability and required controls
Verify Title V/part 70 permitting status and whether the affected source will require a permit or permit modification per §63.741(d)
If using any air pollution control device not listed in the subpart, prepare technical description and test data to submit to the Administrator at least 120 days before compliance date per §63.743(c)
Prepare recordkeeping systems to retain solvent identities, vapor pressures, HAP constituent documentation, and monthly/annual usage records as required in §63.752(b)
