candidates.title: Area Source Standards for Plating and Polishing Operations (Subpart WWWWWW)

criteria.criterion: if the facility is engaged in one or more of the listed plating or polishing processes (non-chromium electroplating; electroless/non-electrolytic plating or coatings such as chromate conversion coating, nickel acetate sealing, sodium dichromate sealing, manganese phosphate coating; dry mechanical polishing after plating; electroforming; electropolishing) then subject
if the facility is an area source (the potential to emit any single HAP is less than 9.07 Mg/yr (10 tpy) and the potential to emit all HAP combined is less than 22.68 Mg/yr (25 tpy)) then subject
if the facility uses or has emissions of compounds of any plating and polishing metal HAP (cadmium, chromium, lead, manganese, or nickel) then subject

if a tank contains one or more plating and polishing metal HAP and is used for non-chromium electroplating, electroforming, electropolishing, electroless plating, or other non-electrolytic metal coating operations then that tank is an affected source under this subpart
if the process is chromium electroplating or chromium anodizing then not subject

if the process materials (as used in the tank) contain cadmium, chromium, lead, or nickel in amounts less than 0.1 percent by weight or manganese in amounts less than 1.0 percent by weight then not subject

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Chromium Electroplating and Chromium Anodizing Tanks (Subpart N)

criteria.criterion: if a tank performs chromium electroplating or chromium anodizing (as defined in this subpart) then the tank is an affected source subject to this subpart
if a tank is an etching tank, rinse tank, or cleaning tank in which neither chromium electroplating nor chromium anodizing is taking place then not subject
if the operation is a research and laboratory operation at the time the process is performed then not subject

if the bath contains chromic acid (CrO3) and electrical current is applied with the workpiece serving as the anode then the process meets the definition of chromium anodizing and is within the scope of this subpart

checklist: Verify whether the bath contains chromic acid (CrO3) or other chromium compounds (check SDS, supplier data, or lab analysis).
Verify whether electrical current is applied to the tank during the process and whether the workpiece functions as the anode or the cathode.

Determine and document the intended process type (chromium anodizing, chromium electroplating, non-chromium electroplating, electropolishing, electroless plating, chromate conversion coating, etching, rinse/cleaning).
Confirm whether the tank is used for etching/cleaning/rinsing only (no electrolytic current) or for an electrolytic plating/anodizing process.
Determine whether the materials (final bath as used) contain plating and polishing metal HAP at or above thresholds (Cd/Cr/Pb/Ni ≥ 0.1% by weight; Mn ≥ 1.0% by weight).
Calculate the facility's potential to emit (PTE) of HAPs to determine area source versus major source status (single HAP ≥ 9.07 Mg/yr (10 tpy) or combined HAPs ≥ 22.68 Mg/yr (25 tpy)).
If claiming an exemption, verify whether the operation is research and laboratory, educational, repair/maintenance, or bench-scale as defined in the subparts.

For applicability to Subpart WWWWWW, identify whether the tank is used for non-chromium electroplating or other listed non-chromium processes; for applicability to Subpart N, identify whether the tank is a chromium electroplating or chromium anodizing tank.

Document dates of construction or reconstruction of the affected source to determine new vs existing source status per the subpart definitions (e.g., March 14, 2008 for Subpart WWWWWW; Feb 8, 2012 for Subpart N where relevant).

candidates.title: Area Sources: Carbon Black Production

criteria.criterion: if you own or operate a carbon black production facility that is an area source of hazardous air pollutant (HAP) emissions then you are subject to this subpart
if you own or operate a carbon black production process unit then that process unit is the affected source under this subpart
if you commenced construction or reconstruction of the affected source on or before April 4, 2007 then the affected source is an existing source
if you commenced construction or reconstruction of the affected source after April 4, 2007 then the affected source is a new source
if your facility is a research and development facility as defined in section 112(c)(7) of the Clean Air Act then this subpart does not apply

candidates.title: Source category-specific applicability, definitions, and requirements (includes Carbon Black Production at paragraph (f))

criteria.criterion: if a carbon black production process unit is located at a major source as defined in section 112(a) of the Clean Air Act then the affected source for carbon black production under this subpart comprises each carbon black production process unit
if you produce carbon black by the furnace, thermal, acetylene decomposition, or lampblack processes then your operations meet the definition of carbon black production

if the HAP concentration of a carbon black production main unit filter process vent emission stream is equal to or greater than 260 parts per million by volume then that main unit filter process vent is subject to the control and applicability requirements in Table 8 to § 63.1103(f)

if the HAP concentration of any carbon black production process vent (other than the main unit filter) is equal to or greater than 260 parts per million by volume as determined by the process vent applicability determination requirements in § 63.1103(f)(3)(iv) then that process vent is subject to the control requirements in Table 8 to § 63.1103(f)

if a carbon black production process vent complies by routing emissions to a boiler or process heater for use as fuel gas then annual boiler/process heater tune-up requirements apply beginning no later than the compliance dates specified in § 63.1102(e)

checklist: Do you produce or recover carbon black as a product (confirm whether the process is furnace, thermal, acetylene decomposition, or lampblack)?
Inventory and describe the carbon black production process unit(s) (reactors, main unit filter, process filters, dryer, tailgas, ducts, vents, storage, product transfer racks).
Determine whether your facility is an area source or a major source of HAPs (compare your actual and potential-to-emit HAPs to the statutory major source thresholds in CAA §112(a)).
If subject to this subpart, determine whether each process unit was constructed or reconstructed on or before April 4, 2007 (existing) or after April 4, 2007 (new).
Verify whether the facility operation is a research and development facility as defined in CAA §112(c)(7).
Identify all waste management units, maintenance wastewater streams, and equipment components that contain or contact HAP and are associated with the carbon black production process unit.

Measure or obtain measurements of HAP concentration (in parts per million by volume) for the main unit filter process vent and other process vents following the process vent applicability determination procedures referenced in § 63.1103(f)(3)(iv).

If any process vent HAP concentration is ≥260 ppmv (per the cited applicability procedure), document which Table 8 control paths you would follow (flare or closed vent plus control device meeting §63.982(a)(2)).

If vents are routed to a boiler or process heater for fuel gas, confirm operation and be prepared to perform the annual tune-up procedures specified in §63.1103(f)(3)(iii) beginning by the compliance dates in §63.1102(e).

Check for any previous applicability tests (including dates) you can rely on (e.g., tests performed after Nov 18, 2016 or after Nov 19, 2021 as referenced) and whether any process changes have occurred since those tests.

Record whether any pressure relief devices used to protect against overpressure in the case of catastrophic failure of the process filter system should be designated as exempt from closed vent inspection requirements and be identified in Notification of Compliance Status if applicable.

judge_text: {"score":2,"reason":"EPA's sole rationale is that the facility process is materially different from the carbon black production processes defined in the rule; our answer explicitly includes the applicability criterion and checklist item requiring confirmation that carbon black is produced by the listed processes (furnace, thermal, acetylene decomposition, lampblack) and thus captures the key reason."}

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants: Surface Coating of Plastic Parts and Products (Subpart PPPP)

criteria.criterion: If you use the emission rate with add-on controls option and route organic HAP emissions from coating operation(s) to a boiler as an add-on control device then you must demonstrate the emissions reductions and ensure the emission capture systems and add-on control devices meet the operating limits required in § 63.4492 (except for solvent recovery systems conducting liquid-liquid material balances) and the work practice standards in § 63.4493.

If the add-on control device you plan to use (for example, a boiler) is not one of the devices listed in Table 1 to this subpart or you wish to monitor an alternative parameter and comply with a different operating limit then you must apply to the Administrator for approval of alternative monitoring under § 63.8(f).

If the add-on control device is not a solvent recovery system for which you conduct a liquid-liquid material balance then you must calculate the organic HAP emission reduction by applying the emission capture system efficiency (CE) and the add-on control device destruction or removal efficiency (DRE) to the mass of organic HAP in the materials served by the capture system using the procedures in § 63.4561(h), treating materials used during deviations as uncontrolled (zero efficiency) unless otherwise approved.

If you intend to use a solvent recovery system and conduct liquid-liquid material balances instead of an add-on control device like a boiler then you must calculate organic HAP emission reductions using the liquid-liquid material balance procedures and monthly solvent recovery efficiency calculations specified in § 63.4561(j).

If you use the emission rate with add-on controls option then you must perform the required initial compliance demonstration for each applicable coating operation and demonstrate compliance with the applicable emission limitations in §§ 63.4490, 63.4492, and 63.4493 as required in § 63.4561(a).

If you use the emission rate with add-on controls option then when calculating monthly and rolling 12-month organic HAP emission rates you must determine mass fraction of organic HAP, density, and volumes and calculate total emissions before and after add-on controls following the procedures in § 63.4561(e), (f), (l), and (m).

checklist: Confirm whether the boiler will be used as an add-on control device that receives captured coating emissions (i.e., emissions routed to the boiler exhaust) rather than only for facility energy use.

Check Table 1 of Subpart PPPP to determine whether the boiler (or its control category) is listed with established operating limits; if Table 1 is not available or the boiler is not listed, prepare to apply for alternative monitoring approval per § 63.4492(c) and § 63.8(f).

Decide whether you will use the emission rate with add-on controls option for specific coating operation(s); document which coating operation(s) are included and exclude operations using other compliance options.

Inventory monthly volumes, densities, and mass fractions of organic HAP for all coatings, thinners/additives, and cleaning materials used on the coating operation(s) you plan to control (to support calculations per § 63.4561(e)–(f)).
Verify whether the control approach is a solvent recovery system (subject to § 63.4561(j) liquid-liquid balances) or a combustion/add-on control (subject to CE and DRE procedures in § 63.4561(h)).

Confirm you have capture system(s) (hoods/enclosures) and the ability to measure or test capture efficiency (CE) and the add-on control device destruction or removal efficiency (DRE) per the performance test requirements referenced in § 63.4561(h) and to establish operating limits during performance tests as required by § 63.4492 and § 63.4561(b).

Assess whether you can meet and continuously demonstrate the operating limits and work practice standards required for controlled coating operations (records, monitoring, and initial compliance demonstration per § 63.4561(a) and ongoing compliance per § 63.4500(a)(2)).

Prepare documentation and recordkeeping to support initial compliance demonstration (performance test reports, CE/DRE test data, monthly material use calculations, and notifications) as required by § 63.4561 and related subpart requirements.

judge_text: {"score":2,"reason":"EPA's note hinges on the boiler being an approved add-on control device under Subpart PPPP. OUR ANSWER explicitly addresses use of a boiler as an add-on control, the need to route captured emissions to it, the requirement to meet §63.4492 operating limits (and Table 1), and the alternative-monitoring/approval path (§63.4492(c) and §63.8(f)) if the device is not listed — so the key EPA rationale is captured."}

candidates.title: Subpart PPPPP - Engine Test Cells/Stands

criteria.criterion: If you own or operate an engine test cell/stand that is located at a major source of HAP emissions then you are subject to this subpart
If you commenced construction or reconstruction of the affected source on or before May 14, 2002 then the affected source is an existing affected source
If you commenced construction of the affected source after May 14, 2002 then the affected source is a new affected source
If you meet the definition of reconstruction in §63.2 and reconstruction is commenced after May 14, 2002 then the affected source is a reconstructed affected source

If changes were made primarily for the purpose of complying with revisions to engine testing requirements under 40 CFR parts 80, 86, 89, 90, 91, or 92 then those changes are not considered a modification or reconstruction
If equipment consists of passive measurement and control instrumentation and electronics then that equipment is not included as part of any affected source reconstruction evaluation

If any portion of a new or reconstructed affected source is used exclusively for testing internal combustion engines with rated power of less than 25 horsepower then that portion does not have to meet this subpart's requirements except for initial notification

If any portion of a new or reconstructed affected source meets any of the criteria in paragraphs (d)(1) through (4) (exclusive testing of combustion turbine engines, rocket engines, noncommercial research/teaching, or testing/evaluating fuels/transmissions/electronics) then that portion does not have to meet this subpart's requirements

candidates.title: Subpart A - General Provisions (definitions, including 'reconstruction' and 'commenced')

criteria.criterion: If the fixed capital cost of the new components exceeds 50 percent of the fixed capital cost that would be required to construct a comparable new source then the replacement meets the 'reconstruction' cost threshold
If it is technologically and economically feasible for the reconstructed source to meet the relevant standard(s) then the second statutory reconstruction criterion is met

If an owner or operator has undertaken a continuous program of construction or reconstruction or has entered into a contractual obligation to undertake and complete, within a reasonable time, a continuous program of construction or reconstruction then construction or reconstruction is considered 'commenced'

If removal and reinstallation of an affected source satisfies the reconstruction criteria then the activity will be construed as reconstruction and the costs of replacing minor ancillary equipment must be considered in determining whether the existing affected source is reconstructed

candidates.title: Subpart KK - Compliance Dates / Reconstruction cost treatment

criteria.criterion: If an affected source has undergone reconstruction then the source is subject to the requirements for new affected sources
If costs are associated with the purchase and installation of air pollution control equipment then those costs are not considered in determining whether the affected source has been reconstructed
If costs are for retrofitting and replacement of equipment that is installed specifically to comply with this subpart then those costs are not considered reconstruction costs

checklist: Determine whether the plant is a major source of HAPs (plant-wide potential to emit ≥10 tpy of any single HAP or ≥25 tpy of combined HAPs).
Confirm whether the equipment in question are engine test cells/stands used for testing uninstalled engines (per Subpart PPPPP definition).
Document the dates when construction, replacement, or other changes to the test cells/stands were commenced and whether any construction/reconstruction activity commenced after May 14, 2002.

Document whether the work was undertaken as a single continuous program or contractual obligation (a single planning/continuous program) versus piecemeal, to assess whether construction/reconstruction was 'commenced' under §63.2.

Prepare a fixed capital cost comparison: calculate the fixed capital cost of the new components you installed/replaced and the fixed capital cost that would be required to construct a comparable new affected source, then determine whether the new-component cost exceeds 50% of the comparable-new-source cost.

Verify whether any of the replaced/added items are passive measurement and control instrumentation and electronics and exclude those items from your reconstruction cost calculation (they are not included per §63.9290(a)(3)).

Itemize costs spent on purchase and installation of air pollution control equipment and on retrofits/replacements installed specifically to comply with this subpart and exclude those costs from the reconstruction cost comparison per §63.826(c).

Determine whether any changes were made primarily to comply with revisions to engine testing requirements under 40 CFR parts 80, 86, 89, 90, 91, or 92 (such changes are not considered reconstruction under §63.9290(a)(3)).

Determine whether any portion of the test cells/stands is used exclusively for testing engines <25 hp or exclusively for combustion turbine engines, rocket engines, noncommercial research/teaching, or testing/evaluating fuels/transmissions/electronics to assess partial applicability exclusions under §63.9290(c)-(d).
Assess whether it is technologically and economically feasible for the (potentially) reconstructed source to meet the relevant standard(s) (second reconstruction criterion in §63.2).

Retain documentation and cost-supporting records for all replaced components, contracts, purchase orders, and scope-of-work descriptions to substantiate the timing, planning status, and cost allocations used in the reconstruction analysis.

Our answer explicitly includes the §63.2 reconstruction cost threshold (>50% fixed capital cost), the requirement to perform a fixed capital cost comparison, and the exclusions for passive measurement/control instrumentation and for control equipment costs (citations §63.2, §63.9290(a)(3), §63.826(c)), so the key reason in the EPA Notes is captured."}

candidates.title: Subpart LLLLL

criteria.criterion: if you install a continuous parameter monitoring system (CPMS) to monitor control device parameters then the CPMS must complete a minimum of one cycle of operation for each successive 15-minute period and meet the 3-hour average data-validity requirements

if you monitor pressure drop across the mist eliminator then the pressure sensor(s) must be located to provide a representative measurement, use a gauge with minimum sensitivity of 0.12 kiloPascals or a transducer with minimum sensitivity of 5 percent of the pressure range, check pressure tap pluggage daily, perform accuracy checks at least quarterly (or after deviations), perform monthly leak checks, and perform quarterly visible inspections of components if redundant sensors are not used

if the control device (e.g., your mist eliminator) is used to comply with the particulate matter standards in this subpart then you may establish pressure-drop operating limits (a minimum and a maximum) using the manufacturer's specifications in lieu of establishing site-specific limits under §63.8689(b)

if a control device is used to comply with the PM, THC, opacity, or visible emissions standards of this subpart then you must conduct periodic performance tests according to the procedures specified in §63.8687 and Table 4 and demonstrate continuous compliance with the operating limits as required in Table 5 according to the schedule in §63.8691(e)

if you are required to monitor and collect data to demonstrate continuous compliance then you must monitor and collect data at all required intervals at all times the affected source is operating (subject to the post‑2020 nonoperation exception) and you may not use data recorded during monitoring malfunctions, associated repairs, or required QA/QC activities in averages or minimum data-availability calculations

if a monitoring system is required then you must develop and have available upon request a written site-specific monitoring plan that addresses the installation location (representative and on or downstream of the last control device), performance and equipment specifications, performance evaluation procedures, ongoing O&M, QA/QC procedures, and recordkeeping and reporting

checklist: Is the mist eliminator the last control device for the Group 2 asphalt storage tank (i.e., is the monitoring location on or downstream of the device)?
Which Subpart LLLLL emission standards is the mist eliminator being used to comply with (particulate matter, opacity, visible emissions, THC)?
Do you have the manufacturer's pressure-drop specification (minimum and maximum) for the mist eliminator and are you intending to use those values as operating limits?
What type of monitoring system will be used (CPMS, CEMS, or COMS)?
If using a CPMS for pressure drop, can the CPMS complete at least one cycle every 15 minutes and produce the hourly/3‑hour averages per §63.8688(a)?
Does your pressure sensor meet sensitivity requirements (gauge ≥0.12 kPa or transducer ≥5% of range) and is it located to provide a representative measurement?
Can you perform daily pressure tap pluggage checks and record them, quarterly accuracy checks, monthly leak checks and quarterly visible inspections (or maintain redundant sensors)?
Have you conducted or scheduled the required periodic performance test(s) per the timing in §63.8691(e) (or do you have an acceptable prior test to use as the periodic test)?
Do you have a written site-specific monitoring plan that documents probe location, equipment/specs, performance evaluation procedures, O&M, QA/QC, recordkeeping, and reporting?

Are you prepared to exclude data from monitoring malfunctions, repairs, and QA/QC activities from compliance averages and maintain records of inspections, calibrations, and validation checks as required?
Will you perform and document any required visible emissions observations (daily or as specified) and maintain records of those observations?

candidates.title: General Provisions (Subpart A)

criteria.criterion: if an owner or operator applies for a waiver of a performance test then the owner or operator remains subject to the performance testing requirements until a waiver is granted

if an application for a waiver of an initial or subsequent performance test is submitted then the application must be submitted at least 60 days before the performance test if the site-specific test plan is not submitted
if an application for a waiver of a performance test is made then the application must include information justifying the request such as technical or economic infeasibility or impracticality

if the owner or operator can demonstrate by other means to the Administrator's satisfaction that the affected source is in compliance with the relevant standard then the Administrator may waive the requirement for performance tests

if a request for a waiver is considered then the Administrator will approve or deny the waiver when the Administrator approves or denies a site-specific test plan, an extension of compliance, or makes a determination of compliance or suitable progress as applicable

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants for Industrial, Commercial, and Institutional Boilers: Area Sources (Subpart JJJJJJ)

criteria.criterion: if your boiler has a heat input capacity of 10 million Btu per hour or greater then you must conduct all applicable performance (stack) tests on a triennial basis (tests completed no more than 37 months after the previous performance test)

if your boiler uses a continuous emission monitoring system (CEMS) for carbon monoxide then the boiler is exempt from the initial CO performance testing in Table 4 to this subpart and from the oxygen concentration operating limit in Table 3
if you are required to conduct performance stack tests then you must conduct them according to §63.7 (including developing a site-specific test plan) and the test procedures in this subpart

if you conduct performance stack tests then the tests must be conducted at representative operating load conditions while burning the type of fuel or mixture that has the highest emissions potential for each regulated pollutant

if you are required to conduct a performance stack test then you must submit a Notification of Intent to conduct the performance test at least 60 days before the performance stack test is scheduled to begin

if an existing affected boiler has not operated on solid fossil fuel, biomass, or liquid fuel since the previous compliance demonstration and more than 3 years have passed since the previous compliance demonstration then you must complete your subsequent compliance demonstration no later than 180 days after restart on those fuels
if you are demonstrating compliance with applicable emission limits then you must do so using performance stack testing, fuel analysis, or a CMS (including CEMS) as applicable

checklist: For each boiler, record maximum heat input capacity (MMBtu/hr) to determine whether it is >= 10 MMBtu/hr
For each boiler, confirm whether a CO CEMS is installed, operating, and maintained per applicable performance specifications

For each boiler, document the date(s) of the last CO performance test, the test results (showing compliance or not), and the date the next triennial test would be due (no more than 37 months after previous test)
Confirm whether you have submitted or will submit a site-specific test plan and/or a Notification of Intent at least 60 days before any scheduled performance test
Prepare evidence and specific justification (technical, economic, or impracticality) to include in any waiver application as required by 40 CFR 63.7(h)(3)(iii)
Determine whether the facility is currently operating under an extension of compliance or has submitted an extension request

Verify planned permanent cessation date for coal use (e.g., April 30, 2020) and whether any boilers will restart on solid fossil fuel, biomass, or liquid fuel before the next required compliance demonstration (if idle >3 years, note 180-day restart rule in 63.11220(e))

Confirm operating records showing continuous compliance (monitoring data, tune-ups, prior test reports) to support a waiver request under the Administrator's judgment that the source is meeting the relevant standards

Verify that any performance tests would be conducted at representative operating loads burning the highest-emission fuel or mixture, and identify which fuel constitutes the highest emissions potential
Ensure recordkeeping and reporting readiness to submit test results and Notifications of Compliance Status within the timeframes required by this subpart

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Halogenated Solvent Cleaning (Subpart T)

criteria.criterion: if an individual batch vapor, in-line vapor, in-line cold, or batch cold solvent cleaning machine uses any of the listed halogenated HAP solvents (methylene chloride, perchloroethylene, trichloroethylene, 1,1,1-trichloroethane, carbon tetrachloride, or chloroform) in a total concentration greater than 5 percent by weight as a cleaning and/or drying agent, then that machine is subject to this subpart
if solvent cleaning activities are limited to wipe cleaning (for example, use of a rag or spray cleaner containing halogenated solvent), then those activities are not covered under this subpart
if an owner or operator has an existing solvent cleaning machine that is subject to this subpart, then an initial notification report must be submitted as required in §63.468(a)

if you own or operate a batch vapor or in-line solvent cleaning machine that complies with the standards in §63.463, then you are required to submit an annual report by February 1 of the year following the reporting year as specified in §63.468(f)

if you own or operate a batch vapor or in-line solvent cleaning machine that complies with the provisions of §63.464, then you are required to submit a solvent emission report every year as specified in §63.468(g)

if your facility meets the definition of an affected facility in §63.471(a) (i.e., all solvent cleaning machines at a major source that are subject to the facility-wide limits, or for area sources, all solvent cleaning machines except cold batch cleaning machines that are subject to the facility-wide limits), then the facility must submit a solvent emission report every year as required in §63.471(h)

if no solvent cleaning machine at the facility currently uses any listed halogenated HAP solvent at concentrations greater than 5 percent by weight (i.e., no halogenated HAP consumption), then the applicability criteria in §63.460(a) are not met and the machine-level and facility-level reporting provisions in §§63.468 and 63.471 are not applicable to those machines

if an affected facility is subject to the facility-wide limits in §63.471(b)(2) then it must maintain monthly logs of solvent additions and deletions and calculate 12-month rolling total emissions as specified in §63.471(c) and report those emissions annually per §63.471(h)

if an owner or operator is complying with §63.463 and uses control devices or monitoring, then recordkeeping and reporting of monitoring results, training statements, solvent consumption estimates, and exceedance reports are required as described in §§63.467 and 63.468 (including annual reports, exceedance reports, and record retention)

checklist: Determine whether any on-site equipment qualifies as a 'solvent cleaning machine' under §63.461 (batch vapor, in-line vapor, in-line cold, or batch cold); exclude buckets/pails <= 2 gallons

For each solvent cleaning machine, verify whether any solvent currently used contains one or more listed halogenated HAPs (methylene chloride, PCE, TCE, 1,1,1-trichloroethane, carbon tetrachloride, chloroform)
For each solvent, verify concentration of listed halogenated HAPs (use MSDS, EPA Method 18, or engineering calculations) to confirm whether concentration is >5% by weight
Confirm whether any cleaning activities are only wipe cleaning (rags or spray) rather than use of a solvent cleaning machine
Review solvent addition/removal logs for the past 12 months to determine any halogenated HAP consumption (kg or lbs) and to support facility-wide or unit emission calculations if applicable

If previously subject but currently not using halogenated HAPs, document the date each machine ceased use of halogenated solvents and maintain records supporting zero consumption (e.g., solvent purchase/use records)

Determine whether the facility is a major source or area source and whether it meets the 'affected facility' definition in §63.471(a) (including whether cold batch machines are excluded for area sources)
If subject, identify which compliance pathway the machine uses (§63.463 vs §63.464) because reporting requirements differ (annual report per §63.468(f) vs §63.468(g))
Check whether initial notifications or initial statements of compliance required under §63.468 (and §63.471(f),(g) for facility-wide) have been submitted previously

Maintain or assemble required records (e.g., solvent addition/removal logs, solvent composition of wastes, calculation sheets) for the retention period specified in §63.471(e) and §63.467 (5 years where applicable)
If any exceedance has occurred in the past reporting period, prepare exceedance reports per §63.468(h) and track monitoring/repair actions as required by §63.467(b)(2)

judge_text: {"score":2,"reason":"EPA's reason — the facility is no longer subject because all machines were removed or converted to non‑regulated solvents (i.e., no use/consumption of listed halogenated HAPs) — is reflected in OUR ANSWER (criterion that no machine uses listed halogenated HAPs >5% so §§63.468/63.471 do not apply, plus checklist items to document cessation/zero consumption)."}

candidates.title: Organic Liquids Distribution (Non-Gasoline) NESHAP

criteria.criterion: if the plant is a major source of HAP and the transfer racks and transport vehicles are part of the collection of activities used to distribute organic liquids into, out of, or within the facility (including transfer racks at which organic liquids are loaded into or unloaded out of transport vehicles and all transport vehicles while loading or unloading at those racks) then those racks and transport equipment are part of the OLD affected source to which this subpart applies

if the storage tanks, transfer racks, transport vehicles, containers, or equipment leak components are part of an affected source already regulated under another 40 CFR part 63 NESHAP then those items are excluded from the OLD affected source (and thus not subject to this subpart EEEE)

if the storage tanks, transfer racks, transport vehicles, containers, or equipment leak components are non-permanent or are used only in special situation distribution loading/unloading operations or maintenance activities then those items are excluded from the OLD affected source (and thus not subject to this subpart EEEE)

candidates.title: Solvent Extraction for Vegetable Oil Production NESHAP

criteria.criterion: if you own or operate a vegetable oil production process that is a major source of HAP (or is collocated at a plant site that is a major source) and that process removes oil from listed oilseeds by direct-contact solvent extraction using an organic solvent such as hexane then the vegetable oil production process is an affected source subject to this subpart

if your vegetable oil production process processes any combination of the listed oilseeds (corn germ, cottonseed, flax, peanut, rapeseed, safflower, soybean, or sunflower) then the subpart's applicability criterion regarding oilseed type is met

if the process uses only mechanical extraction techniques, or uses only batch solvent extraction and batch desolventizing equipment, or processes only agricultural products that are not listed oilseeds then the vegetable oil production process is not subject to this subpart
if your HAP emissions increase such that the plant site becomes a major source then you become subject to all requirements of this subpart

checklist: Determine whether the plant site is a major source of HAPs (≥10 tpy single HAP or ≥25 tpy total HAP).
Confirm whether the facility operates a vegetable oil production process as defined in 40 CFR 63.2872 (continuous process producing crude vegetable oil and meal by direct contact with a solvent).
Verify whether the oil extraction method is solvent extraction (direct contact with hexane) versus mechanical-only or batch solvent extraction/desolventizing.
List all agricultural feedstocks processed and confirm whether any are listed oilseeds (corn germ, cottonseed, flax, peanut, rapeseed, safflower, soybean, sunflower).

Determine whether the transfer racks and transport equipment are dedicated to unloading solvent (hexane) for use in the on-site vegetable oil production process or are used for broader distribution activities independent of the oil production process.

Identify whether the transfer racks, storage tanks, transport vehicles, or equipment leak components are already assigned to or regulated under another 40 CFR part 63 subpart (i.e., are part of another NESHAP affected source).

Determine whether the transfer racks or equipment are non-permanent or are used only for special situations (maintenance, upset liquids management) or for maintenance activities (which would exclude them from EEEE per 63.2338(c)(2)–(3)).

Establish whether the transfer racks are loading/unloading organic liquids into storage tanks or process piping that are part of the vegetable oil production process (to assess inclusion in subpart GGGG solvent-handling components).
Document whether the transport vehicles are connected to transfer racks while loading/unloading at the site (to assess EEEE coverage of transport vehicles during loading/unloading).
Determine the facility’s classification of the affected source (new, reconstructed, or existing) for each applicable subpart.

judge_text: {"score":2,"reason":"The EPA note’s key rationale — the racks/equipment are dedicated to and solely support the solvent-extraction vegetable oil process and thus fall under Subpart GGGG (and therefore are excluded from EEEE) — is reflected in the answer: GGGG applicability criteria for solvent (hexane) extraction, the EEEE exclusion for components already regulated under another Part 63 subpart (63.2338(c)(1)), and checklist items (dedication to on-site oil production, assignment to another NESHAP) are all included."}

candidates.title: Subpart S

criteria.criterion: if you operate an enclosure opening subject to § 63.450(b) then perform a visual inspection of the closure mechanism at least once every 30 days to ensure the opening is maintained in the closed position and sealed
if you use a closed-vent system required by § 63.450(a) then visually inspect the closed-vent system (including ductwork, piping, enclosures, and connections to covers) every 30 days

if you operate a pulping process condensate closed collection system subject to § 63.446(d) then visually inspect the closed collection system every 30 days and comply with the inspection and monitoring requirements specified in § 63.964 of subpart RR except for the specified recordkeeping differences

if an inspection identifies visible defects in ductwork, piping, enclosures, or connections or if an instrument reading is 500 parts per million by volume or greater above background or enclosure openings are not maintained at negative pressure then a first repair effort must be made as soon as practicable but no later than 5 calendar days and completed no later than 15 calendar days (unless delay is allowed for technical infeasibility or to avoid greater emissions)

if you use a control device, technique, or an alternative operating parameter other than those specified in paragraphs (b) through (l) of this section then you must install a continuous monitoring system (CMS) and establish appropriate operating parameters to demonstrate continuous compliance to the Administrator's satisfaction

if you select or propose monitoring parameter values, monitoring frequency, or averaging time then you must provide the rationale (including all data and calculations) for the selected operating parameter value and monitoring frequency to the Administrator for approval

candidates.title: Subpart A

criteria.criterion: if you wish to use an alternative monitoring procedure (minor, intermediate, or major change) then you remain subject to the existing monitoring requirements of this part until the Administrator specifies or approves the alternative

if you wish to use an alternative monitoring procedure then you must submit an application that describes the proposed alternative (addressing the four elements in the definition of monitoring) and a performance evaluation test plan as specified in paragraph (f)(4) of this section

if you submit a request to use an alternative monitoring method then the Administrator will notify you of approval or intention to deny approval within 30 calendar days after receipt of the original request (and within 30 days after receipt of any supplementary information) and, if approved, you must continue using the approved alternative until further approval is granted

candidates.title: Subpart UUUU

criteria.criterion: if a time period (e.g., monthly) is specified in this subpart then that period refers to the standard calendar periods
if you want to change the time periods specified in this subpart then you may change those periods by mutual agreement with the Administrator as specified in subpart A

if a provision of this subpart requires completing a task during each of multiple successive periods then you may perform the required task at any time during the specified standard calendar period provided the task is conducted at a reasonable interval after completion of the task during the previous period

checklist: Identify the exact regulatory requirement(s) imposing the "every 30 days" inspection (e.g., 40 CFR 63.453(k) for enclosure/closed‑vent systems and 40 CFR 63.453(l)(1) for pulping process condensate closed collection systems).

Confirm whether the affected system is a pulping process condensate closed collection system subject to § 63.446(d) (i.e., covered by 40 CFR 63.453(l)) or an enclosure/closed‑vent system subject to § 63.450(a)/(k).
Determine whether the collection/vent system construction is hard‑piping or ductwork (Subpart H distinctions affect inspection procedures).
Verify whether the closed‑vent system contains bypass lines or bypass valves (affects monthly visual seal inspection requirements).
Document current inspection scheduling method (rolling 30‑day interval vs calendar‑month schedule) and actual historical inspection dates and results.
Assess whether any parts are designated unsafe or difficult to inspect and whether written plans exist to inspect them as frequently as practicable or per the difficult‑to‑inspect provisions.

Assemble performance and operational data, engineering assessments, and manufacturer's recommendations to support a rationale that once‑each‑calendar‑month inspections provide an equivalent level of monitoring and control (data to be provided to Administrator per 40 CFR 63.453(n)).

Prepare an application/monitoring plan per 40 CFR 63.8(f)(4) that describes the proposed alternative monitoring schedule, addresses the four elements of monitoring, includes a site‑specific performance evaluation test plan if required, and provides requested data and calculations to justify the change.
Plan to request mutual agreement with the Administrator to change the time period per 40 CFR 63.5560(d)(1) (coordinate with the Administrator using procedures in Subpart A).

Confirm ability to meet corrective action timelines (first repair effort within 5 calendar days and repair completed within 15 calendar days) if an inspection identifies defects or instrument readings ≥500 ppm above background, or document rationale if delay is necessary and technically infeasible without shutdown.
Identify staffing and operational constraints (weekend/holiday coverage) and document how the proposed calendar‑month schedule addresses these constraints while maintaining compliance readiness.

Retain/prepare records and procedures to demonstrate continuous compliance and to support any Administrator review of the proposed alternative (including any CMS quality control or performance evaluation materials if a CMS is proposed).

judge_text: {"score": 2, "reason": "EPA's note indicates a conditional (partial) approval tied to Administrator approval of an alternative monitoring approach and meeting specific conditions. The answer identifies the applicable 30‑day requirements, the need torequest/justify an alternative under 40 CFR 63.8(f), the calendar‑month/mutual‑agreement provisions (40 CFR 63.5560(d)), and the repair/monitoring/recordkeeping conditions (including providing rationale/data per 63.453(n) and meeting repair timelines). These key conditional bases from the EPA note are captured in the criteria and checklist."}

candidates.title: Polymers and Resins (Subpart JJJ)

criteria.criterion: if a plant site contains one or more thermoplastic product process units (TPPUs) located at a major source, then the provisions of Subpart JJJ apply to that affected source

if equipment (including pressure relief devices) is in organic hazardous air pollutant (organic HAP) service at a TPPU that is part of an affected source, then the owner or operator must comply with the equipment leak provisions of subpart H as modified by § 63.1331

if a pressure relief device is in organic HAP gas or vapor service at an affected source subject to Subpart JJJ, then the operating, pressure-release, and pressure-release-management requirements in § 63.1331(a)(9) apply to that device unless the routing or other exemptions in § 63.1331(a)(9)(iv) apply

if a pressure relief device in organic HAP service releases to the atmosphere as a result of a pressure release event, then the owner or operator must calculate the quantity of organic HAP released during each pressure release event and report as required in § 63.1335(e)(6)(xiii)

if a pressure relief device in organic HAP gas or vapor service does not include a rupture disk, then instrument monitoring using Method 21 must be conducted no later than 5 calendar days after a pressure release to verify instrument reading of less than 500 ppm above background

if a pressure relief device consists of or includes a rupture disk, then a replacement disk must be installed as soon as practicable but no later than 5 calendar days after a pressure release (unless routed to an exempt control or as otherwise allowed by § 63.171)

candidates.title: Equipment Leaks / Pressure Relief Devices (Subpart H)

criteria.criterion: if a pressure relief device is in gas or vapor service, then except during pressure releases it must be operated with an instrument reading of less than 500 ppm above background as measured by the method in § 63.180(c)

if a pressure relief device returns to organic HAP gas or vapor service following a pressure release and does not include a rupture disk, then instrument monitoring as specified in § 63.180(c) must be conducted no later than 5 calendar days after return to service to verify <500 ppm above background

if a pressure relief device is routed to a process or fuel gas system or is equipped with a closed-vent system capable of capturing and transporting leakage to a control device or back to the process, then the requirements of paragraphs (a) and (b) of § 63.165 do not apply to that device

if a pressure relief device is equipped with a rupture disk upstream of the device, then the requirements of paragraphs (a) and (b) of § 63.165 do not apply provided a rupture disk is installed upstream as soon as practicable but no later than 5 calendar days after each pressure release

if a pressure relief device is in organic HAP service and is subject to the paragraph (e) provisions (i.e., affected sources after the specified compliance dates), then the owner or operator must (among other requirements) operate the device with <500 ppm except during releases, equip the device with monitoring capable of identifying releases/recording time and duration/notifying operators, and apply at least three redundant prevention measures

if a pressure relief device is of a type listed in § 63.165(e)(5) (heavy liquid service, thermal expansion relief valves, pressure relief devices on mobile equipment, certain pilot-operated or balanced bellows devices), then that device is exempt from the pressure release management requirements of paragraph (e)(3)

checklist: Determine whether your plant site is a major source and whether the equipment is part of one or more TPPUs (40 CFR 63.1310(a))

Verify whether the process unit(s) at your site are designated as TPPUs (thermoplastic product process units) under § 63.1310(f) and retain documentation of the primary product determination if applicable (40 CFR 63.1310(f))

For each portable container, identify whether it is considered 'equipment' or a 'storage vessel' and whether it is permanently attached to motor vehicles or otherwise excluded (check capacity, design pressure, and mobility per 40 CFR 63.1312 storage vessel criteria)

For each pressure relief device (PRD), record whether it is operated in organic HAP service (identify the HAPs present and confirm they are listed organic HAPs) and the number of hours each PRD is in organic HAP service per calendar year (compare to the 300-hour threshold in 40 CFR 63.160(a))

For each PRD, determine whether it vents to atmosphere or is routed to a closed-vent system, control device, process, fuel gas system, or drain system (40 CFR 63.1331(a)(9)(iv); 40 CFR 63.165(c),(e)(4))

For each PRD, determine whether it consists of or includes a rupture disk, is pilot-operated, is balanced bellows type, is a thermal expansion relief valve, or is located on mobile equipment (40 CFR 63.165(d); 40 CFR 63.165(e)(5))

For PRDs that remain subject to the standards, verify existing monitoring: Method 21 or as referenced for instrument readings (<500 ppm above background), presence of monitoring capable of identifying releases/recording time and duration/notifying operators, and ability to perform post-release monitoring within 5 calendar days (40 CFR 63.1331(a)(9)(i)-(iii); 40 CFR 63.165(a),(b),(e)(2)-(3))
Count total number of PRDs and determine whether any are located on equipment considered 'mobile' or otherwise excluded from pressure-release-management requirements (40 CFR 63.165(e)(5)(iii))

If considering an alternative compliance approach (e.g., routing to closed vent and control device or using Part 65 options where available), document the design and operation demonstrating routing to control device/process/fuel gas/drain and ensure the closed-vent and control meet the referenced requirements (40 CFR 63.1331(a)(9)(iv); 40 CFR 63.165(e)(4))

If a release occurs, be prepared to calculate the quantity of organic HAP released, perform root cause and corrective action analyses, implement corrective actions on the required schedule, and include required reporting as specified (40 CFR 63.1331(a)(9)(iii)(B); 40 CFR 63.165(e)(3)(iii),(6),(7))

candidates.title: Subpart S — Pulp and Paper NESHAP (monitoring and test procedures)

criteria.criterion: if an owner or operator is subject to the standards specified in §§ 63.443(c) and (d), 63.444(b) and (c), 63.445(b) and (c), 63.446(c), (d), and (e), 63.447(b), or 63.450(d) then the owner or operator must install, calibrate, certify, operate, and maintain a continuous monitoring system (CMS) including a continuous recorder as specified in § 63.453(a).

if an owner or operator uses a control device, technique, or an alternative parameter other than those specified in paragraphs (b) through (l) of § 63.453 then the owner or operator must install a CMS and establish appropriate operating parameters that demonstrate continuous compliance to the Administrator's satisfaction as specified in § 63.453(m).

if proposing or establishing site-specific monitoring parameters or operating parameter values for the parameters required under paragraphs (b) through (j), (l), and (m), or for parameters referenced in paragraphs (f), (i), (j)(2), and (m) of § 63.453 then the owner or operator must follow the procedures in § 63.453(n)(1)–(4) (including continuously recording parameters during performance tests and providing the rationale and data for Administrator approval).

if using an open biological treatment system to comply with the condensate treatment standards in § 63.446(e)(2) then the owner or operator must perform the daily monitoring procedures and quarterly performance tests specified in § 63.453(j) and conduct performance testing and percent/mass removal calculations using the procedures in § 63.457(l).

if complying with the kraft pulping condensate requirements in § 63.446 then the owner or operator must measure total HAP concentration as methanol for condensate compliance measurements as specified in § 63.457(g).

candidates.title: Subpart MM — Kraft/Soda Recovery Furnaces, Lime Kilns (monitoring requirements)

criteria.criterion: if the facility operates an affected kraft or soda recovery furnace or lime kiln equipped with an ESP then the owner or operator must install, calibrate, maintain, and operate a continuous opacity monitoring system (COMS) in accordance with § 63.864(d).

if the facility operates an affected kraft or soda recovery furnace, kraft or soda lime kiln, sulfite combustion unit, or smelt dissolving tank equipped with a wet scrubber then the owner or operator must install, calibrate, maintain, and operate a continuous parameter monitoring system (CPMS) to determine and record scrubber pressure drop and scrubbing liquid flow rate at least once every successive 15-minute period as specified in § 63.864(e)(10).

if the owner or operator wishes to monitor alternative control device operating parameters for an ESP, wet scrubber, RTO, or fabric filter then they may do so only subject to prior written approval by the Administrator as provided in § 63.864(e)(13).

if the owner or operator uses an air pollution control system other than an ESP, wet scrubber, RTO, or fabric filter and seeks to use alternative monitoring parameters then the owner or operator must submit an alternative monitoring request describing the control device, test results verifying performance, proposed operating parameters and limits, measurement frequency, and QA procedures for Administrator approval as required in § 63.864(e)(14).

candidates.title: Subpart EEEEE — Alternative monitoring application procedures (monitoring-plan content and approval)

criteria.criterion: if you request approval to use an alternative monitoring method to demonstrate compliance then you must submit a monitoring plan that includes a description of the control or pollution prevention technique, a description of the continuous monitoring system or method including operating parameters to be monitored, test results demonstrating compliance, operating limit(s) (if applicable) determined from tests, and the frequency of measuring and recording and operation and maintenance requirements, and you may not use the alternative monitoring method until the Administrator approves the monitoring plan as specified in § 63.7747(c)–(d).

if you wish to request approval to use an alternative monitoring method then you may submit the request in the notification of construction or reconstruction for new sources or at any time as specified in § 63.7747(b).

checklist: Confirm whether your facility operates a kraft pulping system (identify pulping process type).
List all equipment that generates pulping process condensates or HAP-containing streams (e.g., brownstock washers, oxygen delignification vents, evaporator condensers, filtrate tanks).
Identify how pulping process condensates are treated (e.g., open biological treatment, anaerobic basins, steam strippers, combustion) and whether treatment is used to comply with § 63.446.
Determine whether you operate control devices relevant to Subpart MM (ESP, wet scrubber, RTO, fabric filter) and which units they serve (recovery furnace, lime kiln, smelt dissolving tank, etc.).

Determine whether you currently operate a CMS/CPMS/COMS and which parameters it records (temperatures, methanol or total HAP concentration, scrubber pressure drop, scrubbing liquid flow rate, opacity, flow rates, pH, VA/A ratios).

Decide whether you intend to propose alternative monitoring parameters or an alternative CMS/CPMS for any control device or treatment system and whether that alternative is for condensate treatment, gas scrubbers, thermal oxidizers, or other devices.

Collect performance-test data and continuous parameter records from the initial performance test(s) (continuous recordings during the test) to support establishing operating limits per § 63.453(n) and § 63.864(j).
If proposing methanol as the surrogate for total HAP in condensate compliance, confirm testing method to be used (e.g., NCASI DI/MEOH-94.03) and whether methanol will be used per § 63.457(g).

Prepare the monitoring plan contents required if requesting alternative monitoring: description of control technique, description of monitoring method and parameters, test results demonstrating compliance, proposed operating limits and how set, measurement frequency, and O&M/QA procedures as described in § 63.7747(c).
Verify whether any site-specific alternative standards (e.g., § 63.459 Flint River or Tomahawk provisions) could apply at your facility location or mill configuration.

candidates.title: Lime Manufacturing Plants

criteria.criterion: If you operate an existing affected source subject to Subpart AAAAA, then you must comply with the applicable emission and performance test deadlines specified in § 63.7083.

If a continuous opacity monitoring system (COMS) is used to monitor an add-on air pollution control device at your facility, then the COMS must be installed at the outlet of the control device and installed, maintained, calibrated, and operated in accordance with PS-1 and the Subpart AAAAA provisions.

If you operate existing lime kilns and any of the conditions in paragraphs (f)(1) or (f)(3) of § 63.7121 exist (positive-pressure FF with multiple stacks, monovent exhaust, or installation of a COMS per PS-1 is infeasible), then you may perform Method 9 visible emissions (VE) measurements in lieu of installing a COMS.
If you are required to have an OM&M plan under Subpart AAAAA, then your OM&M plan must address installation, operation, and maintenance of COMS and other CPMS per § 63.7113 and § 63.7100(d).

candidates.title: General Provisions

criteria.criterion: If you are the owner or operator of an existing affected source who is unable to comply with a relevant standard because installation of controls (e.g., a COMS) is necessary, then you may request an extension of compliance under the procedures in § 63.6(i).

If you submit a request for an extension of compliance under § 63.6(i) because installation of controls is necessary, then the request must be submitted in writing to the appropriate authority no later than 120 days prior to the affected source's compliance date unless the need arose after that date due to circumstances beyond your reasonable control.

If you request an extension of compliance under § 63.6(i), then your request must include a description of the controls to be installed and a compliance schedule with dates for initiating on-site construction/installation and for achieving final compliance as specified in § 63.6(i)(6).

If the Administrator (or an authorized State) grants an extension of compliance, then the extension will be in writing and will identify the affected sources, termination date, required steps and any other conditions to assure installation of controls and protection of health as specified in § 63.6(i)(10).

If you submit a nonfrivolous request for an extension in accordance with § 63.6(i), then the request will stay the applicability of the rule to the emission points in question until the request is granted or denied.

checklist: Confirm whether your facility is an LMP (lime manufacturing plant) subject to Subpart AAAAA.

Determine whether the affected kilns are 'existing' or 'new' and the dates construction/reconstruction commenced to identify the applicable compliance date per § 63.7083 (check relevant dates: Jan 5, 2004; Jan 5, 2023; July 16, 2024; July 16, 2027; Sept 16, 2019).
Identify whether the emission points in question exhaust through an add-on control device whose outlet would require a COMS under § 63.7113(g)(1).
Verify whether a COMS was installed on the control device on or before Feb 6, 2001 (to determine whether older COMS requirements may apply) per § 63.7113(g)(2).

Assess whether installation of a COMS in accordance with PS-1 is infeasible for the kiln(s) (physical/site constraints) or whether you instead have a positive-pressure baghouse with multiple stacks or a monovent, per § 63.7121(f)(1)–(3).
Compile your OM&M plan and confirm it addresses COMS/CPMS installation, operation, calibration, and maintenance per § 63.7113 and § 63.7100(d).

Decide whether you will request an extension: if so, prepare a written request including description of controls to be installed and a compliance schedule with milestone dates (initiation of on-site construction/installation and final compliance) as required by § 63.6(i)(6).

If seeking an extension, confirm submission timing: submit the extension request no later than 120 days before the compliance date unless the need arose after that date and include explanation/date when you first learned of the problem per § 63.6(i)(4)(i)(B)–(C).
Determine whether your State has an approved Part 70 permit program or delegated authority (because the State may grant extensions consistent with § 63.6(i)).
If granted an extension, be prepared to incorporate the extension conditions into (or apply for revision of) your Title V permit as required by § 63.6(i)(4)(i)(A) and § 63.6(i)(10).

Gather evidence and dates showing why additional time is necessary for COMS installation (procurement lead times, construction schedule, calibration/certification steps) to support the compliance schedule in the extension request.
Prepare to provide progress reports and to meet any milestones or additional conditions the Administrator or State may impose if an extension is granted (per § 63.6(i)(11)).

OUR ANSWER treats COMS as a control eligible for a §63.6(i) extension and does not include the EPA distinction that precludes using the control-installation extension for COMS."}

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Phosphate Fertilizer Production (Subpart BB)

criteria.criterion: If you use a continuous monitoring system (CMS) to demonstrate compliance with any applicable emission limit then you must develop and keep on site a site-specific monitoring plan that includes probe location justification, performance and equipment specifications, performance evaluation procedures and acceptance criteria, ongoing O&M procedures, ongoing data quality assurance procedures, ongoing recordkeeping and reporting procedures, and a schedule for conducting initial and subsequent performance evaluations

If you use a CMS then you must conduct performance evaluations of the CMS in accordance with your site-specific monitoring plan and the performance evaluation provisions of this subpart, and for fabric filters you must record the bag leak detection system sensitivity, range, averaging period, and alarm set points during the performance test

If you use a CPMS to establish operating parameter limits then the baseline operating parameter values must be determined as the arithmetic average of operating parameter measurements recorded during the three test runs conducted for the most recent performance test unless the absorber pressure-drop methodology or the alternative procedures based on previous performance tests are used

If you use a bag leak detection system then you must install, calibrate, maintain, and continuously operate it consistent with the site-specific monitoring plan, and you must not adjust sensitivity, range, averaging period, alarm set points, or alarm delay time except as established in your site-specific monitoring plan and sensitivity may not be increased more than 100 percent or decreased more than 50 percent over a 365-day period unless following a complete inspection showing the fabric filter is in good operating condition

If you will change monitoring parameters via a petition under §63.8(f) or request alternative monitoring parameters then the site-specific monitoring plan requirements apply and the plan must be submitted to the Administrator upon request at least 60 days before the initial performance evaluation of the CMS

checklist: Is a CMS/CPMS and/or bag leak detection system installed for each phosphate fertilizer process line or storage building subject to Subpart BB (identify which control device type: absorber, fabric filter, wet ESP)? (see 40 CFR 63.625(a), 63.625(d), 63.625(e))

Is there a current site-specific monitoring plan on site that includes: probe location justification; performance and equipment specs; performance evaluation procedures and acceptance criteria; O&M procedures; QA/QC procedures; recordkeeping/reporting procedures; and a schedule for initial and subsequent performance evaluations? (verify against 40 CFR 63.628(c)(1)(i)-(vi), (c)(2), (c)(3))

Was the site-specific monitoring plan submitted to the Administrator upon request at least 60 days before the initial performance evaluation of the CMS (or was a petition under §63.8(f) submitted)? (verify 40 CFR 63.628(c), 63.628(c)(3))

When were the most recent performance evaluations of the CMS and of any bag leak detection systems conducted, and do the evaluation records show the required parameters recorded (e.g., sensitivity, range, averaging period, alarm set points for bag leak detectors)? (verify 40 CFR 63.626(h), 63.625(e)(3), 63.625(e)(6))

Are annual performance tests (or required frequency) and the dates of those performance tests documented (including the three runs used to set operating parameter baselines)? (verify 40 CFR 63.626(a), 63.626(b), 63.625(d)(1)(i))

Were operating parameter limits established as the arithmetic average of the measurements recorded during the three test runs from the most recent performance test (or via the absorber ±20% methodology or the alternative procedure based on previous performance tests), and are the test reports available to support that? (verify 40 CFR 63.625(d)(1)(i), 63.625(d)(1)(ii)(A), 63.625(d)(1)(ii)(B))

Have any adjustments to bag leak detection sensitivity, range, averaging period, alarm set points, or alarm delay time been made in the last 365 days and, if so, are they documented and consistent with the limits and procedures in the site-specific monitoring plan (including any inspection justification if sensitivity changed by >100% or <-50%)? (verify 40 CFR 63.625(e)(6), 63.625(e)(7))

Does the site-specific monitoring plan explicitly specify the timing (relative to performance tests) for conducting CMS performance evaluations (i.e., does the plan permit performance evaluations within a 5-day window prior to performance tests or require same-day evaluations), and if changing that timing, was Administrator approval requested/obtained as required? (verify 40 CFR 63.628(c)(2), 40 CFR 63.628(c)(3))

Have performance test results and associated documentation been submitted to the Administrator within the required timeframe after each performance test, and are records retained on site as required? (verify 40 CFR 63.627(e), 63.627(c))

candidates.title: Phosphate Fertilizer Production Plants (Subpart BB)

criteria.criterion: if a phosphate fertilizer process line or granular triple superphosphate process line is subject to this subpart then you must install, calibrate, maintain, and operate a continuous monitoring system (CMS) with an accuracy of ±5 percent that determines and permanently records the mass flow of phosphorus-bearing material fed to the process

if an affected phosphate fertilizer process line is subject to this subpart then you must maintain a daily record of equivalent P2O5 feed calculated by determining the total mass rate of phosphorus-bearing feed using the procedures in §63.626(f)(3)

if you use a CMS to demonstrate compliance then you must develop and retain a site-specific monitoring plan that documents sampling location justification, performance and equipment specifications, performance evaluation procedures and acceptance criteria, ongoing operation and maintenance procedures, ongoing data quality assurance procedures, and recordkeeping/reporting procedures as required in §63.628(c)

if you wish to use an alternative monitoring method or alternative monitoring parameters then the Administrator must approve the request under the authorities retained in this subpart (including approval of requests under §63.8(f))

if you use a CMS then you must conduct a performance evaluation of the CMS in accordance with §63.8(e) and your site-specific monitoring plan, and for fabric filters you must conduct a performance evaluation of the bag leak detection system consistent with the referenced guidance

if you determine the equivalent P2O5 feed rate for use in performance test calculations then you must determine the mass flow rate of the phosphorus-bearing feed using the measurement system described in §63.625(a)

checklist: Identify which process lines you operate (e.g., diammonium/monoammonium phosphate process lines, granular triple superphosphate process lines, and any granular triple superphosphate storage buildings).
For each process line, verify whether it is an affected source under Subpart BB (check construction/reconstruction dates relative to December 27, 1996, per the definitions in §63.621).

Document the current measurement system(s) used to determine mass flow of phosphorus-bearing feed (e.g., magnetic flow meters): manufacturer/model, installation location, measurement range, calibration records, maintenance history, and probe/interface locations. (See §63.625(a)(1) and §63.628(c)(1)(i)-(ii)).
Measure and document the actual accuracy of the existing monitoring method over its operating range to determine whether it meets the ±5 percent accuracy requirement. (See §63.625(a)(1)).

Document how equivalent P2O5 feed is currently calculated (mass flow Mp and P2O5 content Rp) and whether P2O5 content measurement methods conform to the Book of Methods / AOAC methods referenced in §63.626(f)(3).

If proposing an alternative monitoring method, prepare a site-specific monitoring plan that includes: justification of sampling/measurement location, equipment and performance specifications, performance evaluation procedures and acceptance criteria, O&M procedures, data quality assurance procedures, recordkeeping/reporting procedures, and schedule for performance evaluations (per §63.628(c)(1)(i)-(vi) and §63.628(c)(2)-(3)).

If proposing an alternative monitoring method or alternative monitoring parameters, prepare and submit a request under §63.8(f) (or other applicable §63.8/§63.7 provisions) and be prepared to obtain Administrator approval (authority retained under §63.632(b)).
Plan and document a performance evaluation of the CMS per §63.8(e) in accordance with the site-specific monitoring plan prior to using the CMS for demonstrating compliance (see §63.626(h)).

If a fabric filter is used for compliance, verify whether a bag leak detection system is required and, if so, document that the bag leak detection installation, calibration, operation, alarm set-points, and corrective action plan are included in the site-specific monitoring plan per §63.625(e) and §63.628(d).
Maintain daily records of equivalent P2O5 feed as required and retain the site-specific monitoring plan and previous versions on site for inspection as specified in §63.628(c)(3) and §63.625(a)(2).

These criteria capture the key reason in the EPA Notes."}

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants for Catalytic Cracking Units and Catalytic Reforming Units (Subpart UUU)

criteria.criterion: if the catalytic cracking unit regenerator vent is subject to the PM limit in 40 CFR 60.102(a)(1), uses a wet scrubber for PM control, you have Administrator-approved alternative monitoring requirements for the continuous opacity monitoring system under 40 CFR 60.105(a)(1), and this subpart requires installation, operation, and maintenance of a continuous opacity monitoring system for the same regenerator vent, then you may request alternative monitoring requirements under § 63.1573(g)

if a specific control device may be monitored using more than one continuous parameter monitoring system then you may select which parameter you will use for compliance but must provide notice to the Administrator if you elect to change the monitoring option

if you performed a performance test to demonstrate compliance then you must base the continuous parameter monitoring operating limits on the results measured during the performance test and any adjustments to those measured values must follow the criteria in § 63.1571(d)
if you choose to adjust the equilibrium catalyst Ni concentration to the maximum level then you may not adjust any other monitored operating parameter

if you want to change an established operating limit for a continuous parameter monitoring system then you must perform an additional performance test, a performance test with an engineering assessment, or an engineering assessment to verify that the new limit ensures compliance
if you change process or operating conditions that could affect control system performance then you must establish a revised operating limit as described in § 63.1571(e)(2)

if you operate a jet ejector type wet scrubber or a wet scrubber equipped with atomizing spray nozzles then you may use daily checks of the air or water pressure to the spray nozzles, maintain records of those checks, and repair faulty lines within 12 hours as an alternative to continuous pressure-drop monitoring

if you wish to monitor process or control device parameters other than those specified in this subpart then you must submit a request to the Administrator that includes a description of the affected source and parameters, the methods to demonstrate the parameter's adequacy, monitoring/recording/reporting frequency and rationale, supporting calculations, and averaging time per § 63.1573(f)

if your source is required to install, operate, and maintain continuous monitoring systems then those monitoring systems must be installed, operated, maintained, and have data acquisition and availability consistent with the requirements in § 63.1572

checklist: Determine whether your FCCU catalyst regenerator vent is subject to the NSPS PM limit at 40 CFR 60.102(a)(1).
Confirm that the FCCU regenerator vent is controlled by a wet scrubber for PM emissions (document scrubber type and configuration).

Verify whether you have an Administrator-approved alternative monitoring requirement under 40 CFR 60.105(a)(1) for the continuous opacity monitoring system for this regenerator vent (obtain approval documentation).

Confirm that Subpart UUU requires you to install, operate, and maintain a continuous opacity monitoring system for that same regenerator vent (check your applicability, Notification of Compliance Status, and Table 3 requirements).
If you base operating limits on a performance test, gather the performance test report(s) and the measured parameter values used to set the operating limits.
Document any adjustments already made to performance-test-measured values and the supporting rationale or calculations used per § 63.1571(d).
Identify whether you seek to change which parameter is monitored for the wet scrubber; if so, prepare to notify the Administrator as required by § 63.1564(a)(2).

Check whether your wet scrubber is a jet ejector or uses atomizing spray nozzles; if so, confirm you perform and retain daily air/water pressure checks and repair faulty lines within 12 hours as required by § 63.1573(b).

Review whether there have been changes in process or operating conditions since the last performance test that could affect control performance and would require establishing a revised operating limit per § 63.1571(e)(2).

If you intend to change an established operating limit, plan and document an additional performance test or engineering assessment (or both) per § 63.1571(e)(1) and gather resources to demonstrate compliance at the new limit.

If proposing alternative monitoring parameters, prepare the approval request package including: description of source and parameter selection rationale; methods/procedures and schedule to demonstrate parameter adequacy; monitoring/recording/reporting frequency and rationale; supporting calculations; and proposed averaging time as specified in § 63.1573(f)(1)–(5).

Ensure your operation, maintenance, and monitoring (OM&M) plan includes the process and control device parameters to be monitored and established operating limits, monitoring procedures, flow rate and coke burn-rate procedures, pH/alkalinity procedures for scrubbers (if applicable), monitoring schedule, quality control plan, and maintenance schedule per § 63.1574(f)(2)(i)–(x).

Confirm that any continuous monitoring systems meet the installation, operation, maintenance, data frequency, data availability, and recordkeeping requirements specified in § 63.1572 (including hourly/15‑minute cycles and data reduction rules).
If you have an existing NSPS-approved alternative monitoring plan for opacity, obtain and include a copy of that approval in any Subpart UUU alternative monitoring request per § 63.1573(g)(3).
