candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants From Iron and Steel Foundries and Steel Pickling—HCl Process Emissions

criteria.criterion: If a wet scrubber is used as the emission control device at a steel pickling facility or acid regeneration plant subject to this subpart, then the owner or operator must install, operate, and maintain systems for the measurement and recording of the scrubber makeup water flow rate and, if required, recirculation water flow rate, monitored continuously and recorded at least once per shift while the scrubber is operating.

If a wet scrubber is used to achieve compliance, then during the performance test the owner or operator must establish site-specific operating parameter values for the minimum scrubber makeup water flow rate and, if applicable, minimum recirculation water flow rate, with operating parameters monitored and recorded during the test (no less frequently than once every 15 minutes) and the compliant values determined as averages of the test runs used to establish emissions.

If a monitoring device is used to meet the monitoring requirements of this subpart, then each monitoring device must be certified by the manufacturer to be accurate to within 5 percent and must be calibrated in accordance with the manufacturer's instructions at least annually.

If the owner or operator develops alternative monitoring requirements for a source subject to this subpart, then the alternative monitoring requirements must be approved by the Administrator before implementation.

If the owner or operator fails to record each of the operating parameters listed for wet scrubbers (makeup and recirculation flow rates), then that failure is a violation of the monitoring requirements of this subpart.

candidates.title: General Provisions for Continuous Monitoring and Alternative Monitoring Plans for Certain NESHAP (CMS requirements)

criteria.criterion: If you are required by §63.9020(e) to monitor an operating parameter, then you must install, operate, and maintain each continuous monitoring system (CMS) and collect data at all times the process is operating, collecting data from at least four equally spaced periods each hour, have valid data for at least 75 percent of operating hours per day, calculate hourly and daily averages from the valid data, and record inspection, calibration, and validation checks as specified in your site-specific monitoring plan.

If you wish to monitor parameters other than those specified for scrubber control devices, then you must request approval in accordance with §63.8(f) by submitting a monitoring plan that (1) identifies the operating parameter to be monitored to ensure the control efficiency is maintained, (2) discusses why the parameter is appropriate for demonstrating ongoing compliance, and (3) identifies the specific monitoring procedures.

candidates.title: General Monitoring Requirements for Control and Recovery Devices (continuous parameter monitoring systems, alternatives)

criteria.criterion: If monitoring is required under this subpart, then monitoring shall be conducted as set forth in this section and the referencing subpart unless the Administrator approves minor changes in methodology or approves the use of alternatives to any monitoring requirements or procedures.

If a continuous parameter monitoring system (CPMS) or other monitoring equipment is used, then it must be installed, calibrated, maintained, and operated according to the manufacturer's specifications or written procedures providing adequate assurance of accurate monitoring, be operated consistent with good air pollution control practices, be installed and operational (and data verified) prior to or in conjunction with performance tests, and be installed so representative measurements of parameters from the regulated source are obtained.

If you establish a range for monitored parameters that indicates proper operation of the control or recovery device, then that range must be based on the results of the most recent performance test and the required information must be submitted in the Notification of Compliance Status or the operating permit application or amendment.

If you wish to monitor a different parameter than those listed in this section or to set unique monitoring parameters, then you may request approval as specified in §63.999(d)(2) (i.e., seek Administrator approval to monitor a different parameter).

checklist: Confirm that your facility is an affected steel pickling facility or acid regeneration plant subject to Subpart CCC (determine applicability to 40 CFR part 63 Subpart CCC).
Confirm the control device for the pickle line HCl emissions is a wet scrubber (not another control device).

Locate and review the most recent performance test reports for the scrubber to determine whether site-specific minimum scrubber makeup water flow rate and minimum recirculation water flow rate were established and record the numeric minimum values and the test averaging intervals.

Determine whether the performance test included (or could be rerun to include) conductivity as an operating parameter so that conductivity-based actions correspond to the established minimum makeup flow/operating parameter values.

Verify whether the scrubber makeup water flow rate and recirculation flow rate are currently measured and recorded continuously and at least once per shift while operating, and collect representative historical records.

If proposing conductivity as the monitoring parameter, prepare a monitoring plan for Administrator approval under §63.8(f) that (a) identifies conductivity as the parameter to be monitored, (b) explains why conductivity demonstrates continued control efficiency, and (c) specifies the exact monitoring procedures, locations, averaging and data handling.

Ensure any CMS or monitoring instrument intended to demonstrate compliance is certified by the manufacturer to be accurate to within ±5% and that calibration procedures and frequency meet the manufacturer's instructions (at least annually per CCC).

Confirm CMS data collection and averaging will meet the CMS requirements (collect data at least four equally spaced periods each hour, obtain valid data for ≥75% of operating hours per day, compute hourly averages using required rules, compute daily average) as required by §63.9025(a).

Verify the CMS (or proposed conductivity monitor) will be installed, operational, and data-verified prior to or in conjunction with any performance test used to set monitoring ranges, and that the system yields representative measurements of the scrubber parameter(s).

Document procedures for immediate corrective action and maintenance if monitored values drop below the site-specific minimums established by performance testing (consistent with §63.1162(a)(2) and §63.1161(b)).

Assemble records and planned submittals required to support an alternative-monitoring approval (performance test data, monitoring plan, rationale connecting conductivity to control efficiency, QA/QC and calibration procedures, planned data averaging and validity rules).
Check whether any other subpart requirements apply at your site (e.g., process vent provisions in Subpart G) that would mandate pH or flow monitoring for certain halogenated vent streams.

These elements reflect the EPA’s stated need for additional parameters and compliance with existing requirements."}

candidates.title: Subpart HHHHHHH

criteria.criterion: If you are using an absorber or acid gas scrubber to meet an emission limit in Table 1 or 2 to this subpart and are required to use CPMS as specified in § 63.11925(c) then you must install and operate the monitoring equipment specified in § 63.11940(c)(1) through (3).

If you wish to use an alternative monitoring parameter or procedure instead of the continuous operating parameters listed in this section then you must request Administrator approval as provided in § 63.11940(h).

If you must establish operating limits for each monitored parameter then the operating limit must be based on values recorded during the performance test and supporting rationale as specified in § 63.11935(d).

If monitoring equipment for pressure, temperature, volumetric flow rate, mass flow rate or conductivity is used as a CPMS then the equipment must be capable of measuring across a range that extends at least 20 percent beyond the normal expected operating range of that parameter as specified in § 63.11935(c)(6).

candidates.title: Subpart SS

criteria.criterion: If monitoring is conducted under this subpart then the monitoring shall be conducted as set forth in this section unless the Administrator specifies minor methodological changes or approves alternatives as provided in § 63.996(b)(1)(i) or (ii) and § 63.996(d).

If a CPMS is used to demonstrate compliance then the CPMS must be installed so that representative measurements of parameters from the regulated source are obtained and the CPMS shall be in continuous operation when emissions are being routed to the monitored device except for specified short maintenance, calibration, or repair periods as specified in § 63.996(c)(4) and (5).

If you must establish a range for monitored parameters that indicates proper operation of the control or recovery device then you must establish that range as specified in § 63.996(c)(6), and the range may be based upon a prior performance test or other methods described in that paragraph.

candidates.title: Subpart G

criteria.criterion: If an owner or operator uses a scrubber to comply with the process vent provisions then the owner or operator must install a pH monitoring device with a continuous recorder and a flow meter at the scrubber influent and determine gas flow using one of the methods in § 63.114(a)(4)(i) through (iii).
If an owner or operator seeks to monitor parameters other than those listed in paragraphs (a) or (b) of this section then the owner or operator may request approval to do so under § 63.114(c).

If an owner or operator must establish a range that indicates proper operation of the control device then the range shall be based on the results of the most recent performance test as specified in § 63.114(e).

checklist: Confirm whether the scrubber in question is an absorber or acid gas scrubber used to meet an emission limit under the referenced subpart and Tables (i.e., determine which subpart and table govern the process vent).
Determine whether CPMS are required for the scrubber under the applicable subpart (e.g., whether § 63.11925(c) or the relevant subpart requires CPMS for this control device).
Identify the current CPMS parameter(s) being used on the scrubber (e.g., inlet pressure, outlet pressure, pressure drop) and the physical measurement locations for those sensors.

Verify whether the present monitoring is a requirement of Subpart HHHHHHH, Subpart G, and/or Subpart SS for this specific process vent (compare your process vent classification and TRE, if applicable).

Assemble performance test data for the scrubber (results, monitored parameter values during the test, and test conditions) that would be used to establish operating limits per § 63.11935(d) and § 63.114(e).

Document the rationale and calculations showing why ambient pressure substituted for outlet pressure would be representative of the monitored pressure differential (engineering assessment, manufacturer recommendations, test data).
Confirm that any proposed CPMS sensor and measurement range cover at least ±20 percent beyond the normal expected operating range (per § 63.11935(c)(6)).

Prepare a site-specific monitoring plan or monitoring plan amendment describing the proposed alternative parameter, monitoring equipment, data collection, QA/QC, and proposed operating limits as would be submitted for Administrator review per the referenced subparts.

Gather records of any prior approval(s) (e.g., Texas approval) for similar alternative monitoring at the facility, including the scope, conditions, and any Administrator correspondence to reference in a new request.

Identify applicable notification/permit filings required to request alternative monitoring (e.g., Notification of Compliance Status, operating permit application or amendment) and the specific supporting information to include (performance test data, monitoring plan, rationale for operating limits).

Confirm continuous operation/availability and representative measurement placement for the proposed ambient-pressure-based monitoring and procedures for immediate repair/replacement and documentation per CPMS operation and maintenance requirements.

candidates.title: Subpart LLLLLL

criteria.criterion: if you use a wet scrubber to control polymerization process equipment then you must maintain the daily average water flow rate at a minimum of 50 liters per minute and operate and maintain a CPMS that measures and records the water flow rate at least every 15 minutes

if you use a wet scrubber to control monomer recovery process equipment then you must maintain the daily average water flow rate at a minimum of 30 liters per minute and operate and maintain a CPMS that measures and records the water flow rate at least every 15 minutes

if you do not use a wet scrubber control device for the polymerization or monomer recovery process equipment then you must submit a monitoring plan to EPA or the delegated authority that includes a device description, performance test results, an O&M and continuous monitoring plan, a list of monitored parameters, and operating parameter limits

if you seek to change the operating limits for a wet scrubber then you must notify the Administrator to conduct a new performance test, conduct that performance test to demonstrate compliance, and establish revised operating limits using CPMS measurements during the test runs

candidates.title: Subpart SS

criteria.criterion: if you are an owner or operator of a regulated source required to monitor under this subpart then monitoring must be conducted as set forth in this section and the relevant sections unless the Administrator approves minor methodological changes or approves alternatives as provided in paragraph (d)

if one CPMS is used as a backup to another CPMS then you must report the results from the CPMS used to meet the monitoring requirements and if both are used during a reporting period you must report results from each for the time each instrument was relied upon

if you operate CPMS equipment then it must be installed, calibrated, maintained, and operated according to manufacturer's specifications or other written procedures that provide adequate assurance of accurate monitoring and maintained consistent with good air pollution control practices

if you want to use alternatives to the continuous operating parameter monitoring and recordkeeping provisions or to monitor a different parameter than those listed then you may request approval as provided in paragraph (d)

candidates.title: Subpart HHHHHHH

criteria.criterion: if you are required by §63.11925(c) to install and operate a CPMS for a control device used to meet process vent emission limits then you must install and operate the applicable CPMS specified in §63.11940(a)–(g), and monitor, record, and calculate CPMS data averages as specified in the subpart

if you are using an absorber or acid gas scrubber to meet an emission limit in Table 1 or 2 to this subpart and are required to use CPMS then you must install and operate either a flow meter to monitor influent liquid flow or a flow meter plus gas stream flow measurement and monitor the liquid-to-gas ratio using one of the specified procedures

if you are using an absorber or acid gas scrubber to meet an emission limit and are required to use CPMS then you must install and operate either pressure gauges at the inlet and outlet to monitor pressure drop or, where applicable based on temperature or specific gravity differences, a temperature or specific gravity monitoring device as specified

if you wish to request approval to use alternatives to the continuous operating parameter monitoring listed in this section or to monitor a different parameter then you may request approval as provided in paragraph (h)

checklist: Determine whether your facility is a regulated source for acrylonitrile polymerization or monomer recovery subject to Subpart LLLLLL (i.e., polymerization process equipment and/or monomer recovery process equipment emitting AN).
Identify whether the control device for the AN-containing streams is a wet scrubber and, if so, whether it controls polymerization process equipment, monomer recovery equipment, or both.

Record the current daily average water flow rate to each wet scrubber (calculate daily averages from 15-minute or finer measurements) and verify whether flows meet or exceed 50 l/min for polymerization control and 30 l/min for monomer recovery control.
Confirm whether a CPMS is installed for each wet scrubber and whether it measures and records water flow at least every 15 minutes and produces daily average values as required.

If you do not use a wet scrubber for a given control point, assemble a proposed monitoring plan including device description, test results (per the referenced performance test method), O&M and continuous monitoring plans, list of operating parameters to be monitored, and proposed operating limits.

If you seek to revise wet scrubber operating limits, determine whether you will request a new performance test and ensure CPMS data can be measured and recorded during each test run to establish revised limits.

Determine whether your scrubber is used to meet emission limits under the process-vent CPMS requirements in Subpart HHHHHHH (e.g., listed in Table 1 or 2) and whether §63.11925(c) requires CPMS for your control device.

If your control device is an absorber or acid gas scrubber, document whether you can/should monitor influent liquid flow (and gas flow or L/G ratio), whether pressure drop monitoring is feasible, and whether pH, caustic strength, or conductivity monitoring is required because the scrubbing liquid is a reactant.

Decide which gas flow determination method you will use (design blower capacity with adjustments, measured gas flow at inlet, or prior representative test data) and assemble supporting documentation if choosing a plan-based method.

Determine whether you intend to request Administrator approval for alternative monitoring parameters or procedures (under Subpart SS, Subpart HHHHHHH, or Subpart LLLLLL where applicable) and prepare the justification and supporting data (performance tests, CPMS data, O&M procedures) needed for that approval.

candidates.title: Subpart RRRRR

criteria.criterion: If a dynamic wet scrubber is applied to meet any particulate matter emission limit in Table 1 to this subpart, then you must maintain the daily average scrubber water flow rate and the daily average fan amperage at or above the minimum levels established during the initial performance test.

If you perform the particulate matter performance test for a dynamic wet scrubber, then you must measure and record the scrubber water flow rate and fan amperage every 15 minutes during each run and establish the operating limits as the lowest average values corresponding to any of the three test runs.

If a dynamic wet scrubber is subject to those operating limits, then you must install, operate, and maintain a continuous parametric monitoring system (CPMS) and monitor the daily average scrubber water flow rate and the daily average fan amperage according to the monitoring requirements.

If you wish to change the operating limits established during a performance test, then you must submit written notification to the Administrator requesting a new performance test, conduct the performance test to demonstrate compliance with the applicable emission limitation, and establish revised operating limits according to the applicable procedures.

If you seek alternatives to the monitoring requirements in paragraphs (b)(1) through (7) of §63.9590, then you may petition the Administrator for approval of alternative monitoring as allowed under §63.8(f) and defined in §63.90.

candidates.title: Subpart DDD

criteria.criterion: If you want to change control device or process operating parameter levels established during performance tests, then you must notify the Administrator of your desire and, upon approval, conduct additional performance tests at the proposed new parameter levels to verify that the emission limits are met.

checklist: Confirm whether each of the twelve scrubbers are dynamic wet scrubbers and whether they are used to meet any particulate matter emission limit in Table 1 to Subpart RRRRR.

Determine the facility construction or reconstruction date(s) for the affected source(s) (e.g., before/after September 25, 2019 and after July 28, 2020) to identify which phased requirements and deadlines apply.
Locate and review the initial performance test reports for each dynamic wet scrubber and extract the CPMS 15-minute measurements for fan amperage and scrubber water flow rate for each test run.

Calculate the average fan amperage and average scrubber water flow rate for each individual test run and identify the lowest average value among the three runs used to establish the site-specific operating limits per §63.9622(b)(2).

Verify whether a CPMS is installed, calibrated, and configured to record fan motor amperage and scrubber water flow rate at 15-minute intervals and to produce daily averages as required by §63.9631(c) and §63.9622(b)(1).

Compare your proposed parametric limit (motor full-load amps measured under no-load + 10%) to the established site-specific operating limit (lowest average fan amperage from the performance test) and document the numerical differences.

If you intend to change the established operating limit to the proposed full-load-amps +10% method, prepare to notify the Administrator and plan a new performance test at the proposed levels (per §63.9622(f) and §63.1186), including test protocol and data to demonstrate compliance with the Table 1 PM limits.
If you prefer a different monitoring approach instead of fan amperage (e.g., pressure drop or other surrogate), prepare a petition under §63.8(f) with supporting data as allowed by §63.9590(c).

Assemble CPMS recordkeeping and data reduction procedures and confirm you can demonstrate continuous compliance and follow corrective action timelines if daily averages fall below established limits per §63.9634(f) and §63.9634(l).

Check whether the scrubbers were treated as representative units within a group of similar emission units (per grouping rules) and whether the representative unit’s operating limits apply to all units in the group (per §63.9634(b)(3)).
Confirm Title V permit requirements and any permit schedule for subsequent performance tests (dates and frequency) that may affect when tests or limit changes can be made (per §63.9634(b)(2)).

candidates.title: Surface Coating of Automobile and Light-Duty Trucks (Subpart IIII)

criteria.criterion: If you seek to use results of a previous transfer efficiency test in lieu of conducting a new initial transfer efficiency test, then the previous test must meet the conditions specified in §63.3160(c)(1) through (3).

If the previous transfer efficiency test was conducted using the methods and conditions specified in this subpart (for transfer efficiency, e.g., ASTM Method D5066-91 or the EPA Protocol), then the 'methods and conditions' requirement of §63.3160(c)(1) is satisfied.

If no process or equipment changes have been made since the previous test or you can demonstrate that the previous test results reliably demonstrate compliance despite any changes, then the condition in §63.3160(c)(2) is satisfied.

If the required operating parameters were established in the previous test or sufficient data were collected in the previous test to establish the required operating parameters, then the condition in §63.3160(c)(3) is satisfied.

If the previous performance test was conducted under representative operating conditions (not during startup, shutdown, malfunction, or nonoperation), and the test records document representative coating operation conditions and representative capture system and add-on control device operating conditions (including flow rate and inlet concentration), then the representative-conditions requirement in §63.3164(a)(1)–(2) is satisfied.

checklist: Identify the date of the prior transfer efficiency test and the test report(s).
Verify the test method used for transfer efficiency (e.g., ASTM D5066-91 or the EPA Protocol) and cite the section of the test report showing the method. (See 40 CFR 63.3161(g))

Confirm the prior test was performed under representative operating conditions and that records document why the test conditions represented normal operation (not during startup, shutdown, malfunction, or nonoperation). (See 40 CFR 63.3164(a)(1))

Document emission capture system and add-on control device operating conditions during the prior test, including flow rates and control device inlet concentrations, and show they were representative of normal operation. (See 40 CFR 63.3164(a)(2))

Confirm whether any process or equipment changes have occurred at the primer-surfacer/topcoat operation since the December 2004 test; if changes occurred, prepare a technical demonstration that the old test results still reliably demonstrate compliance. (See 40 CFR 63.3160(c)(2))

Locate in the prior test report whether the required operating parameters were established or whether sufficient data were collected to establish operating limits; if not explicit, evaluate whether the data are sufficient to derive the parameters. (See 40 CFR 63.3160(c)(3))

Assemble all supporting records you would submit to the Administrator to request approval to use previous test results (test methods, raw data, process/equipment change documentation or reliability demonstration, and established operating parameters). (See 40 CFR 63.3160(c))

candidates.title: Subpart NNNNN

criteria.criterion: If you are required by § 63.9020(e) to monitor an operating parameter, then you must install, operate, and maintain each CMS and collect data as specified in § 63.9025(a)(1) through (6).

If you operate a scrubber control device, then you may request approval under § 63.8(f) to monitor parameters other than those specified in § 63.9020(e) only by submitting a monitoring plan that identifies the operating parameter, explains why it is appropriate to demonstrate ongoing compliance, and specifies the monitoring procedures as required in § 63.9025(b)(1) through (3).

If you use a caustic scrubber or a water scrubber to meet the emission limits in Table 1 to this subpart, then you must keep records of the daily average scrubber inlet liquid or recirculating liquid flow rate and the daily average scrubber effluent pH as specified in § 63.9035(b)(1) and (2).

If the affected source is operating, then you must monitor continuously (or collect data at all required intervals) at all times the source is operating except for specified monitor malfunctions, associated repairs, and required QA/QC activities, and you may not use data recorded during those malfunction or repair periods in data averages and compliance calculations as stated in § 63.9035(d) and (e).

candidates.title: Subpart CCC

criteria.criterion: If you are a steel pickling facility or acid regeneration plant and you use a wet scrubber as the emission control device, then you must install, operate, and maintain systems to measure and record the scrubber makeup water flow rate and, if required, recirculation water flow rate continuously and record at least once per shift while the scrubber is operating as required in § 63.1162(a)(2).

If you use an emission control device other than a wet scrubber, then you must install, operate, and maintain systems for measurement and recording of the appropriate operating parameters for that control device as required in § 63.1162(a)(3).
If you wish to implement alternative monitoring requirements, then you may develop and implement alternative monitoring only subject to approval by the Administrator as provided in § 63.1162(a)(6).

If a monitoring device is used, then it must be certified by the manufacturer to be accurate to within 5 percent and be calibrated at least annually per the manufacturer's instructions as required in § 63.1162(a)(5) and § 63.1162(b)(3).

candidates.title: Subpart SS

criteria.criterion: If you are the owner or operator of a regulated source required to monitor under this subpart, then the general monitoring requirements in § 63.996 apply to you (except as limited in § 63.996(a)(2) and (3)).

If you seek minor methodology changes or alternatives to the specified monitoring requirements, then the Administrator must specify or approve those changes or alternatives as provided in § 63.996(b)(1)(i) and (ii) or in paragraph (d) of § 63.996.

If you install and operate CPMS or other monitoring equipment, then that equipment must be installed, calibrated, maintained, and operated according to manufacturer's specifications or other written procedures that provide adequate assurance of accurate monitoring and must be operated consistent with good air pollution control practices as required in § 63.996(c)(1) and (2).

If you wish to monitor a different parameter than those listed for establishing proper operation ranges under paragraph (c)(6), then you may request approval to monitor a different parameter or set unique monitoring parameters as provided in § 63.996(d)(2).

If you establish a range for monitored parameters that indicates proper operation of the control or recovery device, then you must submit the information required in § 63.999(b)(3) in the Notification of Compliance Status or the operating permit application or amendment as referenced in § 63.996(c)(6).

checklist: Determine which Subpart(s) the affected source is subject to (Subpart NNNNN, Subpart CCC, Subpart SS) under the citations provided.

Verify whether the scrubber is being used specifically to meet emission limits under the applicable subpart (e.g., Table 1 to Subpart NNNNN or the emission limits under Subpart CCC) or is solely functioning as an acid recovery device not relied on for emission control.
If relying on the scrubber for emission control, identify whether the scrubber is a caustic scrubber, a water scrubber, or another type of control device.
Obtain the initial compliance test data used to establish operating limits (e.g., parameters, minimum flow rates, pH, or other values established during performance testing).

Decide which operating parameter(s) you propose to monitor as alternatives (e.g., scrubber base temperature, indicators of proper liquid flow) and document how each parameter demonstrates maintenance of control efficiency measured during the initial test.

Prepare a monitoring plan per § 63.9025(b)(1)–(3) (or § 63.9025(c) if not a scrubber): identify parameter, justify appropriateness, and specify monitoring procedures; include data collection frequency, averaging, and QA/QC procedures consistent with § 63.9025(a)(1)–(6).
For caustic or water scrubbers, compile records and instrumentation capability to log daily average inlet/recirculating flow rates and daily average effluent pH as required by § 63.9035(b).
Confirm whether your flow instrumentation are 'flow indicators' (not subject to Subpart SS requirements) or qualify as CPMS/monitoring devices subject to § 63.996 requirements.
Ensure proposed monitoring equipment can meet manufacturer certification and calibration frequency requirements (e.g., certified ±5% and at least annual calibration where applicable under § 63.1162).

Document continuous monitoring capability and data availability to meet required sampling frequency and valid-data requirements (e.g., four equally spaced periods per hour and 75% hourly coverage per 24-hr period as in § 63.9025(a)).

Prepare to submit the monitoring plan and request for alternative monitoring under § 63.8(f) to the Administrator, including any justification and procedural details requested by the applicable subpart.

Be prepared to show how data from the proposed parameters will be used in compliance demonstrations and how malfunction, repair, and QA/QC data exclusions will be handled consistent with § 63.9035(d)–(e) and relevant SS provisions.

candidates.title: Ethylene Oxide Emissions Standards for Sterilization Facilities

criteria.criterion: if you choose to demonstrate compliance using EtO continuous emission monitoring systems (EtO CEMS) then you must install and operate an EtO CEMS on each outlet for the control system in accordance with the requirements of this subpart and Performance Specification 19 (PS 19)

if an EtO CEMS is used to provide data under this subpart then the monitoring system must be capable of measuring EtO mass emissions (convertible to lb/hr), must be certified according to PS 19, and any additional flow/diluent/moisture monitors needed to convert concentration to lb/hr must be certified per part 75

if you intend to use an analyzer or sensor (either for performance testing or as part of a CEMS) then the instrumentation must be continuous (averaging time ≤ 1 minute), have the measurement range to properly quantify EtO including a method detection limit sufficiently below the applicable emission concentrations, and use EtO gaseous calibration standards that meet PS 19 criteria

if you use an EtO CEMS to provide compliance data then you must meet the ongoing QA/QC, certification/recertification, and audit requirements (daily/7-day calibration checks, quarterly gas audits/DSA/CGA/RAA, RATAs, LOD/interference/ME tests, recordkeeping, and electronic reporting) specified for EtO CEMS in Appendix A to this subpart

if your facility uses less than 100 lb/yr of EtO then you may instead elect to demonstrate continuous compliance via annual or periodic performance testing and/or parametric monitoring as allowed by this subpart, in lieu of operating EtO CEMS

checklist: Determine facility annual EtO use (is facility < 100 lb/yr?).
Decide whether you will demonstrate compliance using EtO CEMS or via performance testing/parametric approach (facility choice affects allowable monitors).
Identify the exact emission stream(s) to be monitored (aeration room exhaust: stack/duct ID, combined streams, or common stack configuration).
Confirm whether the proposed CEA ET-6200R U series is continuous with averaging time ≤ 1 minute and can produce sustained, timestamped concentration outputs suitable for hourly averaging.

Verify the ET-6200R measurement range and method detection limit (MDL) versus the EtO concentrations and the requirement that detection be at least an order of magnitude below the concentration equivalent of the applicable emission limit.

Obtain manufacturer or third-party test data demonstrating LOD (controlled and field SADL), interference testing, measurement error (ME) tests, response time, and linearity per PS 19/Appendix A requirements.

Confirm that the analyzer can be incorporated into a certified CEMS and that replacement/maintenance procedures allow meeting PS 19 certification and Appendix A recertification (e.g., ability to perform daily CD tests, 7-day CD, calibrations, dynamic spiking if used).
Verify availability of EtO gaseous cylinder calibration standards that meet PS 19 and how the analyzer will be calibrated (zero, mid, high) and audited (CGA, DSA) per § 63.365 and Appendix A.

Confirm capability to convert concentration (ppbv) to lb/hr via an approved flow measurement system (Part 75 certified flow monitor or otherwise required flow monitoring) and that the data acquisition system can calculate hourly averages and lb/hr per Appendix A procedures.

Confirm ability to perform and document required QA tests: quarterly RAA/RATA schedules, quarterly cylinder gas audits (CGA), dynamic spiking audits (DSA), interference tests, LOD tests, ME tests, and the ability to submit required records and electronic reports via CEDRI.

Document the representative sampling location(s) and ensure the probe/sample interface meets Appendix A and PS 19 extractive or in-situ requirements (probe orientation, sample line, heated line if needed).

Gather the vendor’s technical documentation showing measurement principle, potential interferences, range, response time, calibration procedures, maintenance procedures, and serial/model numbers to include in the monitoring plan and certification submittals.

Confirm whether you will use the device as a primary certified EtO CEMS, a redundant backup, a non-redundant backup, or a temporary like-kind replacement and verify which certification/QA tests apply (see Appendix A sections on backup systems and time limits).
Verify that stack gas flow, diluent gas, and moisture monitors needed to compute lb/hr are installed and certified per Part 75 (and meet the Part 75 QA schedules and grace period rules).

Confirm recordkeeping locations and retention capability for all required monitoring, certification, QA/QC, and reporting records for the periods specified in Appendix A (e.g., 5 years) and ability to produce required reporting fields (hourly concentrations in ppbv with required rounding, special codes, monitor IDs).

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants for Natural Gas Processing Plants (Subpart HH)

criteria.criterion: if a piece of ancillary equipment or a compressor is located at a natural gas processing plant and operates in VHAP service equal to or greater than 300 hours per calendar year, then it is subject to the equipment leak standards in this subpart

if the percent VHAP content of the process fluid that contacts or is contained in a piece of ancillary equipment or compressor can be reasonably expected never to exceed 10.0 percent by weight (determined using the procedures in § 63.772(a)(1)), then that piece of equipment is considered not in VHAP service

if determining the percent VHAP content for the purpose of § 63.772(a)(1), then use Method 18 of 40 CFR part 60, appendix A, or ASTM D6420-99 (2004) provided the provisions of paragraphs (a)(1)(ii)(A) through (D) of § 63.772 are followed
if a piece of ancillary equipment or compressor contains or contacts the field gas before the extraction of natural gas liquids, then it is in wet gas service

if any ancillary equipment and compressors contain or contact a fluid with a total VHAP concentration less than 10 percent by weight as determined according to § 63.772(a), then the owner or operator is exempt from the ancillary equipment and compressor equipment-leak requirements in paragraph (c)(3) of § 63.764

if an ancillary equipment item or compressor operates in VHAP service less than 300 hours per calendar year, then the owner or operator is exempt from the ancillary equipment and compressor equipment-leak requirements in paragraph (c)(3) of § 63.764

checklist: Confirm the facility is a natural gas processing plant as defined in 40 CFR 63.761 (i.e., engaged in extraction of NGL or fractionation of mixed NGL) and that the equipment in question is located at that plant

Identify which pieces of equipment are 'ancillary equipment' (pumps, pressure relief devices, sampling connection systems, open-ended valves, lines/valves/flanges/connectors) and which are compressors (per 40 CFR 63.761)
For each ancillary equipment item and compressor, determine whether it 'contains or contacts' field gas prior to NGL extraction (i.e., wet gas service) or contacts processed fluids
For each ancillary equipment item and compressor, document the number of hours per calendar year it operates in VHAP service to compare to the 300-hour threshold

Collect representative samples of the process fluids that contact or are contained in each piece of equipment and determine total VHAP weight percent using either Method 18 (40 CFR part 60, app. A) or ASTM D6420-99 (2004) following § 63.772(a)(1)(ii) conditions (target compounds per § 63.772(a)(1)(ii)(A); target concentration range per § 63.772(a)(1)(ii)(B); additional calibration/checks per § 63.772(a)(1)(ii)(C); and restriction in § 63.772(a)(1)(ii)(D))

If using ASTM D6420-99 (2004), ensure the target compound list and concentration range apply and document the additional system continuing calibration check for non‑Table 1.1 compounds as required by § 63.772(a)(1)(ii)(C)

Maintain records of the VHAP determinations, sampling dates, methods used, analytical reports, and the owner/operator’s rationale that VHAP can be reasonably expected never to exceed 10.0% by weight for each surveyed stream (per recordkeeping requirements referenced in subpart)

If claiming exemption based on VHAP < 10% or <300 hours of VHAP service, retain supporting calculations, sampling/analysis reports, and hours-of-service logs to demonstrate the exemption per § 63.764(e)(2)

If any equipment is determined to be in wet gas service or VHAP service ≥300 hours/yr and therefore potentially subject to § 63.769, verify compliance obligations and monitoring/repair schedules under § 63.769 and § 63.772 (e.g., monitoring frequency, Method 21 no-detect procedures, leak repair timelines)

candidates.title: Subpart A

criteria.criterion: if required to do performance testing by a relevant standard, then the owner or operator must perform such tests within 180 days of the compliance date for such source

if a force majeure is about to occur, occurs, or has occurred and may cause or caused a delay in testing beyond the regulatory deadline, then the owner or operator shall notify the Administrator in writing as soon as practicable and before the performance test deadline unless the initial force majeure or a subsequent force majeure event delays the notice

if asserting a claim of force majeure to delay a performance test, then the owner or operator shall provide a written description of the force majeure event, a rationale attributing the delay to the force majeure, describe measures taken or to be taken to minimize the delay, and identify a date by which the owner or operator proposes to conduct the performance test
if an extension to the performance test deadline is requested due to force majeure, then the decision to grant an extension is solely within the discretion of the Administrator
if an extension of the performance test deadline has not been approved by the Administrator, then the owner or operator remains strictly subject to the requirements of this part

if the owner or operator is unable to conduct the performance test on the date specified in the notification due to unforeseeable circumstances beyond his or her control, then the owner or operator must notify the Administrator as soon as practicable and without delay prior to the scheduled performance test date

candidates.title: Subpart EEEEE

criteria.criterion: if subject to the iron and steel foundry standard in this subpart, then you must conduct a performance test no later than 180 calendar days after the compliance date specified in § 63.7683 to demonstrate initial compliance with each emissions limitation that applies to you

if initial compliance for a work practice standard or an operation and maintenance requirement in this subpart is not demonstrated using a performance test, then you must demonstrate initial compliance no later than 30 calendar days after the compliance date

if conducting a performance test under this subpart, then the performance test must be conducted under conditions representative of normal operations and tests may not be conducted during periods of malfunction

candidates.title: Subpart ZZZZZ

criteria.criterion: if a metal melting furnace or building housing foundry operations is subject to an emissions limit in this subpart and must demonstrate initial compliance, then you must conduct a performance test within 180 days of your compliance date and report the results in your notification of compliance status

if you own or operate an existing iron and steel foundry and have a prior performance test conducted within the last 5 years using the methods and procedures specified in this subpart and either no process changes have been made since the test or you can demonstrate the prior test reliably demonstrates compliance despite changes, then you may choose to submit the prior performance test results instead of conducting a new test provided you notify the Administrator of your intent no later than 60 days after your compliance date

if you are required to electronically submit a report through CEDRI and a force majeure event is about to occur, occurs, or has occurred (including lingering effects) within the period beginning five business days prior to the submission due date that prevents timely electronic reporting, then you must notify the Administrator in writing as soon as possible and provide a written description of the force majeure event, a rationale attributing the delay to the force majeure, measures taken or to be taken to minimize the delay, and the date by which you propose to report

if you submit a force majeure claim for failure to timely comply with an electronic reporting requirement under this subpart, then the decision to accept the claim and allow an extension to the submittal deadline is solely within the discretion of the Administrator

checklist: Identify the applicable compliance date for your facility under the relevant standard (e.g., § 63.7683 or § 63.10895) and calculate the 180-day performance test deadline and, if applicable, the 30-day work-practice/OM deadline
List the specific emission units (e.g., Phase 1 melting furnace, other metal melting furnaces) and the emissions limits or work-practice standards that trigger an initial performance test

Confirm whether a prior performance test for the same unit exists within the last 5 years, whether it used the methods/procedures in the subpart, and whether any process changes occurred since that test

Document the exact dates and facts of the furnace malfunctions and the labor strike, including when management and responsible personnel first knew (or should have known) the events might delay testing

Determine whether the events prevented scheduling or conducting a performance test (i.e., were they beyond the facility's control and did they make testing infeasible) versus constituting a period of 'malfunction' for which tests must not be conducted

Assemble evidence and contemporaneous records showing measures taken to minimize delay (repairs, rescheduling efforts, contractor availability, safety assessments, steps to resume testing) and a proposed date to perform the test as soon as practicable

If relying on force majeure for electronic submissions, verify whether the filing was required via CEDRI/CDX and whether the force majeure event occurred within the 5 business day window before the submission due date

Prepare the written notification to the Administrator (or delegated State authority if applicable) that includes: description of the force majeure event, rationale attributing the delay to it, measures taken/to be taken to minimize delay, and the proposed date for conducting the performance test or submitting the report

Confirm whether the facility has submitted the 60-calendar-day advance notification of intent to conduct a performance test (or timely rescheduled-test notice per § 63.7(b)(2)) and retain copies of all correspondence

Record the date the performance test is actually completed and prepare to submit the performance test results and the notification of compliance status within the applicable reporting timeframe (e.g., 60 days after completion) via the required electronic system or via the CBI procedures if claiming confidentiality (noting emissions data is not protected)
Retain all supporting records described above and all other required subpart records for at least 5 years (with most recent 2 years onsite) as required by § 63.10899(a)

judge_text: {"score":2,"reason":"EPA’s key reason—that the furnace malfunctions and labor strike qualify as a force majeure under MACT Subpart A—is reflected in the provided criteria (40 CFR 63.7(a)(4) force majeure notification/content/discretion and 40 CFR 63.7(b)(2) for unforeseeable circumstances), so the notes’ rationale is captured."}

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants for Cellulose Products Manufacturing (Subpart UUUU)

criteria.criterion: if you own or operate a cellulose products manufacturing operation located at a major source of HAP emissions then this subpart applies to you

if a CMS is required by this subpart then you must develop and make available a site-specific monitoring plan that addresses installation location, performance and equipment specifications for the analyzer and data system, and performance evaluation procedures including calibrations

if you use a CEMS to measure hydrogen sulfide then the CEMS must be installed, operated, and maintained according to PS-7 of 40 CFR part 60, appendix B and must undergo performance evaluation as required in § 63.8 and this subpart
if you use a CEMS that uses gas chromatography to measure organic HAP then the CEMS must be installed, operated, and maintained according to PS-9 of 40 CFR part 60, appendix B

if you operate any CMS for this subpart then you must conduct a performance evaluation of each CMS in accordance with your site-specific monitoring plan and operate and maintain the CMS in continuous operation according to that plan

candidates.title: General Provisions (Subpart A)

criteria.criterion: if you wish to use an alternative monitoring procedure (minor, intermediate, or major change) to any monitoring requirement then you must apply to the Administrator and include the information required for an alternative monitoring application and, if the alternative will be used as the performance test method, submit the application at least 60 days before the performance evaluation

if you submit an application to use an alternative monitoring method then the application must include a description of the proposed alternative addressing the four elements of monitoring and a performance evaluation test plan with data quality objectives and QA procedures
if the Administrator approves an alternative monitoring method then you must continue to use the approved alternative monitoring method until the Administrator approves another monitoring method

if a CMS is not a CPMS then you must check zero and high-level calibration drift at least once daily and adjust whenever the 24-hour zero (low-level) drift exceeds two times the limits of the applicable performance specification(s)

if a CMS will be used to demonstrate compliance then you must conduct the CMS performance evaluation according to the applicable performance specification and the site-specific performance evaluation plan (and notify the Administrator of the performance evaluation per § 63.8)

checklist: Confirm that your facility is a cellulose products manufacturing operation (cellulose food casing) and is a major source of HAP (single HAP ≥ 10 tpy or total HAP ≥ 25 tpy) per 40 CFR 63.5485(b)
Identify whether Baseline-MOCON Model 8900 will function as a CEMS, COMS, or CPMS for the regulated parameter(s) (H2S and CS2/total sulfide) at the affected emission point(s)

Determine whether the existing site-specific monitoring plan for Subpart UUUU specifies a CEMS performance specification (e.g., PS-7 for H2S or PS-9 for GC) that the new instrument must meet, or whether the plan allows an approved alternative

If the new instrument does not meet the referenced performance specification(s), verify whether you will prepare and submit an alternative monitoring application to the Administrator and whether that application will be used as the performance test method (if so, submit ≥ 60 days before the performance evaluation)

Assemble a site-specific performance evaluation test plan that includes evaluation objectives, schedule, data quality objectives, internal and external QA, and procedures for initial and subsequent calibration, calibration drift determination, preventive maintenance, data recording, and accuracy audits (per § 63.8(e)(3) and (c)(2)(i)-(v))

Verify the Baseline-MOCON 8900's calibration and accuracy characteristics (including NIST traceability where required) and whether those characteristics meet any accuracy/traceability requirements in the site plan or Subpart A (e.g., CPMS validation device accuracy requirements)

Confirm instrument cycle time and data recording frequency meet the relevant averaging and minimum-data requirements (CEMS: one cycle per 15-minute period and hourly averages from ≥4 equally spaced points; data availability ≥75% over averaging period) per § 63.5545(e)(3)-(4) and § 63.8(g)(2)
Plan for daily or required frequency calibration drift checks and recordkeeping for zero/high-level drift and corrective action documentation per § 63.8(c)(6)
Check whether any previously approved alternative monitoring method exists for your affected source and whether approval conditions require continued use or periodic reevaluation per § 63.8(f)(5)

Determine whether the alternative monitoring application must include demonstration of a definite and consistent relationship between the alternative instrument measurements and the specified method (and prepare such comparative data if requested) per § 63.8(f)(2)(viii)
Decide whether the alternative method will be used during a performance test; if yes, schedule the performance evaluation and Administrator notification per § 63.8(e)(2) and (f)(4)(i)
Prepare to exclude monitoring data recorded during monitor malfunctions, QA activities, calibrations, and periods of no flow from data averages and reporting per § 63.5560(c) and § 63.8(g)(5)

However it does not explicitly state the EPA’s key point that a full linearity-type (multi‑point) calibration is still required; the answer refers generally to calibrations, performance specs (PS‑7/PS‑9) and drift checks but does not clearly require full linearity calibrations as noted in the EPA letter."}

candidates.title: Performance testing requirements

criteria.criterion: if required to do performance testing by a relevant standard and no waiver is obtained under this section or the conditions of paragraph (c)(3)(ii)(B) apply then the owner or operator must perform such tests within 180 days of the compliance date for such source
if a waiver of a performance testing requirement has not been granted by the Administrator then the owner or operator of an affected source remains subject to the requirements of this section

if an application for a waiver of a performance test is submitted then the application shall include information justifying the owner or operator's request such as the technical or economic infeasibility, or the impracticality, of the affected source performing the required test

candidates.title: Performance test methods and procedures to determine initial compliance

criteria.criterion: if multiple emission points are vented to one common control device to meet the requirements of § 63.703 then only one performance test is required to demonstrate initial compliance for that group of emission points

if affected HAP emission points are located in an area with other gaseous emission sources not affected by this subpart then during a performance test the owner or operator must isolate the affected HAP emission points from all other gaseous emission points by either building a temporary total enclosure or shutting down all gaseous emission points not affected
if the requirements of § 63.7(e)(2)(iv) or § 63.7(h) are met then the owner or operator is not required to conduct an initial performance test

candidates.title: Extension of compliance, and performance test, monitoring, recordkeeping and reporting waivers and alternatives

criteria.criterion: if, in the Administrator's judgment, the source is meeting the relevant standard(s) on a continuous basis, or the source is being operated under an extension of compliance, or the owner or operator has requested an extension of compliance and the Administrator is still considering that request then individual performance tests may be waived upon written application to the Administrator

if an application for a waiver of a performance test is made then the application shall be submitted at least 60 days before the performance test if a site-specific test plan is not submitted and shall include information justifying the request such as the technical or economic infeasibility, or the impracticality, of the affected source performing the required test

if the Administrator approves or denies an extension of compliance, or approves or disapproves a site-specific test plan, or makes a determination of compliance or suitable progress towards compliance then the Administrator will approve or deny a request for a waiver of a performance test

checklist: Identify which specific NESHAP relevant standard(s) require performance testing for the argon stir stations (which subpart and which §63.xxx provisions apply at your facility).

Confirm whether the argon stir stations and the ladle metallurgical furnace (LMF) both vent to the same baghouse (common control device) and document the ducting and actual inlet(s) and outlet(s) to the baghouse.
Determine whether the baghouse exhaust sampling location(s) are at the outlet of the control device and prior to any release to the atmosphere (sampling port availability per applicable test method).
Verify whether prior performance tests were conducted on the baghouse or affected emission points within the past 5 years and whether any process changes occurred since those tests.

Assess whether you can isolate the argon stir emissions from other gaseous/particulate emission sources during testing by (a) constructing a temporary total enclosure around the affected emission point(s) or (b) shutting down all gaseous/particulate emission points not subject to the same standard for the duration of the performance test, and document feasibility.

If isolation by shutdown is not feasible, document why testing of the argon stir emissions cannot be conducted because of interference from LMF/baghouse influent (measurements, stack tests, emissions data showing confounding sources).

Assemble technical justification demonstrating impracticality (or technical/economic infeasibility) of performing the required test—include monitoring data, process schedules, baghouse influent composition and flow data, and any prior test data showing confounding influences.

Prepare to submit a written waiver application (including the justification above) at least 60 days before the scheduled performance test date if you are not submitting a site-specific test plan, and retain records to show submission timing.

If seeking a waiver based on continuous compliance, compile and be ready to provide evidence of continuous compliance with the relevant standard(s) (operational records, monitoring, maintenance logs, previous test results).

Determine whether you can instead demonstrate compliance by grouping emission points to a single performance test for the common control device (per the relevant subpart's allowance) and prepare test plan accordingly if applicable.

Confirm whether alternative test methods or a site-specific test plan could address the interference and whether you will request Administrator approval for alternative methods (see Method 301 validation and §63.7(f) process if applicable).

Be prepared to retain and provide performance test records for the required retention period and to submit test results or waiver decision documentation to the Administrator or permitting authority per the applicable subpart procedures.

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants for Hydrochloric Acid Production

criteria.criterion: If you own or operate an HCl production facility that produces a liquid HCl product at a concentration of 30 weight percent or greater during its normal operations and is located at, or is part of, a major source of HAP then subject
If an HCl production facility is also subject to any NESHAP listed in paragraphs (b)(1) through (5) of § 63.8985 then not subject

If the HCl production facility is located following the incineration of chlorinated waste gas streams, waste liquids, or solid wastes and emissions are subject to § 63.113(c) (subpart G) then not subject
If the HCl production facility produces HCl through the direct synthesis of hydrogen and chlorine and is part of a chlor-alkali facility then not subject
If the HCl production facility is a research and development facility then not subject

If all gaseous streams containing HCl and Cl2 from HCl process vents, storage tanks, and transfer operations are recycled or routed to another process for process purpose prior to discharge to the atmosphere then not subject

If you use a caustic scrubber control device or water scrubber control device and you conduct a performance test then subject to establishing operating limits that include a minimum value for scrubber inlet liquid or recirculating liquid flow rate based on values measured during the performance test and minimum and maximum values for scrubber effluent pH based on values measured during the performance test

If you use a caustic scrubber or a water scrubber to meet the emission limits in Table 1 to this subpart then subject to keeping records of daily average scrubber inlet liquid or recirculating liquid flow rate and daily average scrubber effluent pH

If you intend to monitor parameters other than those specified in § 63.9020(e) for a scrubber then subject to requesting approval in accordance with § 63.8(f) and submitting a monitoring plan that meets the requirements of § 63.9025(b)

If you are required to conduct a performance test (per Table 3 to this subpart) then subject to developing and following a site-specific test plan per § 63.7(c)(2) and conducting tests under representative/normal operations as specified in § 63.9020(a)

checklist: Verify the typical liquid HCl product concentration during normal operations (is it ≥ 30 weight percent?).
Verify whether the facility is a major source of HAP (potential to emit ≥ 10 t/yr of a single HAP or ≥ 25 t/yr combined HAP).
Verify whether the facility is part of a chlor-alkali operation producing HCl by direct synthesis (which would exclude the facility).
Verify whether the HCl production facility is subject to any other listed NESHAPs (e.g., subparts S, CCC, MMM, SS, or GGG) that would preclude applicability under this subpart.
Verify whether all gaseous streams containing HCl/Cl2 are recycled or routed to another process prior to atmospheric discharge.
Confirm whether the scrubber in question is a caustic scrubber control device as defined in the subpart.

If a performance test has been or will be conducted: collect the site-specific test plan, the measured scrubber inlet/recirculating liquid flow rates and scrubber effluent pH values from each test run, and documentation that test conditions represent normal operations.

If proposing alternative monitoring/operating parameters (e.g., 65 gpm minimum recirculation, ≥2 wt% caustic), prepare and be ready to submit a monitoring plan under § 63.8(f) that (a) identifies the parameter to be monitored, (b) explains why it demonstrates ongoing compliance, and (c) specifies the monitoring procedures (per § 63.9025(b)(1)–(3)).

Be prepared to operate and document a continuous monitoring system per § 63.9025(a): collect data at least four equally spaced periods each hour, achieve ≥75% data availability per 24-hour period, calculate hourly and daily averages as required.

Assemble recordkeeping to retain daily average scrubber inlet/recirculating flow and daily average scrubber effluent pH, and records of inspections/calibrations/validation checks per the site-specific monitoring plan.

If relying on a design evaluation in lieu of a performance test for HCl storage/transfer operations, prepare documentation addressing vent composition, liquid-to-vapor ratio, scrubbing liquid flow rate and concentration, temperature, reaction kinetics, and scrubber internals (ASTM E224 may be used to determine HCl concentration as needed).

The candidate criteria and checklist explicitly cite the need for performance testing to establish operating limits (§63.9020), the need to conduct tests under representative/normal operations (§63.9020(a)), and the requirement to request approval and submit a monitoring plan (§63.8(f), §63.9025(b)). Those items capture the key reason given by EPA."}

candidates.title: Subpart R (Bulk gasoline terminals)

criteria.criterion: If a bulk gasoline terminal is subject to the provisions in § 63.422(b)(1) and uses a thermal oxidation system to control displaced gasoline vapors, then a continuous parameter monitoring system (CPMS) capable of measuring temperature must be installed in the firebox or in the ductwork immediately downstream from the firebox in a position before any substantial heat exchange occurs.

If an owner or operator proposes to monitor an operating parameter other than those listed in paragraphs (a)(1)–(4) of § 63.427, then the alternative parameter will be allowed only upon demonstrating to the Administrator's satisfaction that the alternative parameter demonstrates continuous compliance with the emission standard in § 63.422(b) or § 60.112b(a)(3)(ii).

If an alternative operating parameter is approved by the Administrator pursuant to § 63.427(a)(5), then the owner or operator must operate the vapor processing system in a manner not to exceed or not to go below, as appropriate, the approved alternative operating parameter value established using the procedures in § 63.425(b).

candidates.title: Subpart BBBBBB (Bulk gasoline terminals - monitoring and testing)

criteria.criterion: If a bulk gasoline terminal subject to this subpart uses a thermal oxidation system, then the owner or operator must install a CPMS capable of measuring temperature in the firebox or in the ductwork immediately downstream from the firebox in a position before any substantial heat exchange occurs.

If a facility uses a thermal oxidation system, then as an alternative to installing a combustion-zone temperature CPMS the owner or operator may monitor the presence of the thermal oxidation pilot flame using a heat-sensing device (e.g., ultraviolet beam sensor or thermocouple) installed in proximity to the pilot light that sends a positive parameter value when the pilot is on and a negative parameter value when the pilot is off.

If pilot-flame monitoring is used as the alternative per § 63.11092(b)(1)(iii)(B)(1), then the owner or operator must develop and submit to the Administrator a monitoring and inspection plan that, at a minimum, demonstrates that the thermal oxidation system is equipped to automatically prevent gasoline loading when the pilot flame is absent and describes verification, preventive maintenance, and recordkeeping procedures (including verification of assist-air blower and vapor line valve operation, semi-annual preventive maintenance, and documenting alarm/shutdown activations and corrective actions).

If an owner or operator proposes monitoring an alternative operating parameter other than those listed in paragraphs (b)(1)(i)–(iii) of § 63.11092, then the alternative parameter will be allowed only upon demonstrating to the Administrator's satisfaction that the alternative parameter demonstrates continuous compliance with the emission standard in § 63.11088(a).

If a thermal oxidation system is monitored with a CPMS measuring combustion-zone temperature and is complying with the emission limitations in item 1 of table 3 to this subpart, then the owner or operator must maintain the 3-hour rolling average combustion zone temperature when gasoline cargo tanks are being loaded at or above the operating limit set during the most recent performance test, with valid operating data excluding periods when no liquid product is being loaded.

candidates.title: Subpart G (Process vent provisions)

criteria.criterion: If an owner or operator of a process vent uses an incinerator (non-catalytic) to comply with § 63.113(a), then a temperature monitoring device equipped with a continuous recorder must be installed in the firebox or in the ductwork immediately downstream of the firebox in a position before any substantial heat exchange occurs.

If an owner or operator of a process vent uses a flare to comply with § 63.113(a) (except as specified in § 63.108(a)), then a device capable of continuously detecting the presence of a pilot flame (e.g., thermocouple, ultraviolet beam sensor, or infrared sensor) is required.

If an owner or operator seeks to monitor parameters other than those specified in § 63.114(a) for a combustion or recovery device, then the owner or operator must request approval of the alternative monitoring parameter according to the procedures in § 63.151(f) or § 63.152(e) of this subpart.

checklist: Verify whether the facility is a bulk gasoline terminal subject to § 63.422(b)(1) or to the applicability provisions of Subpart BBBBBB (e.g., item references in Table 2/3 of Subpart BBBBBB).
Identify which control device is used for vapor control at the loading rack (thermal oxidation system/incinerator, flare, carbon adsorption, refrigerated condenser, or other).

If a thermal oxidation unit is used, confirm whether the current monitoring is a firebox/combustion-zone temperature CPMS or a pilot-flame detection device, and whether the pilot device provides a continuous positive/negative signal.

Confirm whether a performance test has been conducted and whether combustion-zone temperature data from that test exist to establish an operating limit (e.g., per § 63.11092(e)(1)/(2) and § 63.427 procedures).
Determine whether the pilot-flame monitoring approach (if proposed) includes an automatic interlock or procedure that prevents gasoline loading when the pilot is absent.

Prepare or confirm ability to provide a monitoring and inspection plan (including daily verification of assist-air blower and vapor line valve operation, semi-annual preventive maintenance, alarm/shutdown log procedures, and documentation of corrective actions) for submittal to the Administrator if using pilot-flame monitoring as an alternative.
Check whether any State, local, or tribal permit or enforceable requirement already specifies an approved monitored operating parameter or limits that could affect allowable alternatives.

Document whether the facility will seek Administrator approval (and under which cited provision: § 63.427(a)(5), § 63.11092(b)(1)(iv), or the approval procedures referenced in § 63.114(c)) and assemble supporting engineering/monitoring data demonstrating continuous compliance with the applicable emission standard.

candidates.title: Subpart CCC (steel pickling facilities and acid regeneration plants)

criteria.criterion: if you are the owner or operator of a new, reconstructed, or existing steel pickling facility or acid regeneration plant, then Subpart CCC allows you to develop and implement alternative monitoring requirements only with approval by the Administrator

if you use a wet scrubber as the emission control device at such a facility, then Subpart CCC requires continuous measurement and recording of scrubber makeup water flow rate (and recirculation flow rate if required) with excursions below minimum performance-test-established values triggering corrective action

candidates.title: Subpart NNNNN (monitoring installation, operation, and maintenance requirements)

criteria.criterion: if you use a scrubber control device and want to monitor parameters other than those specified in §63.9020(e), then you may request approval under §63.8(f) by submitting a monitoring plan that identifies the operating parameter, explains why it demonstrates ongoing compliance, and specifies monitoring procedures

if you propose alternative (non-continuous) monitoring parameters or reduced frequency, then your request must include descriptions of the affected source and parameters, methods to demonstrate the parameter's suitability, proposed monitoring/recording/reporting frequency and rationale, supporting calculations, and proposed averaging time
if a continuous monitoring system is used or required, then data collection, averaging, and data validity must meet the CMS operation and data requirements specified in §63.9025(a)(1)–(6)

candidates.title: Subpart SS (general monitoring requirements for control and recovery devices)

criteria.criterion: if you are required to monitor under this subpart and you seek alternatives to the continuous operating parameter monitoring and recordkeeping provisions, then you may request approval to use alternatives as specified in §63.996(d)(1)

if you want to monitor a different parameter than those listed for establishing proper operation of the control device, then you may request approval to monitor a different parameter or to set unique monitoring parameters as specified in §63.996(d)(2)

checklist: Identify the permitting authority/Administrator contact and any state/local permit requirements that may affect approval in South Carolina
