candidates.title: Subpart VVVV

criteria.criterion: if you have an enclosure in the emission capture system then you must install a device to measure and record either the flow rate or the static pressure in the duct from each enclosure to the add-on control device

if you install a flow measurement device then it must be located to provide a representative flow measurement in the duct between each enclosure and the add-on control device and must meet the sensor siting, calibration, and inspection requirements

if you install a pressure measurement device then it must be located to provide a representative measurement of the pressure drop across each enclosure opening and/or the duct static pressure between the enclosure and control device and you must perform daily pressure tap checks and the specified transducer/manometer calibration checks

if your capture device is not part of a permanent total enclosure then you must establish an operating limit for either the gas volumetric flow rate or duct static pressure and also establish an operating limit for pressure drop across at least one opening in each enclosure

if you perform the emission test required by § 63.5716 then you must monitor and record either the gas volumetric flow rate or duct static pressure at least once every 15 minutes during each of the three test runs and the average of the three test runs is the minimum operating limit

if you operate a continuous parameter monitoring system then it must complete a minimum of one cycle of operation for each successive 15-minute period and produce valid data for at least 90 percent of the hours during which the process operated

candidates.title: Subpart UUU

criteria.criterion: if you want to monitor parameters other than those required in this subpart then you must request approval from the Administrator to monitor alternative process or control device operating parameters

if you request approval to monitor alternative parameters then you must submit a request that includes a description of each affected source and the parameter(s) to be monitored, the methods and procedures to demonstrate that the parameter indicates continuous compliance, the frequency and content of monitoring, supporting calculations, and the averaging time

if you use an approved alternative procedure for determining gas flow rate for a regenerator you must install and operate continuous parameter monitoring for hourly average volumetric air flow and gas temperature and calculate the hourly average actual exhaust gas flow rate using the applicable equations

candidates.title: Subpart QQQQQ

criteria.criterion: if you use a control technique other than a solvent recovery system and/or solvent substitution then you may request approval to use an alternative method of demonstrating compliance with the emission limitations in § 63.9500(a) and (b)

if you request approval to use an alternative method of demonstrating compliance then you must submit a description of the proposed testing, monitoring, recordkeeping, reporting, and the proposed basis for demonstrating compliance including test plans or prior test results and a monitoring plan with performance specifications and quality assurance procedures
if you propose to use an alternative method of demonstrating compliance then you must not begin use of the alternative method until approval is granted by the Administrator

checklist: Determine whether each emission capture enclosure qualifies as a permanent total enclosure (PTE) per Method 204 (appendix M to 40 CFR part 51)
Confirm the add-on control device type (RTO/thermal oxidizer) and the physical duct(s) connecting each enclosure to the RTO
Document current monitoring: whether facial velocity through natural-draft openings and/or pressure drop across openings is being measured, and the location of existing sensors and taps
Verify ability to install and continuously log duct static pressure between each enclosure and the RTO and to measure pressure drop across at least one enclosure opening
Plan to perform the required emission test (per § 63.5716) and confirm capability to record static pressure or flow at least once every 15 minutes during each of three test runs
Confirm continuous parameter monitoring system can complete ≥1 cycle per 15-minute period, provide ≥4 cycles for a valid hour, and produce valid data for ≥90% of operating hours

Prepare a monitoring plan with: description of control technique, test results demonstrating compliance, proposed operating limit(s) based on test results, monitored parameters and monitoring frequency, and QA/QC procedures (per 40 CFR 63.1573(f) and 63.9570(c))

Establish sensor siting, daily pressure-tap checks, calibration schedules (monthly/quarterly/semiannual as required), and inspection procedures per the sensor requirements in 40 CFR 63.5725(f)(3) and (f)(4)

Identify the approving authority (EPA Administrator vs delegated state/local authority for Ohio) and confirm application submission route and that no alternative monitoring begins before Administrator approval

Assemble records and procedures needed for ongoing compliance: records of calibrations, daily checks, monitoring data averages (3‑hour averages), and semiannual/annual reports or deviations per the applicable subpart requirements

judge_text: {"score":2,"reason":"The answer includes the key regulatory bases cited by EPA: Subpart VVVV authorizes/sets requirements for using duct static pressure monitoring (and related sensor, calibration, and testing requirements), and Subparts UUU/QQQQQ (and the checklist) address requesting and obtaining Administrator approval and the required monitoring plan/QA to demonstrate continuous compliance with PTE requirements. Those criteria capture the EPA Notes rationale that an alternative monitoring method can be approved to demonstrate continuous compliance."}

candidates.title: Subpart HH (Equipment leak standards for natural gas processing plants)

criteria.criterion: if ancillary equipment is located at a natural gas processing plant and operates in VHAP service equal to or greater than 300 hours per calendar year then the equipment leak standards in §63.769 apply to that ancillary equipment and compressors

if ancillary equipment or compressors are subject to and controlled under subpart H of this part or are subject to and controlled under 40 CFR part 60, subpart OOOO then the equipment leak standards in §63.769 do not apply to those ancillary equipment and compressors

if a piece of ancillary equipment or a compressor contains or contacts a fluid whose total VHAP concentration can be reasonably expected never to exceed 10.0 percent by weight then that piece of equipment is not in VHAP service for purposes of determining applicability under this subpart

if a potential leak interface must be determined to operate with no detectable emissions then the no detectable emissions test procedure shall be conducted in accordance with Method 21 (40 CFR part 60, appendix A) as specified in §63.772(c)

if pumps in VHAP service, valves in gas/vapor and light liquid service, or pressure relief devices in gas/vapor service are located at a nonfractionating plant that does not have the design capacity to process 283,000 standard cubic meters per day or more of field gas then those pieces are exempt from the routine monitoring requirements and paragraphs (c)(1) through (3) of §63.769

candidates.title: Subpart A (Control device and alternative work practice requirements)

criteria.criterion: if the applicable subpart requires monitoring of equipment with a 40 CFR part 60, appendix A-7, Method 21 monitor then the owner or operator may choose to use the alternative work practice using an optical gas imaging instrument instead of the Method 21 monitor provided the requirements of §63.11(c) and §63.11(d) are met

if the alternative work practice is used to identify leaks then the regulated equipment selected for this work practice must also be monitored annually using a 40 CFR part 60, appendix A-7, Method 21 monitor and the annual Method 21 results must be retained and (if required) submitted as specified in §63.11(d)(7) and §63.11(e)(4)(vii)

if the alternative work practice is used then the optical gas imaging instrument and program must meet the instrument specifications, daily instrument check, leak survey procedure, detection sensitivity selection, rescreening-after-repair, and video recordkeeping requirements specified in §63.11(e)

checklist: Identify each piece of equipment you consider 'ancillary equipment' per the definition in 40 CFR 63.761 (e.g., pumps, pressure relief devices, sampling connection systems, open-ended lines, valves, flanges, connectors)
Confirm the facility is a natural gas processing plant (i.e., engaged in extraction of NGLs or fractionation prior to custody transfer) as used in Subpart HH definitions (40 CFR 63.761)

For each ancillary piece, determine whether the fluid it contains or contacts has total VHAP concentration ≥ 10.0 wt% (or can be reasonably expected never to exceed 10.0 wt%) by testing per 40 CFR 63.772(a)(1) (Method 18 or ASTM D6420-99 (2004))

For each ancillary piece determined to be in VHAP service, document the number of hours per calendar year it operates in VHAP service to determine if it is ≥ 300 hours/year (threshold in 40 CFR 63.769(a))
Verify whether any ancillary equipment or compressors are already subject to and controlled under subpart H or 40 CFR part 60, subpart OOOO (if yes, §63.769 does not apply) per 40 CFR 63.769(b)

If equipment contacts glycol or glycol mixtures, document whether that glycol is used in a glycol dehydration unit or merely as a cooling jacket fluid (i.e., whether it contacts field gas or is part of a glycol dehydration unit per 40 CFR 63.761 and 63.772 definitions)

If the plant is a nonfractionating plant, determine the plant's design capacity to process field gas to see if it is less than 283,000 standard cubic meters per day to evaluate the exemptions in 40 CFR 63.769(c)(5)

If you intend to rely on a 'no detectable emissions' determination, confirm ability to perform Method 21 instrument monitoring consistent with the performance, calibration, and calibration gas requirements in 40 CFR 63.772(c)

If you intend to use the alternative work practice (optical gas imaging) in lieu of Method 21, prepare documentation of equipment/processes/facilities to be included, select the detection sensitivity from Table 1 to subpart A, and prepare to meet the §63.11(e) requirements (daily instrument check with calculated mass flow, video records with date/time stamps, detection sensitivity level, rescreening after repair, and 5-year record retention)

If using the alternative work practice, plan to conduct and retain results of the required annual Method 21 screening of the regulated equipment as specified in 40 CFR 63.11(d)(7) and 63.11(e)(4)(vii)

Maintain records demonstrating compliance with the inspection/repair schedules in §63.773(c) if Subpart HH inspection/monitoring applies (e.g., repair attempts within 5 days, completed within 15 days, or documented delay justification during shutdown)

candidates.title: Subpart LLLLL

criteria.criterion: if you are required to conduct a performance test to demonstrate compliance with Subpart LLLLL then you must notify the Administrator of your intention to conduct the performance test at least 60 calendar days before the performance test is scheduled to begin
if you are an existing affected source subject to Subpart LLLLL then you must conduct initial performance tests no later than 180 days after the compliance date specified for your source

if you intend to use results of a previously-conducted emission test in lieu of an initial performance test then you must demonstrate to the Administrator that (1) no changes have been made to the process since the prior test, (2) the operating conditions and test methods conform to this subpart, (3) the control device and process parameter values from the prior test will be used to demonstrate continuous compliance, and (4) the prior test was completed within the last 60 months

if you conduct an initial compliance demonstration (including a performance test) then you must submit a Notification of Compliance Status containing the performance test results before the close of business on the 60th calendar day following completion of the performance test

candidates.title: Subpart A (General Provisions)

criteria.criterion: if you are required to do performance testing by a relevant standard then you must perform the required tests within 180 days of the compliance date for the source unless a waiver of performance testing is obtained or other exceptions in §63.7(a) apply

if you are required to conduct a performance test then you must notify the Administrator in writing of your intention to conduct the performance test at least 60 calendar days before the performance test is initially scheduled to begin

if a force majeure is about to occur, occurs, or has occurred and you intend to assert a claim to delay testing beyond the regulatory deadline then you must notify the Administrator in writing as soon as practicable (and before the performance test deadline unless delayed by the force majeure), provide a written description and rationale, describe measures to minimize the delay, and identify a proposed test date, and the Administrator may grant or deny an extension at their discretion

if you request a waiver of an initial performance test then your application (including justification such as technical or economic infeasibility) must be submitted at least 60 days before the performance test if the site-specific test plan is not submitted with the waiver request

if you wish to change an applicable time period or postmark deadline (for example the 60-day notification) then you must request the adjustment in writing as soon as practicable and the Administrator may approve an adjustment (and will notify approval or disapproval within 15 calendar days after receiving sufficient information)

if you intend to use an alternative test method in place of the method specified in the relevant standard then you must notify the Administrator of the intention to use the alternative method at least 60 days before the performance test, validate the method using Method 301, and submit the Method 301 validation results and justification with the notification

checklist: Determine whether your facility is an affected source subject to Subpart LLLLL (asphalt roofing manufacturing) and whether Subpart LLLLL requires an initial performance test for your emission points
Identify the compliance date for your source (or startup date) to calculate the 180-day deadline for initial testing under §63.8686(a)
Choose and record the planned performance test start date (day 0) and confirm whether you can provide ≥60 calendar days advance notice to the Administrator

Confirm whether you will rely on a previously-conducted emission test: record the prior test completion date (must be within 60 months), document that no process or control changes occurred, and verify test methods and operating conditions match Subpart LLLLL requirements
Decide whether you will submit a site-specific test plan and whether you will request EPA/state review (if so, plan to submit concurrently with the 60-day notification)

If you plan to request a waiver of the initial performance test, prepare the waiver application documentation (technical and/or economic justification) and be ready to submit it ≥60 days before the scheduled test if not submitting the site-specific test plan

If you anticipate claiming force majeure to move the test into your high-volume period, document the force majeure rationale, timeline, and measures to minimize delay and be prepared to notify the Administrator as soon as practicable before the test deadline
If you plan to use an alternative test method, confirm Method 301 validation status, assemble Method 301 results and justification, and plan to notify the Administrator ≥60 days before the test

Verify whether your State is delegated for notifications or whether to send notices to the appropriate EPA Regional Office (per §63.9(a)(4)), and identify the correct recipient and contact information

Plan for retention and submission logistics: retain performance test records for at least 5 years and prepare to submit the Notification of Compliance Status (including test results) before the close of business on the 60th calendar day after test completion

candidates.title: § 63.8 Monitoring requirements (General provisions)

criteria.criterion: If an owner or operator wishes to use an alternative monitoring procedure, then they must submit an application to the Administrator as described in 40 CFR 63.8(f)(4).

If the alternative monitoring procedure will serve as the performance test method to demonstrate compliance, then the application must be submitted at least 60 days before the performance evaluation is scheduled to begin as required by 40 CFR 63.8(f)(4)(i).

If an owner or operator submits a request to use an alternative monitoring method, then the application must include a description addressing the four elements in § 63.2 and a site‑specific performance evaluation test plan as specified in 40 CFR 63.8(f)(4)(ii) and 40 CFR 63.8(e)(3).

If the Administrator approves the use of an alternative monitoring method for an affected source, then the owner or operator shall continue to use that approved alternative until the Administrator approves the use of another monitoring method as allowed under 40 CFR 63.8(f)(5)(iii).

candidates.title: §§ 63.342–63.348 National Emission Standards for Chromium Electroplating and Anodizing (Subpart N)

criteria.criterion: If an owner or operator requests an alternative monitoring method under Subpart N, then requests and approvals shall be considered in accordance with 40 CFR 63.343(c)(8) and the procedures in 40 CFR 63.8(f)(1), (f)(3), (f)(4), and (f)(5).

If the proposed alternative constitutes a major alternative to monitoring as required in this subpart, then approval of that major alternative to monitoring is an authority retained by the U.S. EPA Administrator and cannot be delegated to State, local, or Tribal agencies under 40 CFR 63.348(c)(3).

If the owner or operator proposes to use an air pollution control device not listed in the Subpart N monitoring table, then they must submit a description of the device, Method 306 test results verifying performance, a copy of the operation and maintenance plan, and proposed operating parameters and monitoring plan for Administrator approval as required by 40 CFR 63.343(d) and 40 CFR 63.344(c).

If the alternative monitoring would replace or modify the continuous monitoring or site‑specific operating parameter monitoring required for the chosen control technique (e.g., pressure drop for mesh pads, velocity pressure for packed‑bed scrubbers, surface tension for wetting agents), then the continuous compliance monitoring requirements in 40 CFR 63.343(c) apply and the monitoring plan is subject to Administrator approval per this subpart.

checklist: Confirm each tank type (enclosed hard chromium electroplating) and whether tanks are new, existing, or reconstructed (affects which §63.342 limits apply).

Determine whether the facility is designated large or small (calculate maximum cumulative potential and/or actual cumulative rectifier capacity; maintain monthly ampere‑hour records per §63.342(c)(3)).

Identify the exact air pollution control device(s) to be used (Palm Technology Emission Eliminating Devices) and verify whether that device type is one of the control techniques specifically listed in Table 1 (CMP, packed‑bed scrubber, PBS/CMP, fiber‑bed) or would be an APCD not listed in the rule.

If the proposed device is not listed, assemble device documentation: device description, Method 306 (or approved alternate) performance test results, operation & maintenance plan (including the O&M elements required by §63.342(f)(3)), and proposed operating parameters and monitoring plan for submittal per §63.343(d).

Assess whether the standard monitoring methods/locations (e.g., pressure‑tap locations, Method 306 sampling at outlet, surface tension measurement Method 306B) are feasible or subject to interferences (e.g., liquid water, other effluent interferences) that would justify an alternative per §63.8(f)(2)(i) and §63.343(c)(8)(ii).

Decide whether the alternative monitoring procedure will be used as the performance test method; if so, plan to submit the alternative application at least 60 days before the performance evaluation per §63.8(f)(4)(i).
Prepare the application contents: description addressing the four monitoring elements in §63.2 and a site‑specific performance evaluation test plan that meets the requirements of §63.8(e)(3).

Determine whether the proposed change is a minor, intermediate, or major change to monitoring (so you know whether EPA approval must be sought and whether approval authority may be retained by the Administrator per §63.348(c)(3)).

Check whether your State/local agency has been delegated implementation/enforcement of Subpart N and confirm, with the EPA Regional Office, whether approval authority for the specific alternative (especially if major) will be handled by EPA or the delegated authority per §63.348(a).

If the alternative is approved, plan to continue using the approved alternative until EPA approves another monitoring method and be prepared to retain and submit records of any out‑of‑control periods, corrective actions, and performance evaluation results as required in §63.8(c) and §63.8(e).

candidates.title: Heat exchange system requirements

criteria.criterion: if the owner or operator monitors the cooling water for the presence of organic HAP or representative substances to detect leaks then samples shall be collected at the entrance and exit of each heat exchange system (or at the entrance and exit of each heat exchanger or group of heat exchangers) and a minimum of three sets of samples shall be taken at each entrance and exit and monitoring frequency shall be monthly for the first 6 months and quarterly thereafter

if an analytical method is used to determine the concentration of monitored substance(s) in cooling water then the method must be an EPA-approved method listed in part 136 that is sensitive to concentrations as low as 10 parts per million and the same method must be used for both entrance and exit samples, and alternative methods may be used only upon approval by the Administrator

if 99 percent by weight or more of the organic compounds that could leak into the heat exchange system are water soluble and have a Henry's Law Constant less than 5.0E-6 atm·m3/mol at 25 °C then owners and operators may monitor the cooling water under paragraph (b) in lieu of using the Modified El Paso Method

if the owner or operator uses the entrance/exit concentration comparison approach in paragraph (b) then a leak is detected only if the exit mean concentration is greater than the entrance mean using a one-sided statistical procedure at the 0.05 level and the amount by which it is greater is at least 1 ppm or 10 percent of the entrance mean, whichever is greater

candidates.title: Process vent, transfer operations, and control device monitoring and test methods

criteria.criterion: if vent or control-device performance sampling is conducted using Method 18, Method 25A, Method 320, or ASTM D6420-18 (when applicable) then the minimum sampling time for each run is 1 hour in which either an integrated sample or four grab samples must be taken and, if grab sampling is used, the grab samples must be taken at approximately equal intervals in time

if a method or data other than the specified Methods (e.g., Method 18 or 25A) is proposed for measuring vent stream concentration or control device performance then that method or data must be validated according to the protocol in Method 301 of appendix A of this part before it may be used in lieu of the specified methods

if an owner or operator seeks to monitor parameters other than those listed in §63.114(a) or (b) or otherwise seeks an alternate monitoring approach for a process vent or recovery device then the owner or operator must submit a request for approval according to the procedures specified in §63.151(f) or §63.152(e) of this subpart

if selecting a sampling site for determination of vent stream flow rate or concentration then the sampling site must be after the last recovery device (if any) but prior to the inlet of any control device and the sampling-site selection method must follow Method 1 or 1A of 40 CFR part 60, appendix A (no traverse needed for vents smaller than 0.10 m diameter)

checklist: Is the measurement target cooling water in a heat exchange system (Subpart F) or a process vent/control device/transfer operation (Subpart G)?

For Subpart F: Which monitoring approach will be used: paragraph (b) monitoring of cooling water, paragraph (c) surrogate monitoring, paragraph (g) Modified El Paso/total strippable hydrocarbon method, or paragraph (l) monitoring in lieu of Modified El Paso (i.e., do the Henry's Law and solubility criteria apply)?

For Subpart F: Confirm sample locations (entrance and exit as defined), number of sample sets (≥3 sets per entrance/exit), monitoring frequency (monthly for first 6 months then quarterly), and that entrance and exit samples are analyzed using the same analytical method

For Subpart F: Is the proposed composite sampling method an EPA part 136 method that is sensitive to 10 ppm (check part 136 listings) and appropriate for both entrance and exit samples, or is it an alternative method that requires Administrator approval under §63.104(b)(3)?

For Subpart F: If proposing an alternative analytical/sample collection technique, prepare to document and request Administrator approval (alternative methods) and to demonstrate equivalence to required sensitivity/accuracy

For Subpart G: Identify which EPA reference method will be used (Method 18, 25A, 320, ASTM D6420-18, Method 320, or another) and verify the method's sample type requirement (integrated vs grab) and minimum run time (1 hour) and number/timing of grabs (minimum four at approx equal intervals) per the cited method-specific provisions

For Subpart G: If proposing composite sampling in place of the required integrated or multiple-grab runs, determine whether the composite approach is validated under Method 301; if not, prepare a Method 301 validation or a formal approval request per §63.114(c) (and the request procedures referenced there)

For Subpart G (transfer/performace tests): confirm sampling-site selection (after last recovery device and before control device inlet) per Method 1/1A, and the required number of runs (usually three) and run durations, as applicable to the test or performance requirement

For either subpart: assemble documentation of proposed sampling procedure, analytical method detection limits, representative prior tests or engineering justification, and any Method 301 validation data or Administrator-approval requests to support a change from specified grab/integrated sampling

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants From Primary Aluminum Production

criteria.criterion: if the source is an existing pitch storage tank subject to Subpart LL, then the compliance date for the pitch storage tank POM limit is October 16, 2017

if an existing pitch storage tank was shut down at the time compliance would have otherwise been required and is subsequently restarted, then the owner or operator must conduct the required initial performance test by the 30th day following startup

if a pitch storage tank must demonstrate initial compliance, then the owner or operator must demonstrate initial compliance by preparing a design evaluation or by conducting a performance test and submitting the specified documentation

if a carbon adsorber is used as the pitch storage tank control device, then the design evaluation must include the carbon-specific parameters listed for carbon adsorbers (e.g., affinity, amount of carbon per bed, number of beds, feed humidity and temperature, flow rate, and desorption/regeneration details)

candidates.title: General Provisions (Compliance with standards and maintenance requirements)

criteria.criterion: if an owner or operator of an existing source is unable to comply with a relevant standard promulgated under this part pursuant to section 112(d) of the Act, then the owner or operator may request that the Administrator or an authorized State grant an extension allowing up to 1 additional year to comply when that period is necessary for installation of controls

if requesting such an extension under paragraph (i)(4), then the request must be submitted in writing no later than 120 days prior to the affected source's compliance date unless the need for the extension arose after that 120-day deadline due to circumstances beyond the owner's reasonable control, in which case the later-submitted request must state when the owner first learned of the problem

if an extension of compliance is requested and the source is required to obtain a title V permit, then the owner or operator must apply for such a permit or apply to have the source's title V permit revised to incorporate the conditions of the extension

candidates.title: Provisions for Extension of Compliance, Waivers and Alternatives (example subpart provisions)

criteria.criterion: if an owner or operator of an existing source is unable to comply with a relevant standard promulgated under this part pursuant to section 112(d) of the Act, then the owner or operator may request that the Administrator grant an extension allowing up to 1 additional year to comply for installation of controls

if requesting an extension under this subpart's procedures, then the request must be submitted in writing not later than 12 months before the affected source's compliance date (or 18 months if including emission points in an emissions average), unless the standard specifies alternative submittal dates

if requesting an extension under this subpart, then the request must include a description of the controls to be installed, a compliance schedule with milestone dates (including initiation and completion of on-site construction/installation and final compliance), and a description of interim emission control steps

checklist: Confirm that the affected emission point is a pitch storage tank subject to Subpart LL (primary aluminum production/paste production/pitch storage) and not excluded by any other subpart

Verify whether the source is an existing source (vs new/reconstructed) under Subpart LL and that the pitch tank POM standard compliance date to which you are comparing is October 16, 2017 (see 40 CFR 63.847(a)(2)(iii))

Document the tank shutdown and restart history (was the tank shut down as of the compliance date and what is the actual restart date); record the date the tank was first used to store pitch after restart
Determine the date by which an initial performance test is required after restart (30 days after first use for pitch storage tanks per 40 CFR 63.847(c)(3)(iv))

Decide whether you will demonstrate initial compliance via a design evaluation or a performance test and assemble the required documentation (design evaluation content or Method 315 performance test) per 40 CFR 63.847(g)(1)–(3)

If using a carbon adsorber, prepare the carbon-specific design evaluation showing affinity, amount of carbon per bed, number of beds, feed gas humidity and temperature, flow rate, and regeneration/desorption schedule or pressure as applicable (per 40 CFR 63.847(g)(2)(v))

Determine whether you are seeking an extension of the October 16, 2017 compliance date for installation of controls and whether the extension is being sought from EPA or from a State with an approved part 70/title V permit program or delegated authority

Check deadline requirements for filing an extension request: (a) under 40 CFR 63.6(i)(4)(i)(B) submit no later than 120 days before the compliance date (unless the need arose after that date and you can justify late submission per 63.6(i)(4)(i)(C)); and (b) under 40 CFR 63.1112(a)(4)(i)(B) submit no later than 12 months (or 18 months as applicable) before the compliance date — determine which subpart’s timing the permitting authority expects you to follow

Prepare the extension request package with the required contents: description of controls to be installed, detailed compliance schedule with milestone dates (award of contracts/orders, start of on-site construction/installation, completion dates, final compliance date), interim control measures, and, if late, a statement of when you first learned of the need for additional time (per 40 CFR 63.6(i)(4)(i)(A),(B),(C) and 40 CFR 63.1112(a)(6)(i))

If the source is required to have a title V permit, verify whether you must apply for or revise the title V permit to incorporate extension conditions and prepare to do so if an extension is requested (per 40 CFR 63.6(i)(4)(i)(A))

Assemble evidence of good-faith progress and planned interim controls (to support the extension request and any progress reports), and be prepared to submit progress reports if an extension is granted (per 40 CFR 63.6(i)(10) / 63.1112(a)(10)-(11) procedures referenced in the provided text)

Record the specific control performance target you must meet (e.g., pitch storage tank control system must reduce inlet POM by 95% per 40 CFR 63.844(d) / 63.843(d)) and the performance target your carbon adsorber is expected to achieve, and prepare monitoring/QA plans required for demonstrating compliance
